lessons.title: Reivindicaciones: patents, standards and the technical report
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

B2's lesson on relative clauses told the story of a forgotten inventor and gave you *la
patente, patentar, el prototipo, el inventor*. This lesson reads the documents themselves: a
patent's claims, an official standard, a test report. Then it does what the CEFR expects of a C2
user, explaining technical material from outside your own field to someone who isn't an expert,
and you'll write such an explanation as this module's graded task.

## Industrial property in Mexico

*La propiedad industrial* (industrial property) covers the rights over inventions, designs,
trademarks and trade secrets; copyright (C1's *los derechos de autor*) is a separate system. In
Mexico it is administered by the IMPI (Instituto Mexicano de la Propiedad Industrial) under the
Ley Federal de Protección a la Propiedad Industrial, in force since November 5, 2020. Its main
rights, as IMPI guidance and the law describe them (checked November 2026):

| Right | What it protects | How long |
|---|---|---|
| *la patente* | an invention that is new, involves an inventive step and has industrial application | 20 years from filing; a supplementary certificate can extend it only to make up for unreasonable delays in granting it |
| *el modelo de utilidad* | a smaller invention: an object, tool or device whose new form or arrangement makes it work better | 15 years from filing |
| *la marca registrada* | a registered trademark (®): a sign that identifies goods or services | 10 years from the grant, renewable |
| *el secreto industrial* | a trade secret: information kept confidential that gives a competitive edge | as long as it stays secret |

Rights must be kept up: a patent whose annual fees aren't paid can lapse, *caducar* (*la patente
caducó*; also used of documents and medicines that expire). Check the IMPI's site for current
fees and terms before relying on any of this.

**[[Prior art]]** (*el estado de la técnica*) is everything made public anywhere before the filing
date: patents, articles, products, talks. An invention is new only if it isn't in the prior art,
and it has *actividad inventiva* (an inventive step) only if it wouldn't be obvious to a skilled
person in the field. A patent holder (*el titular de la patente*, *la titular*) can grant others
*una licencia* (a license to use the invention) in exchange for *regalías* (royalties, usually
plural), and can sue for *infracción* (infringement) when someone else makes or sells it
without permission. *La explotación* of a patent is its commercial use: no sense of abuse here.

## How a patent is written

A patent application has a title, an abstract, a description (in Spain, *la memoria
descriptiva*), the claims and the drawings (*los planos* in everyday technical talk, also
blueprints; *el plano* is also a city map). The legal heart is the claims. A **[[patent claim]]**
(*una reivindicación*) defines exactly what is protected, and each claim is one long sentence:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  accTitle: The parts of an independent patent claim
  accDescr: Four boxes, one below the other. The preamble names the object, una válvula para grifería. The transition, que comprende, introduces the elements. The elements are listed: una carcasa, un obturador. The characterizing part, caracterizada porque, gives what is new.
  A["Preámbulo: Una válvula para grifería,"] --> B["Transición: que comprende"]
  B --> C["Elementos: una carcasa…, un obturador…,"]
  C --> D["Parte característica: caracterizada porque…"]
```

- *Comprende* means "comprises" (includes at least these parts), not "understands".
- *Caracterizado porque* (one word, *porque*) introduces what is new; it agrees with the object
  (*caracterizada*, for *la válvula*).
- A dependent claim narrows an earlier one: *La válvula de conformidad con la reivindicación 1,
  caracterizada porque…*
- Reference numbers in parentheses point to the drawing: *el resorte (18)*.
- *Dicho / dicha* (the aforesaid) repeats an element already named, so nothing is ambiguous.

## Standards and the technical report

A Mexican official standard, *una norma oficial* or NOM (*norma oficial mexicana*), is a
mandatory technical regulation under the Ley de Infraestructura de la Calidad (published July 1,
2020); voluntary standards are NMX. A NOM sets *especificaciones* (technical requirements) and
test methods; a product may need *la homologación* (certification or type approval) before it is
sold. *Homologar* means to certify as meeting a standard, and in Mexico also to harmonize: *Las
dos dependencias acordaron homologar criterios* (The two agencies agreed to harmonize criteria).

A test report uses:

- the passive and the impersonal: *Se midió el caudal a 200 kPa* (The flow was measured at 200
  kPa);
- noun chains: *ensayo de durabilidad del obturador* (plunger durability test);
- measurements with their tolerance: *6.0 L/min ± 0.2* (*la tolerancia* is the permitted
  variation). Mexico writes the decimal point, Spain the decimal comma (*6,0*); the RAE accepts
  both.
- the vocabulary of wear: *el desgaste* (wear and tear), *la durabilidad*, *el componente*, *la
  carcasa* (casing, housing). A process is drawn in *un diagrama de flujo* (flowchart).

## A patent application

![A patent-style line drawing of a valve in cross-section. A horizontal body, numbered 10, has an inlet on the left, 12, and an outlet on the right, 14. Inside, a plunger, 16, sits in the passage, pushed down by a coiled spring, 18, above it. On top of the spring is a toothed gear, 20, turned by a knob outside the body, 22. Arrows show water flowing from left to right. A legend below names the seven numbered parts, and a caption reads Figura 1 (solicitud ficticia).](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

> **Solicitud de patente (ficticia). Válvula ahorradora de agua para grifería doméstica**
>
> **Resumen.** La invención se refiere a una válvula ahorradora de agua que se instala entre la
> toma de agua y la llave de lavabos y fregaderos. La válvula comprende una carcasa (10) con una
> entrada (12) y una salida (14), un obturador (16) desplazable y un resorte (18) que lo mantiene
> en posición de cierre parcial. Un engranaje (20), accionado por una perilla de ajuste (22),
> modifica la tensión del resorte y, con ello, el caudal máximo. Según los ensayos descritos, el
> dispositivo limita el caudal a 6.0 L/min ± 0.2 sin reducir de manera perceptible la fuerza del
> chorro.
>
> **Estado de la técnica.** En el estado de la técnica se conocen reductores de caudal de disco
> perforado, que se instalan en la boca de la llave. Dichos reductores presentan dos
> inconvenientes: el caudal no puede ajustarse una vez instalados, y los orificios se obstruyen
> con el sarro del agua, lo que acelera su desgaste.
>
> **Descripción breve.** La presente invención resuelve dichos inconvenientes mediante un
> obturador cuya apertura máxima puede regularse sin desmontar la válvula. Ninguno de los
> documentos citados describe la combinación de un obturador de resorte con un engranaje de
> ajuste. Los componentes internos son de latón y de un polímero de alta durabilidad; en el
> ensayo de desgaste, la válvula completó doscientos mil ciclos de apertura y cierre sin fugas.
>
> **Reivindicaciones**
>
> 1. Una válvula ahorradora de agua para grifería doméstica, que comprende una carcasa (10)
> provista de una entrada (12) y una salida (14), y un obturador (16) dispuesto entre ambas,
> caracterizada porque comprende además un resorte (18) que empuja dicho obturador (16) hacia
> una posición de cierre parcial y un engranaje (20) que modifica la tensión de dicho resorte
> (18).
> 2. La válvula de conformidad con la reivindicación 1, caracterizada porque el engranaje (20)
> se acciona mediante una perilla de ajuste (22) situada en el exterior de la carcasa (10).
> 3. La válvula de conformidad con la reivindicación 1 o 2, caracterizada porque el caudal
> máximo es de 6.0 L/min, con una tolerancia de ± 0.2 L/min, a una presión de entrada de 200 kPa.
> 4. La válvula de conformidad con cualquiera de las reivindicaciones anteriores, caracterizada
> porque la carcasa (10) es de latón.

**Summary in English.** The abstract presents a water-saving valve fitted between the water
supply and the faucet: a casing with inlet and outlet, a sliding plunger held partly closed by a
spring, and a knob-driven gear that changes the spring's tension and so the maximum flow, said to
be 6.0 L/min ± 0.2 without a noticeably weaker stream. Existing perforated-disc reducers can't be
adjusted and clog with scale. The invention adjusts without dismantling; no cited document
combines a spring plunger with an adjusting gear; it survived 200,000 cycles without leaking.
Claim 1 protects the combination; claims 2–4 add the external knob, the flow figure and a brass
casing.

**Glosses.** *La toma de agua* = water supply connection; *la llave* = faucet (Mexico; lesson 18
compares *el grifo*); *el obturador* = plunger, shut-off piece; *el resorte* = spring; *la
perilla* = knob; *el caudal* = flow rate; *el sarro* = limescale; *el latón* = brass.

## Explaining it to a lay reader

Mediation for a non-expert reader follows a few rules:

| Do | Why |
|---|---|
| start from the problem the reader knows | *Hoy los reductores se tapan…* gives a reason to read on |
| replace terms or define them once | *obturador* → *una pieza móvil que deja pasar más o menos agua* |
| explain how, step by step, in active verbs | *el resorte empuja la pieza* |
| keep the source's figures and their source | *según las pruebas del inventor* |
| keep the limits | an application is not yet a granted patent |
| add no facts or praise of your own | the reader must be able to trust the summary |

> **Una válvula para gastar menos agua en casa**
>
> Una solicitud de patente describe una pieza pequeña que se instala debajo del lavabo o del
> fregadero, entre la tubería y la llave, para que salga menos agua sin que el chorro se sienta
> débil.
>
> Ya existen reductores de este tipo: son discos con agujeros que se colocan en la boca de la
> llave. Tienen dos problemas: no se pueden ajustar y, con el tiempo, los agujeros se tapan con el
> sarro del agua.
>
> La nueva válvula funciona de otra manera. Por dentro tiene una pieza móvil que deja pasar más o
> menos agua, y un resorte que la empuja para cerrar el paso en parte. Con una perilla que queda
> por fuera, conectada a un engranaje (unas ruedas dentadas), se puede apretar o aflojar el
> resorte y así decidir cuánta agua sale como máximo, sin desarmar nada.
>
> Según las pruebas que presenta el propio solicitante, la válvula deja pasar como máximo unos
> seis litros por minuto y resistió doscientas mil aperturas y cierres sin gotear.
>
> Conviene tener en cuenta dos cosas. Estas cifras vienen de la solicitud: todavía no las ha
> comprobado nadie más. Y una solicitud no es aún una patente: en México, el IMPI debe revisar si
> la idea es de verdad nueva antes de concederla.

**Summary in English.** A patent application describes a small part fitted under the sink,
between the pipe and the faucet, so less water comes out without a weak stream. Existing
perforated-disc reducers can't be adjusted and clog with scale. The new valve has a moving piece
pushed partly shut by a spring; an outside knob turns a gear to tighten or loosen the spring and
set the maximum flow, without taking anything apart. The applicant's own tests give at most about six
liters a minute and 200,000 cycles without dripping. Two cautions: the figures come from the
application, and the IMPI must still examine it.

The explanation keeps the problem, the mechanism, the figures with their source and the limits,
and drops the reference numbers, *dicho* and the claim structure. *Unos seis litros* rounds *6.0
± 0.2*, which is fair for this reader; in a technical summary you would keep the tolerance.

**Checklist for your own explanation**

- Does the first paragraph say what the thing is and why a reader should care?
- Is every term replaced or defined once?
- Is every figure the source's, with its source named?
- Are the source's hedges and limits still there, and nothing added?
- Is the register right for the publication and its reader, from start to finish?

Now write your own: the task gives you a different technical text and a reader.

```assignment
writing: es6-m4-w16-divulgacion
```

## Pronunciation

- *reivindicación*: *rei-vin-di-ka-SIÓN*, five syllables (*rei* is one).
- *engranaje*: *en-gra-NA-he*; *homologación*: *o-mo-lo-ga-SIÓN* (silent *h*).

## Common mistakes

- ***Comprende* = comprises**, and *caracterizado porque* is one fixed phrase.
- **False friends**: *el plano* is a drawing or a map, not an airplane; *la explotación* of a
  patent is commercial use.
- **Overstating**: an application isn't a patent, and the applicant's tests aren't independent
  proof.
- **Adding to the source**: "the best valve on the market" is your opinion, not the patent's.

## Key points

- A patent protects an invention that is new against the prior art, involves an inventive step
  and has industrial application; in Mexico, for 20 years from filing.
- Each claim is one sentence: preamble, *que comprende*, the elements, *caracterizado porque*.
- NOMs are mandatory standards; reports use the passive, noun chains and tolerances.
- A lay explanation keeps the problem, the mechanism, the figures with their source and the
  limits, and adds nothing.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Honors: Lea el instructivo: the language of medicine leaflets
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Lesson 14 followed a diagnosis from the doctor's note to a letter for the patient. The
**[[package insert]]** is the next document in that chain: the leaflet folded inside a medicine's box, which
the patient reads alone, often at night, often worried. It has to be exact enough for the
regulator and clear enough for anyone. That double audience gives it a language of its own:
fixed sections, a scale of warnings, and a set of imperative and impersonal forms you'll meet on
every box.

Everything here is about how leaflets are written. The medicine in this lesson is invented, and
its doses are fictional. For any real medicine, follow your doctor or pharmacist and the leaflet
in its own box.

## The leaflet in Mexico and Spain

In Mexico the leaflet is *el instructivo*; regulatory texts also call it *el inserto*. In
Spain it is *el prospecto*: you'll hear *lee el prospecto* there where a Mexican says *lee el
instructivo*. Mexico's medicine regulator is COFEPRIS (the Comisión Federal para la Protección
contra Riesgos Sanitarios), and the labeling standard for medicines, NOM-072-SSA1-2012, was
published in the *Diario Oficial* on November 21, 2012. A secondary site's summary of the standard
(read November 2026) lists the leaflet's contents roughly as follows; check the official text
before relying on the details. Doctors get a separate, technical document, the prescribing
information (in Mexico usually *la información para prescribir*).

| Section | What it says |
|---|---|
| *denominación genérica y distintiva* | the medicine's generic name and, if it has one, its brand name |
| *forma farmacéutica y formulación* | tablet, capsule, syrup…; the active ingredient and the inactive ones |
| *indicaciones* | what it is for |
| *contraindicaciones y precauciones* | who mustn't take it; care in pregnancy, breastfeeding, driving |
| *reacciones adversas* | side effects, by frequency |
| *interacciones* | with food, drink and other medicines |
| *dosis y vía de administración* | how much, how often, and how it enters the body |
| *sobredosis o ingesta accidental* | what to do if too much is taken |
| *leyendas* | fixed warnings, such as *No se deje al alcance de los niños* |

The key terms:

- *El principio activo* is the active ingredient, the substance that acts; *el excipiente* is an
  inactive ingredient (binder, sweetener, coating) that still matters for allergies and
  intolerances.
- *La posología* is the dosage regimen: how much, how often, for how long. B2's *la dosis* is one
  amount; the *posología* is the whole plan.
- *La contraindicación* is a reason not to use the medicine at all, stronger than a precaution.
- *La vía de administración* is the route: *oral, intravenosa, tópica* (on the skin).
- *El comprimido* is the technical word for a tablet, standard in Spain's leaflets and found on
  Mexican boxes too, though Mexican boxes more often say *la tableta*; in everyday speech A1's
  *la pastilla* is the usual word everywhere.
- *El genérico* is a generic medicine, sold under its generic name once the original patent has
  expired; as an adjective, *un medicamento genérico*.
- *La sobredosis* (plural *las sobredosis*) is an overdose.
- *La farmacovigilancia* is the monitoring of medicines after they reach the market: leaflets
  ask patients to report suspected side effects to it.

![A package insert for the invented medicine, laid out as a tall folded sheet. A dark title band reads ALVORASTINA, comprimidos 7 mg, instructivo para el paciente (ficticio). Below it, eight boxes in two columns, each with its heading and a sample line. Left column: Fórmula (each tablet contains 7 mg of alvorastina), Indicaciones (relieves allergic rhinitis symptoms), Contraindicaciones (don't take it if you are allergic), Precauciones (may cause drowsiness: don't drive). Right column: Reacciones adversas (common: headache, dry mouth), Interacciones (sedatives increase drowsiness), Posología (one tablet a day, with or without food), Sobredosis (if you take too much, go to the emergency room). The boxes are not numbered, because their order varies from leaflet to leaflet. A shaded band at the bottom, with a warning triangle, holds the Leyendas: keep out of children's reach; report adverse reactions.](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

## The language of instructions and warnings

Leaflets speak to the reader in three ways, often on the same page:

| Form | Example | Where |
|---|---|---|
| *usted* imperative | *Tome un comprimido al día. No lo mastique.* | Mexican and Spanish leaflets for patients |
| impersonal *se* + subjunctive | *Consérvese a temperatura ambiente. No se deje al alcance de los niños.* | fixed legends, labels and boxes, very common in Mexico |
| infinitive | *No usar después de la fecha de caducidad.* | short labels, especially in Spain |

The *se* + subjunctive forms (*consérvese, agítese, no se use*) are old-fashioned in speech but
alive on every Mexican box: read them as "should be kept", "shake", "do not use".

Warnings come in grades, and the grade is information:

| Strength | Phrase |
|---|---|
| absolute | *No tome este medicamento si…*; *No se administre a…* |
| strong | *Evite…*; *No maneje ni opere maquinaria…* |
| check first | *Consulte a su médico antes de…* |
| emergency | *Suspenda el tratamiento y busque atención médica de inmediato si…* |

Side effects are listed by frequency. Leaflets in the European Union, Spain's included, use the fixed
bands of the EU's leaflet template: *muy frecuentes* (more than 1 in 10 people), *frecuentes* (up to 1 in 10), *poco
frecuentes* (up to 1 in 100), *raras* (up to 1 in 1,000), *muy raras* (up to 1 in 10,000). A
reader who knows the bands won't panic at a long list of *raras*.

## An invented leaflet

> **INSTRUCTIVO PARA EL PACIENTE. Ficticio: este medicamento no existe.**
>
> **Alvorastina, comprimidos de 7 mg.** Medicamento genérico. Vía de administración: oral.
>
> Lea todo este instructivo antes de empezar a tomar el medicamento y consérvelo: puede
> necesitar leerlo de nuevo. Si tiene alguna duda, consulte a su médico o farmacéutico.
>
> **1. Qué es y para qué se usa.** La alvorastina es un antihistamínico. Está indicada para
> aliviar los síntomas de la rinitis alérgica estacional (estornudos, comezón de nariz,
> escurrimiento nasal y ojos llorosos) en adultos y adolescentes a partir de 12 años.
>
> **2. Fórmula.** Cada comprimido contiene 7 mg de alvorastina (principio activo). Excipientes:
> lactosa, celulosa y estearato de magnesio.
>
> **3. Contraindicaciones.** No tome este medicamento si es alérgico a la alvorastina o a
> cualquiera de los excipientes, ni si padece insuficiencia renal grave. No se administre a
> menores de 12 años.
>
> **4. Precauciones.** *Embarazo y lactancia:* si está embarazada, cree que podría estarlo o está
> amamantando, consulte a su médico antes de tomar este medicamento. *Conducción:* puede causar
> somnolencia; no maneje ni opere maquinaria hasta saber cómo le afecta. Evite las bebidas
> alcohólicas durante el tratamiento. Este medicamento contiene lactosa: si su médico le ha
> dicho que tiene intolerancia a algunos azúcares, consúltelo antes de tomarlo.
>
> **5. Interacciones.** Informe a su médico si toma otros medicamentos, en especial
> tranquilizantes o medicamentos para dormir, ya que pueden aumentar la somnolencia.
>
> **6. Posología (dosis ficticias).** Adultos y adolescentes a partir de 12 años: un comprimido
> al día, con o sin alimentos. Trague el comprimido entero con un vaso de agua; no lo mastique.
> Si olvida una dosis, tómela en cuanto se acuerde, salvo que falte poco para la siguiente; en
> ese caso, sáltese la dosis olvidada. No tome una dosis doble para compensarla.
>
> **7. Sobredosis o ingesta accidental.** Si toma más de lo indicado, o si un niño ingiere el
> medicamento por accidente, acuda de inmediato al servicio de urgencias más cercano y lleve
> consigo este instructivo.
>
> **8. Reacciones adversas.** Como todos los medicamentos, este puede producir reacciones
> adversas, aunque no todas las personas las presentan. Frecuentes: somnolencia, dolor de cabeza,
> boca seca. Poco frecuentes: mareo, cansancio. Suspenda el tratamiento y busque atención médica
> de inmediato si presenta hinchazón de la cara o de la garganta, o dificultad para respirar.
>
> **9. Conservación.** Consérvese a no más de 30 °C, en su empaque original. No se use después de
> la fecha de caducidad.
>
> No se deje al alcance de los niños. Reporte las sospechas de reacciones adversas al sistema de
> farmacovigilancia.

**Summary in English.** An invented leaflet for a fictional antihistamine tablet. It treats
seasonal allergy symptoms in people aged 12 and up. Each tablet has 7 mg of the active ingredient
plus lactose and two other excipients. It must not be taken by people allergic to any ingredient,
with severe kidney failure, or under 12. In pregnancy or breastfeeding, ask a doctor first; it
can cause drowsiness, so no driving until you know how it affects you; avoid alcohol; lactose
intolerance needs a doctor's advice. Sedatives add to the drowsiness. One tablet a day (fictional
dose), swallowed whole; a forgotten dose is taken late unless the next is near, and never
doubled. Overdose means the emergency room, with the leaflet. Common side effects: drowsiness,
headache, dry mouth; swelling of the face or throat or trouble breathing means stop and get help
at once. Store below 30 °C; keep away from children; report side effects.

**Glosses.** *El estornudo* = sneeze; *la comezón* = itching; *el escurrimiento nasal* = runny
nose (Mexico); *la insuficiencia renal* = kidney failure; *amamantar* = to breastfeed; *la
somnolencia* = drowsiness; *el tranquilizante* = sedative; *tragar* = to swallow; *masticar* = to
chew; *saltarse* = to skip; *las urgencias* = the emergency room; *el mareo* = dizziness; *la
hinchazón* = swelling; *el empaque* = packaging (Mexico).

## Worked examples

### Example 1: three questions from a patient

A neighbor shows you the leaflet and asks three things. The method: find the section first,
then read the exact wording, and answer with its strength, no stronger and no weaker.

1. *¿Lo puedo tomar si estoy dando pecho?* (Can I take it while breastfeeding?) Section 4:
   *consulte a su médico antes de tomar este medicamento*. The leaflet neither forbids it nor
   allows it: it sends her to her doctor. Saying "no, it's forbidden" would turn a *check first*
   into an *absolute*, the grade of section 3.
2. *Se me olvidó la de ayer. ¿Me tomo dos hoy?* (I forgot yesterday's. Do I take two today?)
   Section 6: *No tome una dosis doble para compensarla.* The answer is no, and the leaflet says
   what to do instead.
3. *¿Me puedo tomar una cerveza?* (Can I have a beer?) Section 4: *Evite las bebidas
   alcohólicas.* A strong recommendation, not an absolute ban, but the reason (drowsiness) is in
   the same section, and the honest answer repeats both.

In each case you relay the leaflet, not your own opinion: you are a mediator, not a pharmacist.

### Example 2: section 6 for an older reader

An older relative finds section 6 dense. The rewrite follows lesson 14's rules: one instruction
per line, concrete times, the reason where it helps, nothing added and nothing lost.

> **Cómo tomarlo**
>
> - Tome **un** comprimido al día. Puede ser con comida o sin comida.
> - Tráguelo entero, con un vaso de agua. No lo muerda.
> - ¿Se le olvidó? Tómelo en cuanto se acuerde.
> - Pero si ya casi es hora del siguiente, no tome el olvidado: espere al siguiente.
> - Nunca tome dos juntos.

How to take it: Take one tablet a day, with or without food. Swallow it whole with a glass of
water; don't bite it. Forgot it? Take it as soon as you remember. But if it's almost time for the
next one, don't take the forgotten one: wait for the next. Never take two together.

Compare the changes: *a partir de 12 años* is gone because the reader is an adult; *salvo que
falte poco para la siguiente* became a separate line beginning with *pero*; *no lo mastique*
became *no lo muerda*, a word every reader knows; the bold *un* carries the most important fact.
Nothing new was added: *con o sin alimentos* became *con comida o sin comida*, and no rule
about mealtimes crept in.

## Pronunciation

- *posología*: five syllables, *po-so-lo-HÍ-a*.
- *excipiente*: *ek-si-PIEN-te* (in careful speech *eks-si-PIEN-te*).
- *farmacovigilancia*: *far-ma-ko-vi-hi-LAN-sia*.

## Common mistakes

- **Downgrading or upgrading a warning**: *consulte a su médico* is not "it's forbidden", and
  *no tome* is not "better not".
- ***La dosis* for *la posología***: the dose is one amount; the dosage includes frequency and
  duration.
- **Contraindicated ≠ not indicated**: *no está indicado* means it isn't meant for that use;
  *está contraindicado* means it could harm.
- **Reading *consérvese* as a past tense**: it's an instruction ("keep it").
- **Spain's word in a Mexican text**: *el prospecto* is understood, but a Mexican pharmacy says
  *el instructivo*.

## Key points

- *El instructivo* (Spain *el prospecto*) has fixed sections: formula, indications,
  contraindications, precautions, adverse reactions, interactions, dosage and route, overdose,
  legends.
- Instructions use the *usted* imperative, the impersonal *se* + subjunctive (*consérvese*) and,
  in Spain, the infinitive.
- Warnings have grades, and frequency bands put side effects in proportion.
- When you relay a leaflet, keep each warning at its own strength and add nothing.

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you complete
the lesson.

lessons.title: Honors: Ante la fe del notario: deeds and wills
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Lesson 13 read a ruling, the text in which a court settles a conflict. Notarial documents work the
other way round: they are written so that conflicts don't happen. When a house changes hands, a
company is founded or a parent makes a will, a notary records it in a form that the law treats as
proof. This lesson reads two such documents, a **[[public deed]]** and a will, and practices
explaining them to the people they affect. It builds on B2's *el notario* and on the legal
formulas of lesson 13, and adds a layer of old-fashioned formulas you only need to recognize.

As in lesson 13, the documents are invented and nothing here is legal advice.

## Two kinds of notary

Mexico belongs to the Latin notariate, shared with Spain, most of Latin America and much of
continental Europe. A Mexican *notario público* is a lawyer with a law degree who has passed a
demanding exam and been appointed by the state government; each state has its own notarial law.
The notary holds *la fe pública*, the power delegated by the State to certify that an act took
place as recorded, so a notarized document is proof in court unless someone proves it false. The
notary also checks the parties' identity and capacity, explains the act's legal effects and keeps
the original in *el protocolo*, the bound record of everything he or she has authorized. To
*protocolizar* a document is to enter it in that record (*protocolizar un acta de asamblea*, to
notarize a shareholders' meeting's minutes).

A US notary public is a different job: someone authorized to witness signatures and take oaths,
who in general doesn't need legal training and may not give legal advice unless also a lawyer.
Because the same word names two very different professions, consumer advocates in the US warn
Spanish speakers that a *notario* sign there doesn't mean a lawyer. When you translate, *notario
público* (Mexico) is best rendered "notary (a lawyer and public official)" the first time, not
just "notary public".

## The structure of a public deed

*La escritura pública* (public deed) is the document a notary drafts and authorizes in the
protocol. The parts vary with each state's law, but most deeds follow this order:

![A layout of a public deed, top to bottom. A heading gives the deed and volume numbers. Then six blocks: Proemio, with place, date and the notary; Comparecencia, naming who appears; Antecedentes, in Roman numerals; Cláusulas, in ordinal words, PRIMERA, SEGUNDA, TERCERA; Generales y certificaciones, beginning YO, LA NOTARIA, DOY FE; and Firmas y autorización, with signature lines and a round seal.](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

| Part | What it does |
|---|---|
| *proemio* | deed number, volume, place and date, the notary's name and notarial office |
| *comparecencia* | who appears: *el compareciente* (*la compareciente*), any person present before the notary |
| *antecedentes* | the background: earlier deeds, registry entries, permits |
| *cláusulas* | what the parties agree, each clause numbered in words (*PRIMERA, SEGUNDA…*) |
| *generales y certificaciones* | the parties' personal details, and what the notary certifies |
| *autorización* | signatures, the notary's signature and seal |

*El otorgante* (*la otorgante*) is the party who grants the act, who gives consent and signs: in
a sale, both buyer and seller; in a will, the testator alone. Normally every *otorgante* is also a
*compareciente*, but not every *compareciente* is an *otorgante*: a witness or an interpreter
appears without granting anything.

### The old formulas

Deeds keep formulas that sound centuries old, because they are. Recognize them; never use them
outside a notarial text.

| Formula | Meaning |
|---|---|
| *ante mí* | before me (the notary speaking) |
| *comparecen* | (the following persons) appear |
| *doy fe* | I attest, I certify |
| *bajo protesta de decir verdad* | under a formal promise to tell the truth (Mexican legal formula) |
| *lo que hago constar* | which I record |
| *a quien conozco* / *quien se identifica con* | whom I know personally / who identifies himself or herself with |
| *el día de su fecha* | on the date given above |

Deeds also write numbers in words (*dos mil veintiséis*) so that no one can change a figure, and
capitalize key names and defined terms (*"LA DONATARIA"*), the notarial cousin of lesson 13's *en
lo sucesivo*.

## A deed: a gift with a life interest

> **ESCRITURA NÚMERO DIECIOCHO MIL CUATROCIENTOS CINCUENTA Y DOS (ficticia)**
>
> En la ciudad de Querétaro, a los catorce días del mes de octubre de dos mil veintiséis, ANTE
> MÍ, licenciada Elena Sáenz Robles, titular de la Notaría Pública número Cuarenta y Uno,
> COMPARECEN: por una parte, los señores Joaquín Medina Torres y Rosa María Linares Ruiz, en lo
> sucesivo "LOS DONANTES"; y por la otra, la señora Valeria Medina Linares, en lo sucesivo "LA
> DONATARIA", con el objeto de formalizar un contrato de donación con reserva de usufructo, al
> tenor de los siguientes antecedentes y cláusulas:
>
> **ANTECEDENTES**
>
> I. Los donantes son propietarios de la casa ubicada en la calle Hidalgo número veintitrés,
> colonia Centro, según consta en la escritura número nueve mil ochenta, inscrita en el Registro
> Público de la Propiedad.
>
> II. Declaran los donantes, bajo protesta de decir verdad, que el inmueble se encuentra libre de
> todo gravamen.
>
> **CLÁUSULAS**
>
> PRIMERA. Los donantes donan a la donataria, quien acepta, la nuda propiedad del inmueble
> descrito en el antecedente primero.
>
> SEGUNDA. Los donantes se reservan el usufructo vitalicio del inmueble. En consecuencia, podrán
> habitarlo, arrendarlo y percibir sus frutos mientras vivan. Al fallecer el último de ellos, el
> usufructo se extinguirá y la donataria adquirirá la plena propiedad.
>
> TERCERA. Los gastos, impuestos y derechos que se causen con motivo de esta escritura serán por
> cuenta de la donataria.
>
> **GENERALES Y CERTIFICACIONES**
>
> YO, LA NOTARIA, DOY FE: de que conozco a los comparecientes, quienes a mi juicio tienen
> capacidad legal para este acto; de que les leí la presente escritura y les expliqué su valor y
> sus consecuencias legales; y de que, conformes con ella, la firman ante mí el día de su fecha.
>
> Firmas de los otorgantes. Firma y sello de la notaria.

**Summary in English.** Deed 18,452 (fictional), Querétaro, October 14, 2026. Before the notary
appear a couple, the donors, and their daughter, the donee, to formalize a gift with a reserved
life interest. Background: the parents own a house, recorded in an earlier registered deed, and
state that it carries no charges. Clauses: they give their daughter the bare ownership; they keep
the usufruct for life (they may live in it, rent it and keep the income), and when the second of
them dies it ends and she becomes full owner; she pays the costs and taxes. The notary certifies
that she knows them, that they have legal capacity, and that she read and explained the deed
before they signed.

**Glosses.** *Al tenor de* = in accordance with (lesson 08's *a tenor de* is the general form);
*el gravamen* = a charge on property, such as a mortgage or lien; *la nuda propiedad* = bare
ownership, without the right to use; *el usufructo* = the right to use a property and enjoy its
income while someone else owns it; *vitalicio* = for life; *arrendar* = to lease; *percibir sus
frutos* = to receive its income (rent, crops); *por cuenta de* = paid by.

## Wills, powers and intestacy

The commonest notarial will in Mexico is *el testamento público abierto*: *el testador* (*la
testadora*) states his or her wishes before the notary, who writes them down. The vocabulary:

- *el heredero* (*la heredera*) inherits all or a share of the estate (B1's *heredar*); *el
  legatario* (*la legataria*) receives a specific item, *un legado*;
- *el albacea* (same form for both genders: *el albacea, la albacea*) is the executor, who
  carries out the will and manages the estate until it is divided;
- *intestado* (adjective and noun) describes a person who dies without a valid will (*murió
  intestado*), and *el intestado* is the estate itself; the law then decides who inherits, in a
  slower process, *la sucesión intestamentaria*. In recent years notaries and governments have
  run a campaign each September, "Septiembre, mes del testamento", with reduced fees (check
  current conditions).

*El poder notarial* is a power of attorney granted before a notary. Mexican civil codes describe
three broad kinds, often combined: *para pleitos y cobranzas* (to sue and collect), *para actos
de administración* (to manage property) and *para actos de dominio* (to sell or encumber it, the
widest).

## Worked examples

### Example 1: reading the deed's clauses

Ask three questions of any clause: who acts, on what, and under what condition.

| Clause | Who | What | Condition |
|---|---|---|---|
| PRIMERA | the parents give; Valeria accepts | the bare ownership of the house | none: it takes effect now |
| SEGUNDA | the parents keep | the life interest (live there, rent, income) | it ends when the second parent dies |
| TERCERA | Valeria pays | the costs, taxes and fees of the deed | none |

So, if a neighbor asks *¿Ya es de Valeria la casa?*, the accurate answer is: *Sí y no. Ya es
dueña, pero sus papás pueden vivir ahí, rentarla y quedarse con la renta mientras vivan.* (Yes
and no. She already owns it, but her parents can live there, rent it and keep the rent for as
long as they live.)

### Example 2: explaining a will to an heir

Joaquín's will, also invented:

> PRIMERA. El testador instituye como únicos y universales herederos a sus hijos Valeria y Andrés
> Medina Linares, por partes iguales.
>
> SEGUNDA. Lega a su nieta, Sofía Medina Paredes, el piano que se encuentra en su domicilio.
>
> TERCERA. Nombra albacea a su hija Valeria y, en caso de que esta no pueda o no quiera
> desempeñar el cargo, a su hijo Andrés.

First: The testator names his children Valeria and Andrés as sole heirs to his whole estate, in
equal shares. Second: He leaves his granddaughter Sofía the piano in his home. Third: He names his
daughter Valeria executor and, if she can't or won't serve, his son Andrés.

Andrés asks what it means for him. A good explanation follows the will clause by clause, uses
his words and *tú*, and flags what the documents don't settle:

> *El testamento dice tres cosas. Tú y Valeria heredan todo, mitad y mitad. El piano no entra en
> esa mitad: es para Sofía. Y Valeria es la albacea: ella hace los trámites y reparte; si ella no
> puede, te toca a ti. Ojo: la casa de Hidalgo ya es de Valeria por la donación, aunque tus papás
> sigan viviendo ahí. Cómo cuenta eso en el reparto es una pregunta para el notario, no para mí.*

The will says three things. You and Valeria inherit everything, half each. The piano isn't part
of that half: it's for Sofía. And Valeria is the executor: she handles the paperwork and divides
things up; if she can't, it falls to you. Careful: the house on Hidalgo already belongs to
Valeria through the gift, even though your parents still live there. How that counts in the
division is a question for the notary, not for me.

The last sentence is the mediator's limit: the explanation relays both documents accurately and
points to the question they raise, without answering a legal question.

## Pronunciation

- *usufructo*: *u-su-FRUK-to*; *testador*: *tes-ta-DOR*.
- *albacea*: four syllables, *al-ba-SE-a*; *compareciente*: *kom-pa-re-SIEN-te*.

## Common mistakes

- **"Notary public" for *notario público*** in a translation for US readers, without saying he
  or she is a lawyer.
- ***El heredero* for every beneficiary**: someone who receives one item is *un legatario*.
- **Changing the ending for gender**: *el albacea* and *la albacea* share one form (never *el albaceo*).
- **Using deed formulas in ordinary writing**: *ante mí, doy fe, el día de su fecha* belong in the
  protocol.
- **Answering legal questions while mediating**: relay the document; send legal questions to a
  professional.

## Key points

- A Mexican *notario público* is a lawyer and a public official who holds *la fe pública*; a US
  notary public is not.
- A public deed runs: *proemio, comparecencia, antecedentes, cláusulas, generales y
  certificaciones, autorización*.
- In wills, *herederos* inherit shares, *legatarios* specific items, and *el albacea* carries
  it all out; dying *intestado* leaves the division to the law.
- Recognize the old formulas (*ante mí, doy fe, bajo protesta de decir verdad*); explain deeds in
  plain words, clause by clause.

lessons.title: Doblado en México: dubbing, neutral Spanish and the pluricentric norm
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

C1 03 asked who decides what is correct. This module asks whose Spanish is the standard. At C2
the answer is "several countries'": you'll read texts from Spain and
the Americas and write for readers in twenty countries at once. This lesson sets out the idea
behind the module, the **[[pluricentric norm]]**, looks at a trade that lives by it, dubbing, and
ends with a task you'll hand in: adapting a Mexican text for readers everywhere.

## One language, several centers

Spanish is *pluricéntrico* (pluricentric): it has several centers of prestige, and each sets
the model for its own country. A news anchor in Mexico City, one in Bogotá and one in Madrid
each speak a **[[standard variety]]** (*la variedad estándar*), the form a country's educated
speakers use in formal speech and writing. Its model is *la norma culta* (the educated norm),
and Mexico's is as correct as Spain's.

The Asociación de Academias de la Lengua Española (ASALE), created at a congress in Mexico in
1951, now has 23 academies: Spain's, nineteen in the Americas (Puerto Rico's included), and those
of the United States, the Philippines and Equatorial Guinea (which joined in 2016). Together they write *panhispánico*
(pan-Hispanic) works that describe each country's usage instead of ranking it: the *Diccionario
de la lengua española* (DLE), the *Nueva gramática* and the *Diccionario panhispánico de dudas*
(DPD), whose second edition was presented in 2024.

*La estandarización* (standardization) left Spanish with one spelling for the whole language
and several educated norms of words and grammar. So *el estándar* (the standard; plural *los
estándares*) is one spelling and many norms. B1's *la norma* stays the word for a single rule.

## Regionalisms, localisms and country marks

A **[[regionalism]]** (*el regionalismo*) is a word or use typical of one region; *el localismo* is
narrower, a word of one city or area. Spanish names them by place:

| Term | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| *el mexicanismo* | a word or use typical of Mexico | *ahorita* (an A1 honors word), B1's *la chamba* (job) |
| *el americanismo* | a word or use of Latin America (all or much of it) | A1's *el celular* (Spain *el móvil*) |
| *el peninsularismo* | a word or use of Spain | *el ordenador* (Mexico *la computadora*) |
| *el hispanismo* | a Spanish loanword in another language | English *patio, plaza, canyon* |

The DLE marks a sense used only in some countries with a *marca de país* (country label): *Méx.*,
*Esp.* (Spain), *Am.* (the Americas), *Ant.* (the Antilles), *Arg.*, *Chile* and so on. Lesson
18's *currar* (to work) is marked "*coloq. Esp.*" (colloquial, Spain) in the online DLE (checked
November 17, 2026). For a writer the marks are warnings, not rules. A marked sense may puzzle
readers elsewhere, so replace it or explain it. But an unmarked word isn't guaranteed to be
general: the DLE gives lesson 18's *molar* (to be cool) no country mark, although it is heard
mainly in Spain.

## Isoglosses

An **[[isogloss]]** (*la isoglosa*) is a line on a dialect map where one feature ends and another
begins. The line for *carro / coche / auto* and the line for *computadora / ordenador /
computador* make two different maps. Isoglosses rarely coincide and rarely follow borders, which
is why "Latin American Spanish" is a useful label for some words and misleading for others.

![A schematic, not a map. Three boxes stand for three areas. Spain: coche, ordenador, móvil. Mexico, Central America and the Caribbean: carro, computadora, celular. The Southern Cone (Argentina, Chile, Uruguay): auto, computadora (computador in Chile), celular. A dashed line for the word for car separates all three boxes; a dotted line for the word for computer separates only Spain from the other two, so the two isoglosses fall in different places.](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The picture is simplified on purpose: *auto* is common in Mexico too, *carro* in Colombia and
Venezuela, and Chile also says *computadora*. So ask, for each word, where it is
usual.

## "Neutral Spanish": a working practice

*El español neutro* (neutral Spanish) is a term from dubbing, subtitling and international
publishing. Nobody speaks it at home. It is a set of decisions that lets one version of a film or
an app work in many countries. Mexico City has long been a center of Latin American dubbing:
*México Desconocido* dates it to 1944–1945, when a Hollywood studio hired Mexican radio actors to
dub in New York, and credits the neutral-sounding Spanish of the capital for helping those
versions travel (take the details as the magazine's account).

A1's *doblar* (to turn) also means "to dub": *Doblaron la serie en México* (They dubbed the series
in Mexico). What dubbers usually avoid and keep:

| Avoid | Keep |
|---|---|
| local slang (*la chamba, la lana, chido*) | general words (*el trabajo, el dinero, genial*) |
| *vosotros* (Spain) and *vos* (the Río de la Plata, Central America) | *tú* and *ustedes* |
| words harmless in one country and rude in another | words with no second sense anywhere |
| a strong regional accent | *el acento neutro*: seseo, yeísmo, careful vowels |

The best-known trap is Spain's *coger*. In Spain it means "to take, to catch" (*coger el
autobús*); in Mexico and much of Latin America it is a vulgar word for sex, so international
texts use *tomar* or *agarrar*. Recognize it; don't practice it.

"Neutral" also depends on the listener: to Argentine and Spanish ears, Latin American dubbing
sounds Mexican, and Spain usually makes its own versions. Subtitles too: in January 2019 the Spanish
subtitles Netflix offered viewers in Spain for Alfonso Cuarón's Mexican film *Roma* recast its
dialogue in Spain's Spanish, and after criticism, Cuarón's included, they were withdrawn.

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| *el estudio de doblaje* | dubbing studio |
| *el actor / la actriz de doblaje*, *el doblador / la dobladora* | voice actor, dubber |
| *la versión original* (VO) | the original-language version (*en versión original subtitulada*) |
| *subtitular*, *el subtitulaje* | to subtitle, subtitling (Mexico's usual term; Spain usually says *el subtitulado*) |
| *la voz en off* | voice-over: a voice heard but not seen |
| *la sincronía* | lip sync: lines matched to the lips |
| *la traducción audiovisual* | translation for screen: dubbing, subtitling, voice-over |

![A dubbing studio. A voice actor stands in a booth facing a large screen that shows a cartoon character. In front of her is a microphone on a stand and, beside it, a lectern holding a script. She wears headphones. Through a window behind her, a director sits at a mixing desk. Labels name la pantalla, el micrófono, el atril, el guion and los audífonos.](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The actor works in *la cabina* (the booth; an honors word of 24h3). *El atril* is the lectern,
and Spain says *los auriculares* for A2's *los audífonos* (headphones).

## Text: *Voces que cruzan fronteras*

A magazine feature; the studio and its director are invented.

> **Voces que cruzan fronteras**
>
> En una calle tranquila de la colonia Del Valle, en la Ciudad de México, una puerta sin letrero
> esconde uno de los oficios más escuchados del continente: Ámbar, un estudio de doblaje donde
> cada semana se graban series, películas animadas y documentales que se verán desde Tijuana
> hasta la Patagonia.
>
> En la cabina, una actriz de doblaje mira la pantalla, lee el guion en el atril y espera la
> señal. "La sincronía es la mitad del trabajo", explica Lucía Ferrer, directora del estudio, con
> veintidós años en el oficio. "La otra mitad es actuar: si el público nota que estamos leyendo,
> perdimos".
>
> —¿Qué es exactamente el español neutro? —le pregunto.
>
> —Una herramienta de trabajo, no un idioma —responde—. Nadie habla así en su casa. Es un
> conjunto de decisiones para que una serie se entienda igual en Lima que en Guadalajara.
> Evitamos los localismos: aquí no decimos "chamba" ni "lana", decimos "trabajo" y "dinero". No
> usamos el voseo ni el "vosotros", y cuidamos las palabras que en un país son inocentes y en otro
> no.
>
> —¿Y el acento?
>
> —Buscamos un acento neutro, que en la práctica es un acento culto, sin rasgos fuertes de
> ninguna región. Pero ojo: lo neutro depende de quién escucha. A un argentino o a un español
> nuestro doblaje le suena mexicano, y tiene razón.
>
> España, explica, suele tener sus propias versiones, con otro reparto. Por eso una misma
> película puede circular con dos doblajes al español, y en las redes nunca falta quien discuta
> cuál es mejor.
>
> Las plataformas digitales cambiaron el ritmo: piden más títulos en menos tiempo. Además del
> doblaje, Ámbar hace subtitulaje para quienes prefieren la versión original y voz en off para
> documentales. "Antes un doblador tenía tres llamados a la semana; ahora puede tener tres en un
> día", cuenta Ferrer.
>
> La traducción audiovisual tiene sus propias reglas. "Un chiste que funciona en inglés puede no
> funcionar en español, y hay que encontrar otro que quepa en el mismo segundo y medio". Cuando
> una adaptación abusa de los mexicanismos, llegan quejas de otros países.
>
> Al terminar, la actriz se quita los audífonos. "Si lo hicimos bien —dice Ferrer—, nadie se
> acuerda de que hubo un doblaje".

**Summary.** (1–2) A Mexico City studio dubs for the whole continent; for its director, lip sync
is half the job and acting the other half. (3–5) Neutral Spanish is a tool, not a language: no
local words, voseo or *vosotros*, care with words rude elsewhere, and an accent that still sounds
Mexican abroad. (6) Spain makes its own versions. (7–8) Streaming has sped the work up; jokes
must be re-created, and too many Mexicanisms bring complaints. (9) Good dubbing goes unnoticed.

**Glosses.** *Si el público nota que estamos leyendo, perdimos* = if the audience notices we're
reading, we've lost (the Mexican preterite for a certain result); *el reparto* = the cast; *un
llamado* = a booked session (dubbing jargon); *que quepa* = that fits (*caber*); *abusa de* =
overuses.

## Adapting a text for readers in other countries

1. **Find the local items**: Mexicanisms, slang, local institutions and acronyms, prices and
   times a stranger can't picture.
2. **Replace, explain or drop each one.** Use a general word (*el carro* → *el automóvil*),
   explain it once (*la colonia, es decir, el barrio*), or drop what the reader doesn't need.
3. **Don't swap one region for another.** Spain's *el coche* for *el carro* only moves the text
   to Madrid. Where no word is general (*los audífonos / los auriculares*), give both or rephrase.
4. **Make references explicit**: *250 pesos mexicanos (MXN)*, 24-hour times, acronyms spelled out
   once.
5. **Keep the register and purpose.** *Tú* works in informal texts across the Americas and Spain.

| To explain a choice | Meaning |
|---|---|
| *lo que en México se llama…* | what is called … in Mexico |
| *conocido en otros países como…* | known in other countries as… |
| *se prefirió … por ser de uso general* | … was chosen because it's in general use |
| *sustituí … por …, más comprensible fuera de México* | I replaced … with …, easier to understand outside Mexico |

### Model

A notice from a cultural center in Puebla (invented):

> ¡Ya llegó el taller de doblaje! Si te late el tema, apártate el sábado 14 de marzo de 10 a 2.
> Es en la sala 3, junto a la alberca. Cuesta 250 pesos y te puedes apuntar en la recepción o
> mandarnos un mensaje. Trae tu celular con audífonos, porque vamos a grabar escenas cortas. Al
> final habrá antojitos y aguas frescas. Si vienes en carro, hay estacionamiento, pero llega
> temprano porque se llena rapidísimo. Si te quedas sin lugar, ni modo: abriremos otro grupo en
> abril.

(The dubbing workshop is here! If you like the idea, save Saturday, March 14, 10 to 2. Room 3,
by the pool; 250 pesos; sign up at reception or message us. Bring your phone and headphones:
we'll record short scenes. Snacks and fruit drinks at the end. There's parking, but it fills up
fast. If you miss out, oh well: another group opens in April.)

A model adaptation for the center's website, for foreign students, with its note (204 words, inside the task's
200–250). It keeps every detail in general Spanish; the note gives each change and its reason:

> **Taller de doblaje**
>
> ¿Te interesa el doblaje? Te esperamos el sábado 14 de marzo, de 10:00 a 14:00, en la sala 3,
> junto a la piscina. La inscripción cuesta 250 pesos mexicanos (MXN) y puede hacerse en la
> recepción del centro o enviándonos un mensaje. Trae tu teléfono con audífonos o auriculares,
> porque grabaremos escenas breves de películas y series. Al final compartiremos un pequeño
> refrigerio con bocados típicos mexicanos y bebidas de frutas naturales. Si vienes en
> automóvil, hay estacionamiento, pero te recomendamos llegar temprano, porque los lugares se
> agotan pronto. Si el grupo se llena, no te preocupes: abriremos otro en abril.
>
> **Nota sobre los cambios.** Sustituí los mexicanismos coloquiales (*te late*, *apártate*, *ni
> modo*) por expresiones de uso general y cambié *alberca* por *piscina*, que se entiende en todos
> los países. Para *audífonos* no hay una palabra común a todos, así que di las dos más
> extendidas. *Antojitos* y *aguas frescas* no tienen equivalente exacto fuera de México, por lo
> que los describí en lugar de traducirlos. Añadí la moneda y el horario de 24 horas, y escribí
> *automóvil* en vez de *carro* sin pasar al *coche* de España. Mantuve el tuteo, adecuado para una
> invitación informal en toda la región.

Before you write, use the five steps above as a checklist, and check that the note gives each
kind of change with its reason.

```assignment
writing: es6-m5-w17-adaptacion
```

## Pronunciation

- *isoglosa*: i-so-GLO-sa, four syllables.
- *pluricéntrico*: plu-ri-CÉN-tri-co, five syllables.
- *panhispánico*: the *h* is silent, so it sounds like *pa-nis-PÁ-ni-co*.
- *sincronía*: sin-cro-NÍ-a; the accent splits *í-a* into two syllables.
- *estándar*, es-TÁN-dar, keeps its stress in the plural: *estándares*, es-TÁN-da-res.

## Common mistakes

- **"Neutral" as Spain's Spanish.** A text with *coche, ordenador, vale* isn't neutral; it's from
  Spain.
- **Mexico's norm as a dialect of the "real" one.** Each country's educated norm is a standard.
- **Over-explaining.** Gloss a local word once, if needed.
- **False friends.** *El hispanismo* isn't a Hispanic person; *la voz en off* is a voice over the
  picture, not dubbed dialogue.

## Key points

- Spanish is pluricentric: each country's *norma culta* is a standard, described together in
  ASALE's panhispanic works.
- Country marks warn a writer, but an unmarked word isn't always general.
- Isoglosses don't coincide or follow borders; *el hispanismo* is a Spanish loanword elsewhere.
- *El español neutro* is a dubbing practice, not a variety, and it still sounds like somewhere.
- To adapt: find, replace or explain, don't swap regions, make references explicit, keep the
  register.
