questions.stem: Complete with aducir in the preterite: "El diputado ___ motivos de salud para no asistir."
questions.explanation: Adujo. Aducir is conjugated like conducir: aduzco, aduje, adujo, adujeron (and adujera in the imperfect subjunctive). A regular-looking adució doesn't exist.

questions.stem: Match each verb to the manner of speaking it describes.
choices: to mutter between one's teeth, often annoyed
to stammer from nerves or surprise
questions.explanation: Mascullar is low and through the teeth; balbucear is hesitant (and what babies do); farfullar is fast and jumbled; refunfuñar is complaining under one's breath. None of them means shouting for joy.

questions.stem: This tasting wheel shows example smells and feelings. Name the descriptor for each numbered sector.

image.alt: The tasting wheel from the lesson without the descriptor names. Five numbered markers: 1 in the Aroma sector with plátano, piña, cítricos; 2 in the Aroma sector with humo de leña, brasas; 3 in the Aroma sector with tierra mojada, hongos; 4 in the Textura en boca sector with té fuerte, cáscara verde; 5 in the Textura en boca sector with terciopelo, crema.

questions.explanation: Banana, pineapple and citrus are afrutado; wood smoke and embers, ahumado; wet earth and mushrooms, terroso; strong tea and green peel leave the dry, puckering feeling called astringente; velvet and cream are aterciopelado. Salado (salty) and picante (spicy) aren't on this wheel.

questions.stem: Which verbs report how someone spoke rather than the argument they made? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Mascullar (to mutter), farfullar (to jabber) and balbucear (to stammer) describe the manner of speaking. Aducir (to offer as a reason) and esgrimir (to wield an argument) report arguments.

questions.stem: Put the parts of a tasting note in the order the lesson recommends.
questions.explanation: A tasting note follows the order of tasting: smell first (en nariz), then the mouth (en boca), then what remains (el regusto, el final), and a recommendation at the end, as in the three notes in the lesson.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The supplier cited transport problems.
questions.explanation: "El proveedor adujo problemas de transporte" (the verb-first orders "Adujo el proveedor problemas de transporte" and "Adujo problemas de transporte el proveedor" are also correct, if more literary). Aduje is the yo form (I cited), which doesn't agree with el proveedor.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The aftertaste is earthy and slightly smoky.
questions.explanation: "El regusto es terroso y ligeramente ahumado"; the two adjectives may also come in the other order. Terroso (earthy) is the tasting word; terrestre means "of the earth, terrestrial" (transporte terrestre) and doesn't describe a flavor.

questions.stem: You are writing the minutes of a meeting. Which verb reports what the director said without judging how she said it?
questions.explanation: Minutes and news reports use neutral verbs: dijo, afirmó, señaló. Masculló (muttered), espetó (snapped) and farfulló (gabbled) all carry the writer's judgment of the speaker's manner.

questions.stem: The claim report ends: "Procede peritaje. Aplica deducible." What will happen?
choices: An expert will assess the damage, and the policyholder will pay part of the cost.
The insurer will pay the whole repair without an inspection.
The police will fine the driver and impound the car.
The claim has been rejected for lack of evidence.
questions.explanation: El peritaje is the expert's appraisal, and procede means it goes ahead; el deducible is the part of the loss the policyholder pays. Nothing in the report mentions a fine, the impound lot (el corralón) or a rejection.

questions.stem: Which sentence belongs to a radio host's traffic report?
choices: Siendo las 08:50 horas, el suscrito fue alertado de un hecho de tránsito.
Vehículo tercero realiza cambio de carril sin precaución.
Y ojo, que Insurgentes sigue cargadita por un choque de hace rato, ¿eh?
Tenía raspaduras en un brazo y fue atendido en el lugar por paramédicos.
questions.explanation: The radio host talks to listeners directly (ojo, ¿eh?) and uses colloquial words (cargadita, de hace rato). The others belong to the police report (el suscrito), the claim report (nominal style, present tense) and Mariana's written statement.

questions.stem: At the family meal, Carmen says: "¡El siniestro! Como si me hubiera caído un meteorito." Why is it funny?
choices: Carmen doesn't know what siniestro means and uses it by mistake.
She drops the insurer's solemn word into family talk and plays on siniestro as "sinister".
She is quoting the radio host, who used the word first.
Siniestro is a rude word in Mexico, so the family is shocked.
questions.explanation: It is a deliberate register shift: the insurance word el siniestro (the claim) clashes with the setting, and that incongruity makes the joke; her last line, lo siniestro (what's sinister), turns it into a pun. She knows the word perfectly well, the radio host never said it, and it isn't rude.

questions.stem: A news story says: "El hospital difundió el parte médico de la cantante." What did the hospital release?
choices: Part of the singer's medical bill.
The doctor's share of the fees.
A list of the singer's doctors.
An official medical bulletin about the singer.
questions.explanation: El parte (masculine) is an official report: el parte médico is a medical bulletin. A1's la parte (feminine) means a part or share, which is what the distractors play on.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of the car, using the Mexican words.

image.alt: A side view of a sedan facing left, with five numbered markers: 1 on the top panel at the front, over the engine; 2 on the slanted front glass; 3 on the side panel over the front wheel; 4 on the top panel at the back; 5 on the rear wheel.

questions.explanation: In Mexico the hood is el cofre (Spain el capó), the trunk la cajuela (Spain el maletero), the fender la salpicadera (Spain el guardabarros); el parabrisas and la llanta (tire) are B2 and A2 words. El volante (steering wheel) is inside the car, and el tanque isn't visible.

questions.stem: The voice note says "el tipo se peló". Complete the formal version for the insurer: "El conductor de la camioneta se ___ a la fuga."
questions.explanation: Darse a la fuga (to flee the scene) is the press and police phrase: se dio a la fuga. Se peló (Mexico, informal) belongs only in casual speech.

questions.stem: Match each colloquial phrase from the voice note to its formal equivalent in Mariana's statement.
questions.explanation: Each colloquial phrase has a formal partner with the same content: se peló → se dio a la fuga, me dio → golpeó, un chavo en moto → un motociclista, no me pasó nada → resulté ilesa. Procede el peritaje (the appraisal goes ahead) translates nothing in the voice note.

questions.stem: Which features mark the voice note as colloquial? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Sound words, slang and tags are marks of speech (la oralidad). Aplica deducible is the claim report's nominal style, and el suscrito (the undersigned) is a police-report formula.

questions.stem: Put these lines from the lesson in order, from the most formal to the most intimate.
choices: Al arribar, se observó un vehículo tipo sedán con daños.
Un motociclista resultó con lesiones leves la mañana de este martes.
Una camioneta de reparto, nos cuentan, se cambió de carril así, sin poner direccional.
Me chocaron con el carro de mi mamá. Estoy bien, ¿eh?
questions.explanation: The police report (al arribar, se observó: official formulas, impersonal se) is the most formal; then the news brief (full, neutral sentences); then the radio host (nos cuentan, así: spoken, public); then the voice note to Lupe (me chocaron, mi mamá, ¿eh?).

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The driver (a woman) was unhurt.
questions.explanation: "La conductora resultó ilesa" or, with the subject after the verb, as news writing often does, "Resultó ilesa la conductora". Ilesa agrees with la conductora; ileso is the masculine.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The van's driver fled the scene.
questions.explanation: "El conductor de la camioneta se dio a la fuga", or with the subject last, "Se dio a la fuga el conductor de la camioneta". Se peló is colloquial and can't take a la fuga.

questions.stem: A driver from Madrid needs to put his luggage in la cajuela of a rented car in Mexico. What would he call it at home?
questions.explanation: Spain's word for the trunk is el maletero (Argentina says el baúl). El capó is Spain's hood (Mexico el cofre), el guardabarros the fender (Mexico la salpicadera), and el parabrisas the windshield everywhere.

questions.stem: A Mexican novel is praised for reproducing "el caló de los barrios de la capital". What does that refer to?
choices: The Romani language of Spain's Gitanos.
The formal speech of the capital's officials.
The Nahuatl spoken in the city's neighborhoods.
questions.explanation: In Mexico el caló is widely used for the slang of the street, which fiction uses to give a neighborhood its sound. Caló first means the Romani variety of the Spanish Gitanos, its usual sense in Spain, but a Mexican novel about the capital's neighborhoods points to street slang.

questions.stem: Choose the correct verb: "El equipo local le ___ una dura derrota al campeón."
questions.explanation: Infligir (to inflict) goes with una derrota, un daño, un castigo. Infringir means to break a rule (infringir una norma); inflingir is a common blend of the two that doesn't exist; absolver is to acquit.

questions.stem: A reviewer wants to say the report has many inaccuracies. Which verb, in its careful-writing sense, says that? "El informe ___ de imprecisiones."
questions.explanation: Adolecer de is to suffer from a defect: El informe adolece de imprecisiones. Carece de imprecisiones would mean it has none; detentar (to hold unlawfully) and ostentar (to hold a title, to show off) don't take de and don't fit.

questions.stem: "Las dos ganadoras recibieron sendos diplomas." What happened?
choices: The winners received two very large diplomas.
The winners shared a single diploma.
questions.explanation: Sendos means one for each: two winners, one diploma each. It doesn't mean "both" or "two each", and the popular sense "huge" isn't standard.

questions.stem: A reader complains that "el momento álgido de las negociaciones" is wrong, because álgido means "very cold". What should the ombudsman answer?
choices: He is right: the paper should have written "el momento más frío".
He is right: álgido can only describe temperatures.
The phrase is a Mexican regionalism, so it is fine only in Mexico.
The DLE records "critical, culminating" as a sense of álgido, so it isn't an error.
questions.explanation: The DLE gives álgido both "very cold" and "critical, culminating", and the second is now the usual sense. A sense the DLE records is not marked wrong. It isn't a regionalism.

questions.stem: Correct the paronym, using proveer in the preterite: "El municipio no previó de agua a tres colonias." → "El municipio no ___ de agua a tres colonias."
questions.explanation: Proveyó: proveer (to supply) is conjugated like leer, so y appears between vowels: proveyó, proveyeron, proveyendo. Prever (to foresee) doesn't take de + what is supplied.

questions.stem: Complete with enmendar in the present: "Si me equivoco, lo ___ en la siguiente edición."
questions.explanation: Enmiendo: enmendar changes e to ie in the stressed syllable (enmiendo, enmiendas, enmienda, enmiendan; but enmendamos).

questions.stem: Match each verb to its meaning.
questions.explanation: Infringir una norma, infligir un daño, absolver al acusado, expiar una culpa. "To spy on" is espiar, the paronym of expiar.

questions.stem: Which sentences use the word in its careful-writing sense? Select all that apply.
choices: La rectora ostenta el cargo desde 2022.
Los dos ciclistas recibieron sendas medallas.
La junta militar detentó el poder durante diez años.
questions.explanation: Ostentar a lawful office, sendas medallas for two cyclists (one each) and detentar for power held unlawfully are all careful uses. Adolecer de recursos uses adolecer for carecer (the DPD calls it improper), and sendos equipos uses sendos for "both" (say ambos equipos).

questions.stem: Each numbered mark on this proof is an error. Choose the correction for each.

image.alt: The newspaper proof from the lesson without the margin corrections, five numbered markers: 1 over the struck-through infringe in the headline El Atlético Bajío le infringe una goleada al líder; 2 over the circled detenta in El diputado Ramírez, que detenta la presidencia de la comisión; 3 over presupesto, with a caret under a missing letter; 4 over the underlined Hubieron in Hubieron quejas por los boletos; 5 under the circled adolece in el estadio adolece de recursos para crecer.

questions.explanation: A team inflige (inflicts) a rout; infringir is to break a rule. The deputy ocupa (holds) the chair; detentar implies he holds it unlawfully. Presupesto is a typo for presupuesto. Hubieron quejas is a solecism: impersonal haber is singular, Hubo quejas. A stadium carece de recursos (lacks them); adolecer de is for defects.

questions.stem: "Hubieron quejas por el precio de los boletos" contains which kind of error?
choices: A paronym: hubieron confused with another word.
An impropriety: a word used with a meaning it doesn't have.
A solecism: an error of syntax (agreement).
questions.explanation: Impersonal haber has no subject and stays singular: Hubo quejas. Making it agree with quejas is an error of syntax, a solecism. An impropriety is an error of meaning (adolecer for carecer); a typo is a slip of the keys.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The court acquitted the defendant (a woman).
questions.explanation: "El tribunal absolvió a la acusada" (or, verb first, "Absolvió el tribunal a la acusada" and "Absolvió a la acusada el tribunal"). Absorber, absorbió, is to absorb: its paronym absolver is the legal verb.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The company broke the building code.
questions.explanation: "La empresa infringió el reglamento de construcción" (or, verb first, "Infringió la empresa el reglamento de construcción" and "Infringió el reglamento de construcción la empresa"). Rules are infringidas (broken); damage and defeats are infligidos (inflicted).

questions.stem: A colleague wrote "el diputado detenta la presidencia". Which comment corrects it with tact and a reason?
choices: "Te sugiero cambiar detenta por ocupa: detentar sugiere que el cargo es ilegítimo."
questions.explanation: The second comment suggests rather than orders, offers an alternative and gives the reason. The first is a bare verdict, the third is a put-down, and the fourth is false: detentar exists, with the sense "to hold unlawfully".

questions.stem: Which spelling does the DPD recommend? "La directora renunció ___."
questions.explanation: Motu proprio (of one's own accord): two r's in proprio and no preposition. De motu propio, the most frequent slip, has both errors.

questions.stem: Which pair is a doublet: an inherited word and a learned word from the same Latin word?
questions.explanation: Estrecho (inherited, -ct- became -ch-) and estricto (learned, -ct- kept) both come from Latin strictum. Estrella has another origin, llamada is simply formed from llamar, and débil isn't related to delgado (whose learned twin is delicado).

questions.stem: In the axolotl's scientific name, Ambystoma mexicanum, what is "mexicanum"?
choices: the name of the scientist who described it
questions.explanation: A species name is genus + specific epithet. Ambystoma is the genus (capitalized); mexicanum, "Mexican", is the epithet (lower case). The family name isn't part of the binomial, and this epithet describes a place, not a person.

questions.stem: How does the RAE's Ortografía (2010) write the Latin phrase for "per person"?
choices: per cápita, in roman type, with an accent
per capita, in italics, without an accent
questions.explanation: The Ortografía treats Latin phrases as unadapted foreign expressions: in italics (or quotation marks) and without written accents, so per capita. The DPD (2005) wrote per cápita, which you will still see in print.

questions.stem: Complete with a two-word Latin phrase meaning "roughly": "___, la mitad de los encuestados estuvo de acuerdo."
questions.explanation: Grosso modo, with no a before it (not a grosso modo) and with double s. C1's a grandes rasgos is the Spanish equivalent.

questions.stem: Write the plural of el espécimen: "La colección guarda tres mil ___."
questions.explanation: Especímenes: unusually, the stress moves one syllable to the right in the plural (like régimen / regímenes), and the written accent moves with it: es-PÉ-ci-men, es-pe-CÍ-me-nes.

questions.stem: Match each Latin phrase to its meaning.
choices: in fact, whatever the law says
on site, in its original place
questions.explanation: A priori (beforehand), de facto (in practice), in situ (on site), sine qua non (essential: una condición sine qua non). "Of one's own accord" is motu proprio.

questions.stem: Which of these are learned words (cultismos) rather than inherited words? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Clamar keeps Latin cl-, íntegro keeps Latin stress and the -gr- cluster, and estricto keeps -ct-: all learned. Llamar (cl- became ll-) and entero (integrum worn down in speech) are their inherited twins.

questions.stem: Match each Greek or Latin element to its meaning.
questions.explanation: Hipertensión, hipotermia, políglota, democracia, ortografía. "Study of" is -logía (herpetología, biología).

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The status quo suits nobody.
questions.explanation: "El statu quo no le conviene a nadie"; also "No le conviene a nadie el statu quo", "No le conviene el statu quo a nadie" and, with nadie before the verb and no no, "A nadie le conviene el statu quo" or "El statu quo a nadie le conviene". Spanish writes statu quo (the Latin ablative), not status quo.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: She resigned from the post of her own accord.
questions.explanation: "Renunció al cargo motu proprio"; the phrase can also follow the verb directly or open the sentence. De motu propio is the classic slip: no de, and proprio has two r's.

questions.stem: What marks "estricto" as a learned word, compared with "estrecho"?
choices: It keeps the Latin -ct- cluster that speech turned into -ch-.
It is used only in Spain.
It comes from Greek, not Latin.
questions.explanation: Both come from Latin strictum. Speech turned -ct- into -ch- (estrecho); the learned borrowing kept it (estricto). Syllable count is no test, both are general Spanish, and neither is Greek.

questions.stem: In which context is "grosso modo" a good choice?
choices: A text message to a friend: "Grosso modo llego a las ocho."
A shopping list: "Tomates, grosso modo dos kilos."
A report: "Grosso modo, el gasto se duplicó en cinco años."
A birthday card: "Te quiero grosso modo."
questions.explanation: Latin phrases belong to formal writing, where they summarize precisely (roughly, the spending doubled). In a text, a list or a card they are decoration at best: más o menos, como a las ocho or unos dos kilos do the job, and "roughly" love is a joke.

questions.stem: Which dictionary describes all the Spanish used in Mexico from 1921 on, not just what differs from Spain?
questions.explanation: The Diccionario del español de México, made at El Colegio de México, describes Mexican Spanish as a whole. The Diccionario de mexicanismos lists only what is particular to Mexico; the DLE covers general Spanish; the DPD advises on doubtful usage.

questions.stem: A sense in the DLE is marked "desus." What does that tell you?
choices: It is used only in Spain.
It is obsolete: found in older texts, not in current use.
questions.explanation: Desus. stands for desusado (obsolete). Derogatory is despect., colloquial coloq., and a country mark such as Esp. limits a sense by place.

questions.stem: Under which headword would you find "cantaríamos" in a Spanish dictionary?
questions.explanation: Spanish dictionaries file verbs under the infinitive, so every form of cantar is lemmatized under cantar. Canto is also a noun with its own entry (song, edge).

questions.stem: Which is the best dictionary-style definition of "el croquis"?
choices: Dibujo rápido y esquemático de un lugar, un objeto o una situación.
questions.explanation: It gives a genus (dibujo) and a difference (rápido y esquemático…), and it can replace the noun in a sentence. The first is circular, the third is too narrow and vague, and the fourth is an adjective phrase defining a noun.

questions.stem: A corpus shows that word A is three times as frequent as word B. What can you conclude?
choices: Word A is correct and word B is wrong.
Word A fits any sentence where B fits.
Word A is more common; whether it fits your sentence depends on its meaning and company.
questions.explanation: Frequency tells you how common a word is, not whether it fits. Check the concordance lines for meaning and collocations. A less frequent word can be exactly right, and it isn't obsolete unless a dictionary or the corpus dates show it.

questions.stem: Lemmatize: under which headword does a dictionary file "adujeron"?
questions.explanation: Adujeron is the ellos preterite of aducir (like conducir: condujeron), so it is filed under the infinitive aducir.

questions.stem: Write the plural: "El CORPES XXI y el Corpus del Español son dos ___ muy consultados."
questions.explanation: El corpus, los corpus: the plural is invariable, like el lapsus, los lapsus.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this dictionary entry.

image.alt: The simplified entry for cofre from the lesson, without the blue labels. Five numbered markers: 1 beside the bold word cofre; 2 above (Del fr. coffre); 3 beside the number 2. that opens the second sense; 4 above the abbreviation Méx.; 5 beside the italic sentence Abrió el cofre para revisar el motor.

questions.explanation: The headword (lema) opens the entry; the origin (Del fr. coffre) follows in parentheses; each numbered sense is an acepción; Méx. is a usage label limiting the sense to Mexico; the italic sentence is an example. This entry has no synonym and no cross-reference (remisión).

questions.stem: Match each work to what it does.
choices: records general Spanish, with country and usage labels
describes all the Spanish used in Mexico
lists words and senses particular to Mexico
groups words by meaning, without definitions
questions.explanation: The DLE (RAE and ASALE) covers general Spanish; the DEM (El Colegio de México) is descriptive of Mexican Spanish as a whole; the Academia Mexicana's dictionary is contrastive; the DPD is normative. Grouping words by meaning is what a thesaurus (un tesauro) does.

questions.stem: Which can a corpus search show you directly? Select all that apply.
choices: how often a word is used
in which countries a word is used more
which words it usually appears with
whether a usage is officially correct
which Latin word it comes from
questions.explanation: A corpus gives frequency, distribution by country (when texts are tagged by country) and collocations, through its concordance lines. It records use, so it can't rule on correctness (that is the DPD's job), and it holds texts, not etymologies (a dictionary gives those).

questions.stem: Put the parts of the lesson's entry for "cofre" in the order they appear, from the start of the entry to the end of sense 2.
choices: the definition: Cubierta del motor de un automóvil.
questions.explanation: The entry opens with the headword and its origin; each sense then gives its number, its part of speech, any usage label, the definition and, after it, an example.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: This sense is marked as obsolete.
questions.explanation: "Esta acepción está marcada como desusada" (or, with the subject last, "Está marcada como desusada esta acepción"). Desusada agrees with acepción, a feminine noun.

questions.stem: Using the lesson's corpus evidence, choose the verb: "El asaltante ___ una navaja y exigió el dinero."
questions.explanation: Esgrimir takes weapons literally (esgrimir una navaja) as well as arguments figuratively; aducir takes only reasons. Apostillar is a verb of saying, and argüyó is misspelled (arguyó) and doesn't take objects like a knife.

questions.stem: Which demonym for people from Monterrey suits an official report?
questions.explanation: Regiomontano is the formal demonym (from a Latin rendering of "royal mountain"), written in lower case. Regio is its colloquial short form; montereyano isn't used; and Spanish doesn't capitalize demonyms.

questions.stem: What is true of the word "chilango" today?
choices: It is the official demonym of Mexico City, used in laws.
It is still always an insult.
It is colloquial; once a derogatory nickname, it is now used proudly by many people from the city.
It refers to people from the Estado de México.
questions.explanation: Chilango began as a derogatory nickname and has largely lost that charge; the RAE records it as colloquial. In formal writing, capitalino or a phrase naming the city is safer. People from the Estado de México are mexiquenses.

questions.stem: What does the usual etymology give for the name Guadalajara?
questions.explanation: Guadalajara comes from Arabic wādī al-ḥijāra, river or valley of stones; guad- (river) also begins Guadalquivir. Mexico's Guadalajara took the Spanish city's name, usually said to be the hometown of Nuño Beltrán de Guzmán, the conquistador who ordered its founding.

questions.stem: A news story says "un ciclista mexiquense". Where is he from?
questions.explanation: Mexiquense is the demonym of the Estado de México, a state that surrounds much of Mexico City but is a different entity. People from Mexico City are capitalinos; people from Mexico in general, mexicanos.

questions.stem: Which sentence is written correctly in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Spanish writes demonyms in lower case (unlike English), and tapatíos keeps its accent on the i.

questions.stem: Write the Spanish exonym: "El próximo congreso será en ___ (London)."
questions.explanation: Londres is the established Spanish exonym for London, and Spanish prose uses it.

questions.stem: Complete with the demonym (masculine singular): "Mi suegro nació en Guadalajara: es ___."
questions.explanation: Tapatío is the usual demonym for Guadalajara, Jalisco, in every register; guadalajarense is also used. Write it in lower case.

questions.stem: Match each Nahuatl place-name ending to the meaning scholars usually give it.
choices: place of, where there are many
questions.explanation: Chapultepec (-tepec, at the hill), Mazatlán (-tlan, place of deer), Zapopan (-pan, on), Acapulco (-co, place). Saints come from the Spanish layer, never from a Nahuatl ending.

questions.stem: Match each place name to the layer it comes from.
choices: a saint joined to an Indigenous name
questions.explanation: Mazatlán is Nahuatl (place of deer); Alcalá is Arabic al-qalʿa (the fortress); the state of Hidalgo honors Miguel Hidalgo; San Juan Teotihuacan joins a patron saint to a Nahuatl name.

questions.stem: Which of these are Spanish exonyms (Spanish names for foreign places that differ from the local name)? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Londres (London), Nueva York (New York) and Pekín (Beijing) are Spanish names for foreign cities. Guadalajara and Monterrey are Spanish-speaking cities whose local names these are.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The church is dedicated to Saint John.
questions.explanation: "El templo está bajo la advocación de San Juan" (or, subject last, "Está bajo la advocación de San Juan el templo"). La advocación is the dedication of a church or town to a saint; el patrono is the saint himself.

questions.stem: How does the RAE recommend writing and saying the name of the country?
choices: Written México, with the x pronounced like Spanish j.
Written México, with the x pronounced ks, as in taxi.
questions.explanation: The x in México (and Oaxaca, Texas) is an old spelling of the sound that became j. The RAE recommends the spelling with x and the j sound; Méjico is recorded but rare and old-fashioned, and the accent is required in Spanish.

questions.stem: A state tourism office is writing a formal press release for readers across the Spanish-speaking world. Which version is best?
choices: Los chilangos y los regios llenaron los hoteles.
Los Capitalinos y los Regiomontanos llenaron los hoteles.
Visitantes de la Ciudad de México y de Monterrey llenaron los hoteles.
Los defeños y los regios llenaron los hoteles.
questions.explanation: Naming the cities is clear to every reader and neutral in register. Chilango and regio are colloquial, defeño is fading, and demonyms are never capitalized in Spanish.

questions.stem: A news report says: "Dos horas después, la policía detenía al sospechoso." What does "detenía" express here?
choices: A single, finished arrest, told with a slowed-down narrative effect
A habit: the police used to arrest the suspect
An arrest that was under way but never completed
A guess about what the police probably did
questions.explanation: This is the narrative imperfect: a single completed event, pinned down by the time phrase "Dos horas después". The preterite "detuvo" would say the same plainly; the imperfect holds the camera on the moment. Without the time phrase, "detenía" would more likely read as a habit or as an action in progress.

questions.stem: A newspaper writes: "El exfuncionario habría salido del país el viernes." What is the best reading in a news report?
choices: He left the country on Friday, as officially confirmed
He would have left the country on Friday if he had been allowed to
He has reportedly left the country on Friday; the paper doesn't vouch for it
He was about to leave the country on Friday
questions.explanation: In the press, the conditional of rumor marks unconfirmed information: "reportedly". It is not a confirmed fact, and there is no "if" clause. Style guides advise reporters to attribute instead: "Según fuentes de la fiscalía, el exfuncionario salió del país el viernes."

questions.stem: Choose the best translation of "Será muy buen detective, pero no sabe escribir."
choices: He'll be a very good detective, but he can't write.
He may be a very good detective, but he can't write.
He was a very good detective, but he couldn't write.
He would be a very good detective if he could write.
questions.explanation: This is the concessive future: "será" grants a point before "pero" (He may be…, but…). It isn't a prediction about the future, and nothing in the sentence is past or conditional.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses the historical present?
choices: Mañana publico la reseña de la novela.
Cada año se publican decenas de novelas negras.
En 1953, María Elvira Bermúdez publica su primera novela.
questions.explanation: The historical present tells a past event in the present: 1953 is long past, yet the verb is "publica". "Mañana publico" is a present used for a planned future, "cada año se publican" a habit, and "¿Publico ya…?" a present asking what to do now.

questions.stem: Which sentence is the plain modern equivalent of the literary "Apenas hubo terminado la frase, cerró los ojos"?
choices: Mientras terminaba la frase, cerró los ojos.
En cuanto terminó la frase, cerró los ojos.
Apenas terminaría la frase, cerró los ojos.
Antes de terminar la frase, cerró los ojos.
questions.explanation: The pretérito anterior ("hubo terminado") marks an event right before another: no sooner had he finished than he closed his eyes. Everyday Spanish says "En cuanto terminó…" (or "Apenas terminó…"). "Mientras terminaba" makes the two overlap, "Antes de terminar" reverses the order, and "terminaría" is a conditional that doesn't fit.

questions.stem: Rewrite as a guess with the future perfect: "Probablemente salió por la puerta de atrás." → "___ por la puerta de atrás."
questions.explanation: The future perfect expresses a guess about the recent past: "Habrá salido por la puerta de atrás" (He must have gone out the back door). "Saldría" (conditional of conjecture) is also possible Spanish, but the task asks for the future perfect.

questions.stem: Complete with the concessive future of "ser": "El comisario ___ terco, pero nunca miente."
questions.explanation: "Será terco, pero…" grants a point (He may be stubborn, but…). The plain present "es" would state it as a fact; the task asks for the concessive future.

questions.stem: Match each sentence to the use of its tense.
left: Dos horas después, la policía detenía al sospechoso.
El sospechoso habría huido a otro estado.
Yo era el detective y tú eras el ladrón.
choices: narrative imperfect: a finished event, slowed down
conditional of conjecture: a guess about the past
future of command: a solemn order
playful imperfect: setting up a game
historical present: a past event told as now
questions.explanation: Each tense is used for an effect: the narrative imperfect slows a finished event; the conditional of rumor reports without confirming; the conditional of conjecture guesses about a past moment; the future of command gives a solemn order; children set up games with the imperfect. No sentence here is in the historical present.

questions.stem: A style guide asks you to replace the conditional of rumor in "El alcalde habría recibido sobornos" with attribution. Which rewrites do that? Select all that apply.
choices: Según la denuncia de la fiscalía, el alcalde recibió sobornos.
El alcalde recibió sobornos, de acuerdo con dos testigos citados por la fiscalía.
Se dice que el alcalde habría recibido sobornos.
questions.explanation: Attribution names the source of the claim: "Según la denuncia de la fiscalía…", "…de acuerdo con dos testigos citados por la fiscalía". "Recibiría" is still an unattributed conditional, and "Se dice que… habría recibido" keeps the rumor conditional and adds only a vague "it is said".

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this book jacket.

image.alt: A book jacket laid flat: the back cover with a block of text lines and a bar code on the left, the spine, and the dark blue front cover on the right with a title, a pale silhouette of a man in a hat beside a streetlamp, a large fingerprint and a small round logo. Six numbers mark the back cover, the text block, the title, the hat, the fingerprint and the logo.

questions.explanation: The back of the jacket is la contraportada, and its text block la sinopsis (C1 words). On the front: el título, el sombrero, la huella dactilar (fingerprint; Mexico also says la huella digital), and the publisher's logo, la editorial. A capítulo is inside the book, and a columna is in a newspaper.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Two hours later, the police arrested the suspect. (Use the narrative imperfect.)
questions.explanation: Narrative imperfect with its time anchor: "Dos horas después, la policía detenía al sospechoso." The subject can also follow the verb, as often in news writing: "Dos horas después, detenía la policía al sospechoso" or "…detenía al sospechoso la policía". "Detenga" is a subjunctive and can't be the main verb here.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: He may be stubborn, but he isn't stupid. (Use the concessive future.)
questions.explanation: The concessive future grants a point before "pero": "Será terco, pero no es tonto." The first half concedes, the second half makes the real claim.

questions.stem: What does "De haberlo sabido, te habría avisado" mean?
choices: If I find out, I'll let you know.
Had I known, I would have told you.
Since I knew it, I told you.
Having known it for a while, I told you.
questions.explanation: "De" + compound infinitive ("de haberlo sabido") is a condition about a past that didn't happen, like "Si lo hubiera sabido". The apodosis "te habría avisado" confirms it: I didn't know, so I didn't tell you.

questions.stem: What is the speaker doing in "Como no llegues a las ocho, nos vamos"?
choices: Warning: if you're not here by eight, we're leaving
Giving a reason: since you didn't arrive, we're leaving
Comparing: like you, we're leaving at eight
Asking how you'll get here by eight
questions.explanation: "Como" + subjunctive ("llegues") is a condition, usually a warning or a threat. With the indicative, "como" gives a reason: "Como no llegaste, nos fuimos" (Since you didn't come, we left).

questions.stem: Which sentence is a mixed-time counterfactual: a past condition with a present result?
choices: Si no hubiera llegado la imprenta, hoy leeríamos menos.
questions.explanation: The protasis "si no hubiera llegado" is past, and the apodosis "hoy leeríamos" is about the present. The first sentence is past in both halves, the second present in both, and the last is an open, real condition.

questions.stem: In "Si llueve, se suspende el partido", which part is the apodosis?
questions.explanation: The apodosis is the result: "se suspende el partido". The protasis is the condition, "si llueve". Either half may come first.

questions.stem: Which phrase means "be that as it may" and belongs to formal writing?
questions.explanation: "Sea como fuere" is a fixed phrase with the future subjunctive "fuere"; the everyday form is "sea como sea". "Aunque sea" means "even if" or "at least", "así sea" "so be it", and "ni que fuera" "as if it were".

questions.stem: Complete with "de" + compound infinitive: "___ la verdad, no habría firmado." (If I had known the truth…)
questions.explanation: "De haber sabido la verdad, no habría firmado" (Had I known the truth, I wouldn't have signed). The compound infinitive "haber sabido" places the condition in a past that didn't happen. "Si hubiera sabido" means the same, but the task asks for the structure without si.

questions.stem: Complete the formal fixed phrase with the future subjunctive of "ser": "Sean cuales ___ los resultados, los publicaremos."
questions.explanation: With a plural noun the phrase is "sean cuales fueren los resultados" (whatever the results may be). The everyday version "sean cuales sean" is also correct, but the task asks for the future subjunctive.

questions.stem: Match each sentence to its meaning.
left: De no ser por ella, nos habríamos perdido.
Bien mirado, el error tiene arreglo.
choices: If you study even a little, you'll pass.
Just letting us know would have been enough.
If it hadn't been for her, we'd have got lost.
If we leave now, we'll be on time.
Looked at carefully, the mistake can be fixed.
questions.explanation: Each structure carries a condition without si: "a poco que" + subjunctive (even a little), "con" + infinitive (just by), "de no ser por" + noun (but for), a gerund (if we…), and a set participle phrase. "Unless" would be "a menos que" or "de no ser que".

questions.stem: Which sentences contain a condition without si? Select all that apply.
choices: De seguir así, cerraremos en un año.
A poco que llueva, se inunda la calle.
questions.explanation: "De seguir así" (if things go on like this) and "a poco que llueva" (if it rains even a little) are conditions. "Como no llegaste", with the indicative, gives a reason, and "salió corriendo" is a gerund of manner, not a condition.

questions.stem: Rewrite with "de" + infinitive: "Si seguimos así, cerraremos en un año." → "___ así, cerraremos en un año."
questions.explanation: "De seguir así, cerraremos en un año." The simple infinitive points to the present or the future; the subject (nosotros) is the same as in the main clause, so it isn't repeated.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Had they won, everything would be different.
questions.explanation: With "de" + compound infinitive, a subject different from the main clause's goes after the infinitive: "De haber ganado ellos, todo sería distinto." "Hubieran" can't follow "de"; with si it would be "Si hubieran ganado ellos…".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: If it hadn't been for the printing press, the book would have been lost.
questions.explanation: "De no ser por" + noun is the protasis: "De no ser por la imprenta, el libro se habría perdido." The subject may also follow the verb: "…, se habría perdido el libro."

questions.stem: What does "Los vecinos, que protestaron, recibieron respuesta" say?
choices: Only the residents who protested got an answer.
All the residents protested, and they got an answer.
The residents got an answer before they protested.
The residents who didn't protest got no answer.
questions.explanation: The commas make the relative clause nonrestrictive: it adds information about all the residents (they protested). Without commas, "Los vecinos que protestaron recibieron respuesta" would single out the ones who protested.

questions.stem: Which sentence is right for careful written Spanish?
choices: Es una colonia que sus calles se hunden.
Es una colonia cuyos calles se hunden.
Es una colonia cuyas calles se hunden.
Es una colonia cuya calles se hunden.
questions.explanation: "Cuyo" agrees with the thing possessed, "calles" (feminine plural): "cuyas calles". "Que sus calles" is frequent in speech, but the DPD advises against it in careful language; the other two have the wrong agreement.

questions.stem: Choose the relative a formal text would use: "Esta es la norma conforme a ___ se otorgan los permisos."
questions.explanation: After a compound preposition like "conforme a", formal Spanish prefers an article with the relative: "conforme a la cual" ("conforme a la que" also works). Bare "que" doesn't follow such a preposition, "quien" is for people, and "cuya" expresses possession.

questions.stem: Which sentence is NOT standard?
choices: Los vecinos, quienes presentaron la queja, esperan respuesta.
Los vecinos que presentaron la queja esperan respuesta.
Los vecinos, que presentaron la queja, esperan respuesta.
Los vecinos quienes presentaron la queja esperan respuesta.
questions.explanation: After a noun, "quien" without a preposition appears only in a nonrestrictive clause, between commas. A restrictive clause takes "que": "Los vecinos que presentaron la queja…".

questions.stem: In which sentence is a comma used wrongly?
choices: Los edificios, que se construyeron sobre arcilla, se inclinan.
El primer pozo, perforado en 1950, se secó; el segundo todavía funciona.
Los edificios construidos sobre la antigua zona lacustre, se inclinan.
La arcilla —según los geólogos— se compacta.
questions.explanation: A single comma never separates a subject from its verb, however long the subject. In the first sentence the commas come in a pair around an aside, which is correct.

questions.stem: Complete with the right form of "cuyo": "El edificio ___ cimentación falló fue desalojado."
questions.explanation: "Cuyo" agrees with the thing possessed, "cimentación" (feminine singular): "cuya cimentación". The building whose foundations failed was evacuated.

questions.stem: Complete with a relative that refers to the whole clause: "El suelo cede, ___ agrieta los muros."
questions.explanation: "Lo cual" and "lo que" both refer back to a whole idea: the ground gives way, which cracks the walls. "Lo cual" is slightly more formal; "el cual" or "que" alone would point to a noun.

questions.stem: Put the steps for unpacking a long sentence in the order the lesson gives.
choices: Find the main verb and its subject
Link each relative to its antecedent
Decide whether the sentence should be split
questions.explanation: Start with the skeleton (main verb and subject), set the asides aside, connect each relative to its noun, and only then judge whether the sentence works or should be split.

questions.stem: Which phrases use a relative correctly? Select all that apply.
choices: el pozo del que sacan el agua
la falla sobre la cual se abrió la grieta
questions.explanation: After a preposition Spanish uses an article + "que", "el cual", or "quien" for people. Without a preposition, a restrictive clause takes plain "que": "el pozo que perforaron", not "el pozo el cual perforaron".

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this cross-section.

image.alt: A cross-section of the ground under a city street: buildings on the street, one tilting with a crack in its wall, and a pump house; a brown clay layer; below it a blue water-bearing layer crossed by a dashed line; a pipe from the pump house down into the blue layer; and a bracket on the left spanning both layers. Six numbers mark the crack, the clay, the blue layer, the dashed line, the pipe and the bracket.

questions.explanation: La grieta is the crack in the wall; la arcilla the soft lake clay; el acuífero the water-bearing layer below; el manto freático the top of the water (the dashed line); el pozo the pipe drilled down to the water; el subsuelo everything below the surface. A socavón is a hole that opens in the street, and a presa a dam: neither is shown.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The ground gives way, which cracks the walls.
questions.explanation: "Lo cual" refers to the whole clause before it: "El suelo cede, lo cual agrieta los muros." "El cual" would need a masculine noun as its antecedent, and here the antecedent is the whole event.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: They live in a neighborhood whose streets are sinking. (For a formal report.)
questions.explanation: "Cuyo" agrees with the thing possessed, "calles": "Viven en una colonia cuyas calles se hunden." "Cuyos" would agree with nothing in the sentence.

questions.stem: Which phrase fits this formal report? "___ la vigilancia comunitaria, la tala ilegal disminuyó." (thanks to)
questions.explanation: "Merced a" is a formal "gracias a" and introduces a cause that helped. "En detrimento de" is "to the harm of", "so pretexto de" "on the pretext of", and "a expensas de" "at the expense of".

questions.stem: In "Sin perjuicio de otras sanciones, se clausurará el aserradero", what does "sin perjuicio de" mean?
choices: without affecting (the other penalties still apply)
questions.explanation: "Sin perjuicio de" means that the other penalties are not affected: the closure is added to them. It doesn't mean "despite" or "instead of".

questions.stem: Which phrase does the DPD (2nd edition, provisional) recommend in place of "en base a"?
questions.explanation: The DPD advises against "en base a" and recommends "sobre la base de" or "a base de"; it also says "con base en" has no linguistic fault, though careful style prefers the other two. "A nivel de" means something else, and the last two aren't set phrases.

questions.stem: Choose the preposition the verb requires: "El conteo ___ medir la superficie ocupada."
questions.explanation: "Consistir" takes "en": "El conteo consiste en medir la superficie ocupada." "Consistir de" is modeled on English "consist of".

questions.stem: Which phrase means "lagging behind"?
questions.explanation: "Ir a la zaga (de)" is to lag behind. "A la luz de" is "in light of", "en vísperas de" "on the eve of", and "al amparo de" "under the protection of".

questions.stem: Complete with the formal phrase meaning "on the eve of": "___ la migración, las monarcas se alimentan sin descanso."
questions.explanation: "En vísperas de la migración" (on the eve of the migration). "En la víspera de" is also correct.

questions.stem: Complete with the preposition: "La vigilancia redunda ___ beneficio de todos."
questions.explanation: "Redundar en" (to result in): "redunda en beneficio de todos" (it benefits everyone).

questions.stem: Match each formal phrase to its plain equivalent.
questions.explanation: Each formal phrase has a plain equivalent that is never wrong: a tenor de / según, a efectos de / para, en lo tocante a / en cuanto a, a falta de / sin, a instancias de / a petición de. "A pesar de" (despite) matches none of them.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct in formal Spanish? Select all that apply.
choices: A la luz de los nuevos datos, conviene revisar el plan.
En la luz de los datos, el plan cambió.
El hotel creció a expensas de los vecinos.
El conteo consiste de medir la superficie.
questions.explanation: "A la luz de" is fixed (not "en la luz de"), and "consistir" takes "en". "A expensas de los vecinos" (at the neighbors' expense) is correct.

questions.stem: Complete with the preposition: "Las comunidades abogan ___ un corredor biológico."
questions.explanation: "Abogar por" (to call for, to advocate): "abogan por un corredor biológico".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: In light of the new data, the plan should be revised.
questions.explanation: "A la luz de" + noun opens the sentence: "A la luz de los nuevos datos, conviene revisar el plan." "En la luz de" isn't the fixed phrase.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The communities are calling for a wildlife corridor.
questions.explanation: "Abogar" takes "por": "Las comunidades abogan por un corredor biológico." The subject can also go last: "Abogan por un corredor biológico las comunidades."

questions.stem: What does the date 1207 in the Cantar de mio Cid's manuscript tell us?
choices: The year the poem was composed
The date in the note (colophon) at the end of the only manuscript
The year the historical Cid died
The year Alfonso X had the poem copied
questions.explanation: The only manuscript ends with a note naming Per Abbat and a date that corresponds to 1207. Many scholars think the note was copied from an earlier manuscript; the surviving copy is usually dated to the fourteenth century, and the date of composition (about 1140? nearer 1200?) is debated.

questions.stem: In thirteenth-century Castilian, what did the x in "dixo" probably sound like?
questions.explanation: Old x was a "sh" sound; it later became the j sound, and the spelling changed to "dijo".

questions.stem: What were the jarchas?
choices: Romance closing verses of poems written in Arabic or Hebrew
Copyists' notes in the margins of manuscripts
questions.explanation: The jarchas close a kind of poem (the moaxaja) written in al-Andalus in Arabic or Hebrew; some close in a Romance language mixed with Arabic. They are read through reconstruction, and their place in the history of lyric is debated.

questions.stem: What form is "fueredes" in "Si vos a la feria fueredes"?
choices: A future subjunctive with the old second-person plural ending -edes
questions.explanation: The future subjunctive ("fuere") was ordinary in conditions; "-edes" is the second-person plural ending before it lost its d, used with vos for one person or several. Here the wife speaks to her husband with a respectful vos; today: "Si vas a la feria".

questions.stem: Why do modern editions of the same medieval work differ?
choices: Medieval authors rewrote every copy themselves
Copyists made slips and changes, and editors compare the copies and choose differently
The RAE revises old texts every decade
Old texts were written in Latin and translated differently
questions.explanation: Every hand copy has traces of its copyist: eye-skips, "corrections", modernized spellings. Editors compare the surviving copies and make choices, which is why a critical edition explains them.

questions.stem: What is a "cantar de gesta"?
choices: A short love poem closing an Arabic poem
An epic poem about a hero's deeds, made to be recited
questions.explanation: A cantar de gesta tells the deeds (gestas) of a hero and was performed by juglares. The jarchas are the short closing verses, and the Siete Partidas the law code.

questions.stem: What is Alfonso X's court credited with?
choices: Bringing the printing press to Castile
Writing the Cantar de mio Cid
Giving Castilian prose its first steady written form
questions.explanation: Alfonso X (king 1252–1284) had histories, the Siete Partidas and scientific works produced, many in Castilian rather than Latin. The jarchas and the Cantar are not his, and printing came two centuries later.

questions.stem: In "ca las aguas eran asaz grandes", what do "ca" and "asaz" mean?
questions.explanation: "Ca" is an old "because", and "asaz" means "very, quite": because the waters were very high.

questions.stem: Which reading strategy does the lesson put first?
choices: Look up every word in a dictionary
Count the syllables of each line
questions.explanation: Reading aloud comes first: many words that look strange on the page ("fablar", "fijo") are recognizable by ear. Then come the regular swaps, the verbs and the little words.

questions.stem: Write the modern spelling of the Old Spanish verb "fablar".
questions.explanation: Latin f- became an aspirated sound and then silent; the spelling h- came later: fablar → hablar, like fazer → hacer and fijo → hijo.

questions.stem: Match each Old Spanish form to its modern form.
questions.explanation: f- became h-, ç became z, the voiceless ss became s, x became j, and -ades lost its d (-áis). "Tenía" is the modern form of "tenie", which isn't listed.

questions.stem: Name the numbered features of this imitation manuscript page.

image.alt: An imitation of a medieval manuscript page: a large red capital E, then eight lines of brown text in old spellings. Six numbers mark the red capital, the mark over the n in the first line, the f of fazer, the ss of passar, the ç of plaça and the x of dixo.

questions.explanation: The red E is la mayúscula; the line over the n is la tilde, an abbreviation for a second n (año = anno); fazer has la f inicial that became h; passar has la doble s; plaça has la cedilla; dixo has la x that became j. A jarcha is a kind of verse and a copista a person, not marks on the page.

questions.stem: Put these events in chronological order.
choices: Rodrigo Díaz, the historical Cid, lives (eleventh century)
The date given in the Cantar's colophon (1207)
The first printing press reaches Mexico City (1539)
Samuel Miklos Stern draws attention to the jarchas (1948)
questions.explanation: The historical Cid lived in the eleventh century; the colophon gives 1207; Alfonso X reigned from 1252; printing reached Mexico City in 1539 (lesson 06); Stern's work on the jarchas dates from 1948.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The copyist skipped a line.
questions.explanation: "Saltarse" (to skip): "El copista se saltó una línea." The subject can also follow the verb: "Se saltó una línea el copista", "Se saltó el copista una línea". "Se salió" means "went out" or "leaked" and doesn't fit.

questions.stem: Complete for careful writing: "La mayoría de los vecinos ___ molestos."
questions.explanation: With "la mayoría de" + a plural noun the verb may be singular or plural, but the DPD (2005, concordancia §4.8) calls only the plural normal when the verb has a predicate adjective: "están molestos". "Está" and "estaba" are singular, and "es" is the wrong verb for a state.

questions.stem: Complete for careful writing: "La gente, cansada de esperar, ___."
questions.explanation: A collective noun takes a singular verb in its own clause. An aside between subject and verb ("cansada de esperar") doesn't make a new clause, so the plural would be a mismatch.

questions.stem: Which sentence is NOT standard?
questions.explanation: In the passive with se, the verb agrees with the noun: "se venden casas". "Se vende casas" is frequent on signs but nonstandard. "Se busca a los responsables" is impersonal (people introduced by a), so the singular is standard there.

questions.stem: Complete: "Lo que necesito ___ vacaciones."
questions.explanation: With a neuter subject ("lo que") and a plural predicate noun, "ser" agrees with the predicate: "Lo que necesito son vacaciones". "Están" is the wrong verb for identifying something, and "sea" the wrong mood.

questions.stem: Complete: "La víctima, un hombre de 40 años, fue ___ al hospital."
questions.explanation: "Víctima" is an epicene noun: feminine for anyone. The participle agrees with the noun, "trasladada", even though the victim is a man.

questions.stem: What is syllepsis?
choices: A noun used with either gender
Agreement by meaning rather than by grammatical form
An old spelling of a word
questions.explanation: Syllepsis is agreement by sense: "La gente llegó tarde y se quejaron" puts the second verb in the plural because people are many. A noun with either gender is an ambiguous noun.

questions.stem: Which noun is epicene?
questions.explanation: "La persona" is feminine whatever the person's sex: an epicene noun. "Estudiante" changes its article (el / la estudiante), "presidenta" is a feminine form, and "mar" is an ambiguous noun: one thing, two genders.

questions.stem: For "Es uno de los que más ___", what does the DPD (2005, concordancia §4.11) say?
choices: Both are accepted; the plural is the more grammatical.
questions.explanation: The subject of the relative is "los que" (plural), so "saben" is the more grammatical choice, but the singular "sabe" is also accepted. Use the plural in writing; don't mark the singular wrong.

questions.stem: Complete: "Tanto el alcalde como la gobernadora ___ a la reunión."
questions.explanation: With "tanto… como", the two subjects add up: plural, "asistieron".

questions.stem: Complete with "vender" in the present: "Se ___ departamentos."
questions.explanation: In the passive with se, the verb agrees with "departamentos": "Se venden departamentos". "Se vende departamentos" is nonstandard.

questions.stem: Which sentences have standard agreement? Select all that apply.
choices: La mayoría de los vecinos votó a favor.
La mayoría de los vecinos votaron a favor.
El informe de los peritos llegaron ayer.
El comité decidió aplazar la votación.
questions.explanation: With "la mayoría de" + a plural noun and no predicate adjective, both "votó" and "votaron" are accepted. A collective like "el comité" takes the singular. In the third sentence the head of the subject is "informe", so the verb must be "llegó".

questions.stem: Match each sentence to the reason for its agreement.
left: Lo que preocupa son las grietas.
La mayoría de las familias están preocupadas.
choices: neuter subject with a plural predicate
epicene noun: agreement with the noun
passive se: the verb agrees with the noun
questions.explanation: Each sentence follows one rule from the lesson. None has a compound subject joined by o.

questions.stem: Correct the verb: "La revisión de las viviendas mostraron daños graves." → "La revisión de las viviendas ___ daños graves."
questions.explanation: The head of the subject is "revisión" (singular); "viviendas" is inside a phrase. So: "La revisión de las viviendas mostró daños graves."

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Most of the families are worried.
questions.explanation: With a predicate adjective, "la mayoría de" + plural takes the plural: "La mayoría de las familias están preocupadas". The verb can also come first: "Están preocupadas la mayoría de las familias".

questions.stem: In the speech, the author says "Leí a Rulfo a los catorce años." Which figure is "Rulfo" here?
questions.explanation: She read Rulfo's books, not the man: the author stands for his work, a link of closeness, which is metonymy. There is no part and whole (synecdoche), no resemblance (metaphor) and nothing given human traits.

questions.stem: "En mi casa había seis bocas que alimentar." Which figure is "seis bocas"?
questions.explanation: A mouth is a part of a person, and here it names the whole person: the part for the whole is synecdoche. Nothing is out of order (hyperbaton), contradictory (oxymoron) or reversed (chiasmus).

questions.stem: Which figure is "una calma impaciente"?
questions.explanation: Two words whose meanings clash, inside one phrase: calm and impatient. That is an oxymoron. A whole self-contradicting statement would be a paradox.

questions.stem: "La literatura no cambió a mi pueblo; mi pueblo cambió mi literatura." Which figure repeats the two key nouns in reverse order?
questions.explanation: Literatura… pueblo / pueblo… literatura: A B, then B A. That reversal is chiasmus (the sentence is also an antithesis). Anaphora repeats the start of phrases; hyperbole exaggerates; asyndeton drops conjunctions.

questions.stem: Match each example to its figure.
left: y llovía y tronaba y nadie salía
Primero dudó, luego sospechó y al final lo supo.
El viento golpeaba la puerta pidiendo entrar.
questions.explanation: Polysyndeton repeats "y"; asyndeton drops every conjunction; gradation rises step by step (doubt, suspicion, knowledge); prosopopoeia gives the wind a wish; zeugma lets "pidió" serve both clauses. Chiasmus and metonymy have no example here.

questions.stem: Complete with the right word. The punctuation mark in "it's" is el ___; the figure that addresses someone absent is el ___.
questions.explanation: El apóstrofo is the mark; el apóstrofe is the figure (Y a ti, abuela…). The two differ by their last vowel.

questions.stem: Which of these contain an oxymoron? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: "Un silencio que grita" and "una calma impaciente" join clashing words inside one phrase. "Cuanto más sé, menos sé" is a whole statement that seems to contradict itself: a paradox. "Te esperé una eternidad" is hyperbole.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of the prize ceremony.

image.alt: The prize ceremony from the lesson without labels. 1 is on the front edge of the raised platform. 2 is on the lectern. 3 is on the woman standing behind the lectern. 4 is on the three people seated at the long table on the platform. 5 is on the rows of people below the platform.

questions.explanation: The prizewinner (la galardonada) speaks from the lectern (el atril) on the raised platform (el estrado), beside the jury (el jurado), facing the audience (el público). El telón (curtain) isn't in the picture, and la peroración is part of a speech, not an object.

questions.stem: Which part of a formal speech usually wins the audience's goodwill, often with modesty or a small story?
questions.explanation: El exordio is the opening. La peroración is the closing; una semblanza is a short biographical sketch read about someone; un panegírico is a text of unqualified praise.

questions.stem: A critic writes: "La presentación del galardonado fue un panegírico." What is she most likely saying?
choices: It was a short formal welcome.
It praised him without a single reservation.
It was a biographical sketch with dates.
It closed the ceremony with a summary.
questions.explanation: Un panegírico is praise with no reservations, and a critic who uses the word is often being ironic. A short formal address is una alocución; a sketch is una semblanza; the closing of a speech is la peroración.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Literature didn't change my town; my town changed my literature.
questions.explanation: "La literatura no cambió a mi pueblo; mi pueblo cambió mi literatura" (or, with a postposed subject, "No cambió la literatura a mi pueblo; …"): the chiasmus keeps the reversed order (A B / B A). "A mi pueblo" takes the personal a because the town stands for its people; "cambiaba" is the wrong tense for a completed change.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: She lost her fear and the six o'clock bus.
questions.explanation: "Perdió el miedo y el autobús de las seis" (or "…el autobús de las seis y el miedo"): one verb, perder, serves two objects in two senses, a zeugma. "La" doesn't fit either noun.

questions.stem: Choose the best word for a review: "La intención es ___; el resultado, menos."
questions.explanation: Loable (laudable) praises an intention or effort, which is why it so often comes before a "but". "Lograda" and "magistral" praise a result, which contradicts "el resultado, menos"; "anodina" (bland) is a criticism.

questions.stem: Which adjective praises a prose without ornament, restrained and economical?
questions.explanation: Sobria means restrained. Recargada (overdone), ampulosa (bombastic) and efectista (flashy) all criticize excess.

questions.stem: What does "un viejo amigo" mean?
choices: a friend who is no longer a friend
questions.explanation: Before the noun, viejo means long-standing: a friend of many years, whatever his age. "Un amigo viejo", with the adjective after the noun, is an elderly friend.

questions.stem: Which phrase means "a true rumor"?
questions.explanation: After the noun, cierto means true: un rumor cierto. Before the noun (cierto rumor, un cierto rumor) it means "a certain rumor". "Ciertamente un rumor" is "certainly a rumor".

questions.stem: A review says: "una novela de factura impecable". What does "factura" mean here?
questions.explanation: In the language of criticism, la factura is the craftsmanship or execution of a work. Its everyday sense, the A2 word, is an invoice.

questions.stem: Complete the softened criticism: "Se ___ de menos una segunda mitad más ágil." (One misses a brisker second half.)
questions.explanation: Echar de menos is "to miss": se echa de menos (one misses) softens a criticism by stating it as an absence.

questions.stem: Which adjectives criticize an excess of ornament or effect? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Recargado (overdone), ampuloso (bombastic) and efectista (flashy) criticize excess. Sobrio (restrained) praises economy.

questions.stem: Name the hidden words on the chart of evaluative vocabulary.

image.alt: The chart of evaluative words with six hidden. 1 is on the quality scale between anodino and desigual. 2 is in the middle of the quality scale, above con altibajos. 3 is at the mastery end, after logrado. 4 is in the contención box before pulcro and depurado. 5 is in the exceso box, above ampuloso. 6 is in the esfuerzos e intenciones box, beside encomiable.

questions.explanation: On the quality scale, fallido sits near failure, desigual in the middle and magistral at mastery; sobrio praises restraint and recargado criticizes excess; loable joins encomiable as praise for an effort. "Omnisciente" and "lineal" are narrative terms from lesson 11.

questions.stem: Put these parts of a review in the order the lesson gives.
choices: a description of what the work attempts
an assessment of strengths and weaknesses, with evidence
a verdict: for whom, and why
questions.explanation: A review moves from describing to judging: the ficha first (title, author, year), then the description of what the work attempts, then the assessment with evidence, and the verdict last.

questions.stem: Which sentence concedes a strength before judging, as a balanced review does?
choices: La novela es pésima y no la recomiendo.
Si bien la trama es previsible, los diálogos están muy logrados.
questions.explanation: Si bien concedes one point (the plot is predictable) and then judges another (the dialogue). The other sentences each state a single judgment without concession.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Although the last chapter is rushed, the novel holds up.
questions.explanation: "Si bien el último capítulo se apresura, la novela se sostiene" (or "…, se sostiene la novela"). Si bien concedes with the indicative. "Sino" corrects a negative and has no place here.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: It is not a failed work, but it is an uneven one.
questions.explanation: "No es una obra fallida, pero sí desigual": after a negative, pero sí adds a second quality instead of correcting the first. "Tampoco" would deny both.

questions.stem: A narrator knows what every character thinks and tells us what will happen years later. What kind of narrator is it?
questions.explanation: Knowing every mind and the future is the mark of the omniscient narrator. A witness knows only what he saw or was told; a protagonist tells his own story; a second-person narration addresses "tú".

questions.stem: Which sentence is in free indirect style?
choices: Pensó que se iría al día siguiente.
Mañana se iría. ¿Y si nadie la extrañaba?
mañana me voy, mañana, sí, ya no aguanto
questions.explanation: Free indirect style uses the narrator's tenses (se iría, extrañaba) with the character's deixis (mañana) and a question with no "pensó". The first is direct speech, the second indirect speech, and the last an interior monologue in the present.

questions.stem: "Años más tarde, vendería la casa." In a past narration, what does this sentence do?
questions.explanation: The conditional "vendería" looks ahead from the story's time to a later moment: a prolepsis. An analepsis would go back in time.

questions.stem: A third-person narrator tells everything through a child's eyes, so we see only what she sees. The voice is third person; what is internal?
questions.explanation: Focalization is whose eyes we see through, and it can differ from the voice. Here the voice is the narrator's, but the focalization is internal, through the child.

questions.stem: Match each term to its definition.
choices: a story that contains another story
fiction that talks about its own writing
a text's dialogue with other texts
the author's own life mixed with invention
questions.explanation: A frame story contains another; metafiction talks about its own writing; intertextuality is a dialogue with other texts; an ensemble novel has many voices; autofiction mixes the author's life with invention. "A jump back in time" is an analepsis, which isn't on the list.

questions.stem: Ana thinks: «Mañana llega el camión». Rewrite it in free indirect style, inside a past narration: "Mañana ___ el camión."
questions.explanation: Free indirect style keeps mañana (the character's point in time) but uses the narrator's past tenses: the conditional "llegaría", or the imperfect "llegaba" (or "iba a llegar"), which Spanish also uses for a planned event seen from the past.

questions.stem: Which features mark free indirect style in Spanish? Select all that apply.
choices: questions and exclamations with no "pensó" or "se preguntó"
mañana and ahora used with past tenses
questions.explanation: Free indirect style uses the narrator's imperfect and conditional, keeps the character's deixis (mañana, ahora) and lets questions and exclamations stand without "pensó". Quotation marks belong to direct speech.

questions.stem: Put these techniques in order of narrative distance, from the narrator's control (farthest) to the character's mind (nearest), as the lesson's diagram shows.
questions.explanation: Summary is all narrator; indirect speech reports with "pensó que"; free indirect style blends the two voices; direct speech quotes the character; the interior monologue gives the thoughts themselves.

questions.stem: Which technique does the lesson give for Valeria Luiselli's Los ingrávidos (2011)?
choices: chapters of a single unbroken paragraph
two first-person narrators in alternating chapters
a woman writing a novel whose voice blends with her subject's
an allegory of a descent to the underworld
questions.explanation: In Los ingrávidos, a young mother writes about a Mexican poet in New York, and the voices bleed into each other: metafiction and splitting. The unbroken paragraphs describe Melchor's Temporada de huracanes; the alternating narrators, Nettel's Después del invierno; the descent, Herrera's Señales que precederán al fin del mundo.

questions.stem: What can a witness narrator (el narrador testigo) know?
choices: only what he saw or was told
questions.explanation: The witness speaks in the first person from beside the main character, so he knows only what he saw or heard about. Knowing every mind and the future belongs to the omniscient narrator.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Years later, she would sell the house.
questions.explanation: "Años más tarde vendería la casa" (often with a comma after "tarde"), or with "años más tarde" at the end or after the verb. The conditional makes it a prolepsis from a past narration. "Antes" contradicts "más tarde".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The story is not linear: it jumps between three periods.
questions.explanation: "La historia no es lineal: salta entre tres épocas." Lineal has one form for both genders, so "lineales" (plural) can't go with "la historia".

questions.stem: "Seguiremos mejorando el servicio." What does this sentence take for granted?
choices: that the service will be free
that the service has been improving
that the service is the worst in the region
that someone will lose their job
questions.explanation: Seguir + gerund presupposes that the action was already going on: the service has been improving. That is assumed, not argued.

questions.stem: "Algunos funcionarios cumplieron." A reader concludes that others didn't, although the sentence never says so. What is that conclusion called?
questions.explanation: An implicature is what a sentence suggests without saying it, inferred because the speaker could have said "todos". It is deniable, unlike a presupposition, which the sentence takes for granted.

questions.stem: "Se tomó la decisión de actualizar las tarifas." What does the construction hide?
questions.explanation: The impersonal se and the nominalization ("la decisión de actualizar") remove the agent: we are not told who decided.

questions.stem: Which phrase is the most neutral way to name the measure in the statement?
questions.explanation: "Un aumento de tarifas" (a rate increase) states what happens. "Actualización" softens it, "tarifazo" frames it as an outrage, and "reordenamiento" is a euphemism for something else.

questions.stem: Match each phrase to its meaning.
choices: to divide a debate into opposed camps
questions.explanation: Maquillar las cifras dresses up figures; edulcorar sweetens bad news; eludir una pregunta dodges it; descalificar al adversario attacks the opponent instead of the argument; polarizar divides people into opposed camps. Naming the agent is what a neutral rewrite does.

questions.stem: Complete: "Ante cada pregunta sobre el costo, el vocero respondió con ___." (evasive answers)
questions.explanation: Responder con evasivas is the set phrase for answering evasively; la evasiva is usually plural.

questions.stem: Which phrases from the statement blame or attack someone instead of informing? Select all that apply.
choices: el consumo irresponsable de algunos usuarios
ciertos actores políticos hayan preferido la desinformación
la red tiene más de cuarenta años
questions.explanation: Blaming "algunos usuarios" makes them a scapegoat, and "ciertos actores políticos hayan preferido la desinformación" disparages unnamed critics. The age of the network and the help desks are information, whatever their purpose.

questions.stem: What is the problem with "el ajuste será, en promedio, de hasta un 18 %"?
choices: It uses the wrong percentage sign.
It mixes an average with a maximum, so the figure is unclear.
It names the agent too clearly.
questions.explanation: "En promedio" gives an average; "hasta" gives a maximum. Together they leave the reader unable to say how much a typical home will pay, which is why the neutral rewrite quotes the wording instead of choosing one.

questions.stem: Order these names for the same measure from the most favorable frame to the most hostile.
questions.explanation: "Actualización tarifaria" softens the increase; "aumento de tarifas" states it; "tarifazo" frames it as an abuse.

questions.stem: A student writes "El gobierno impone su narrativa" in a formal essay. What should she know?
choices: Narrativa can only mean a novel.
The phrase is a calque that the RAE has banned.
Narrativa is always the best word for an argument.
This sense is recent and debated; relato or discurso are safer.
questions.explanation: The "framing story" sense of narrativa spread recently, often attributed to English influence, and its status is debated; relato or discurso avoid the debate. Its older sense is fiction as a genre, not only a novel, and no ban exists.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: From January on, the utility will raise the rates.
questions.explanation: "A partir de enero, el organismo aumentará las tarifas" (or "…aumentará las tarifas el organismo", or "…aumentará el organismo las tarifas"). A neutral rewrite names the agent and uses "aumentar", not the euphemism "actualizar".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: According to the utility, the network loses water.
questions.explanation: "Según el organismo, la red pierde agua" (or "…, pierde agua la red"). Según attributes the claim to its source; the indicative "pierde" reports it as the source's statement.

questions.stem: What did Lope de Vega defend in his Arte nuevo de hacer comedias (1609)?
choices: the strict classical rules of five acts
what audiences liked over what classical rules required
questions.explanation: The Arte nuevo defended, half ironically, the formula the public enjoyed: three acts, comic and tragic mixed, many meters. It was not a defense of classical rules or of prose.

questions.stem: In Golden Age theater, what is a jornada?
questions.explanation: In the comedia nueva, the three acts were called jornadas. The everyday sense (B1's jornada laboral) is a working day; a comic interlude is an entremés.

questions.stem: Who is the gracioso?
choices: the old father who guards the honor
the king who settles the conflict
questions.explanation: El gracioso is the galán's servant: hungry, cowardly and witty, the voice of common sense. The old father is el barba; the suitor is el galán.

questions.stem: In the comedia, what is la honra?
choices: a medal given by the king
public reputation, what others say about you
inner virtue known only to God
questions.explanation: La honra is reputation: that is why a rumor could be as dangerous as a crime. A decoration is la condecoración; inner virtue is not what these plots turn on.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of the corral de comedias.

image.alt: The plan of the corral from the lesson without labels. 1 is on the stage at the top. 2 is in the middle of the open yard. 3 is on the tiered benches on the left side. 4 is on the gallery at the bottom, opposite the stage. 5 is on the latticed boxes along the right wall.

questions.explanation: The stage (el escenario) is at one end; the standing public filled el patio; las gradas were tiered benches along the sides; los aposentos were latticed boxes rented by noble families; la cazuela, opposite the stage, was the women's gallery. El entremés and el auto sacramental are kinds of play, not places.

questions.stem: Match each work to its author.
questions.explanation: Calderón wrote La vida es sueño and the auto sacramental El gran teatro del mundo; Ruiz de Alarcón, La verdad sospechosa; Lope, the Arte nuevo. Sor Juana belongs to the period but wrote none of these.

questions.stem: Where was Juan Ruiz de Alarcón born?
choices: in New Spain, in Taxco or Mexico City
questions.explanation: He was born in New Spain around 1581; sources differ between Taxco and Mexico City. He studied in Mexico and Salamanca and died in Madrid in 1639.
