questions.stem: Which are features of the comedia nueva? Select all that apply.
choices: five acts and strict classical unities
questions.explanation: The comedia nueva had three jornadas, mixed tragic and comic, and used many meters. Five acts and the classical unities are what it abandoned.

questions.stem: Complete: a short comic one-act piece performed between the acts of a comedia is el ___.
questions.explanation: El entremés (plural los entremeses): the comic interlude, often better loved than the play.

questions.stem: What is an auto sacramental?
choices: a one-act religious allegory performed for Corpus Christi
a prologue spoken before a play
questions.explanation: The auto sacramental is a one-act allegory on a religious theme, with abstract figures as characters, performed for Corpus Christi; Calderón was its master. The interlude is the entremés; the prologue, the loa.

questions.stem: In the lesson's original scene, how does the audience learn that the glove is Tomillo's?
choices: Clara says so to her brother.
Tomillo says it in an aside.
questions.explanation: Tomillo admits it in an aparte, an aside heard only by the audience. Nobody on stage knows, which drives the enredo.

questions.stem: Which questions are central to La vida es sueño?
choices: free will against fate, and disillusionment with appearances
the price of bread in Madrid
questions.explanation: A prince told that he is fated to be a tyrant chooses to act well: free will against fate. Disillusionment (el desengaño), seeing that worldly glory is appearance, is the Baroque idea beside it.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Honor is reputation, not virtue.
questions.explanation: "La honra es la reputación, no la virtud." The comma sets off the denied element after the affirmed one. "Sino" would need a negative before it (no es la virtud, sino la reputación).

questions.stem: Which Golden Age play did Pierre Corneille adapt as Le Menteur?
questions.explanation: Le Menteur (1644) adapts Ruiz de Alarcón's La verdad sospechosa, the comedy of a compulsive liar trapped by his lies.

questions.stem: How does modernismo relate to English "modernism"?
choices: They are the same movement in two languages.
Modernismo is a late-19th-century Hispanic movement; English modernism is later and closer to the vanguardias.
Modernismo is a 20th-century architecture style only.
English modernism came first and modernismo copied it.
questions.explanation: Modernismo (about 1880–1915) is earlier and different; English modernism (Joyce, Eliot) corresponds more to the Spanish vanguardias. Call it modernismo in English.

questions.stem: What is a Spanish alexandrine?
choices: a line of fourteen syllables in two halves of seven
a line of twelve syllables, as in French counting
a line with no fixed meter
questions.explanation: The Spanish alexandrine has fourteen syllables split 7 + 7; French counts its alexandrine as twelve because the languages count line endings differently. A line with no fixed meter is free verse; abba quatrains are redondillas.

questions.stem: Who founded the Revista Azul in Mexico City in 1894?
choices: Manuel Gutiérrez Nájera and Carlos Díaz Dufoo
questions.explanation: Gutiérrez Nájera, El Duque Job, founded it with Carlos Díaz Dufoo; it outlived him by more than a year. Nervo is linked to the later Revista Moderna.

questions.stem: Match each book to its author.
questions.explanation: Darío wrote Azul… (1888) and Prosas profanas (1896); Martí, Versos sencillos (1891); Gutiérrez Nájera, Cuentos frágiles (1883). Nervo wrote none of these.

questions.stem: Put these in chronological order, earliest first.
choices: Darío, Cantos de vida y esperanza
questions.explanation: Ismaelillo 1882, Azul… 1888, the Revista Azul 1894, Prosas profanas 1896, Cantos de vida y esperanza 1905.

questions.stem: Which are marks of modernismo? Select all that apply.
choices: the swan as an emblem of beauty
synesthesia: one sense described through another
free verse as its standard form
questions.explanation: The swan, exoticism and synesthesia are its marks. Free verse was a step it pointed toward, not its standard form: its signature line was the alexandrine.

questions.stem: "Un azul que suena a campana lejana" describes a color as a sound. This figure of mixed senses is la ___.
questions.explanation: La sinestesia (synesthesia) describes one sense in terms of another; the modernistas loved it.

questions.stem: How does the lesson describe Martí's Versos sencillos?
choices: rare and learned words chosen for color
short eight-syllable lines in plain words
questions.explanation: Versos sencillos uses short eight-syllable lines in quatrains and everyday words, in the service of sincerity. Alexandrines, mythology and rare words describe Darío's Prosas profanas.

questions.stem: Critics accused the modernistas of preciosismo. What were they criticizing?
choices: an excess of ornament and precious objects
questions.explanation: Preciosismo (preciosity) is an ornate style overloaded with jewels, ivory and rare words, the danger of a movement that compared its craft to goldsmithing.

questions.stem: Why does 1898 matter in the history of modernismo?
choices: It is the year the Revista Azul was founded.
Spain lost its last American colonies, and Darío's later poetry turned graver and more American.
questions.explanation: In 1898 Spain lost its last American colonies and the United States rose as the continent's power; Darío's Cantos de vida y esperanza (1905) reflects that shift. The Revista Azul is from 1894, Ismaelillo from 1882, and Darío died in 1916.

questions.stem: What is the main claim of the lesson's original essay?
choices: Modernismo's form was also a stance, and its influence ran from Spanish America to Spain.
Modernismo was only decoration with no ideas.
Modernismo began in Madrid and spread to the colonies.
Martí and Darío had nothing in common.
questions.explanation: The essay argues that beauty of form was a way of thinking and a rebellion, and that for once the renewal traveled from the former colonies to Madrid. It concedes the charge of preciosity but rejects reducing the movement to it.

questions.stem: What is el verso libre?
choices: a line of exactly eight syllables
a line that must rhyme abba
verse with no fixed meter or rhyme
prose printed as poetry by mistake
questions.explanation: Free verse has no fixed meter or rhyme. The modernistas pointed toward it by mixing line lengths; the avant-gardes made it common.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Modernismo renewed poetry in Spanish.
questions.explanation: "El modernismo renovó la poesía en español" (or, with the verb first, "Renovó el modernismo la poesía en español" or "Renovó la poesía en español el modernismo"). "La prosa" would change the meaning.

questions.stem: What does the lesson say about Amado Nervo?
choices: He was born in Nicaragua and founded the Revista Azul.
He was a Mexican poet and diplomat who moved from refined images to a barer, more spiritual poetry.
He died fighting for Cuba's independence.
questions.explanation: Nervo (Tepic, 1870–1919) was a poet and diplomat linked to the Revista Moderna, whose late poetry became plainer and more spiritual. Martí died fighting for Cuba; Darío, born in Nicaragua, wrote Azul…; Gutiérrez Nájera co-founded the Revista Azul.

questions.stem: In the lesson's ruling, what happened to the case against the Presidente Municipal?
choices: It was dismissed, because he denied giving the order and the complainant offered no proof otherwise.
The amparo was granted against him, because he signed the closure order.
The amparo was denied, because the court found his order lawful.
He was ordered to issue a new, properly reasoned closure order.
questions.explanation: Considerando SEGUNDO and resolutivo PRIMERO: he denied the act (negó la existencia del acto reclamado) and nothing proved otherwise, so "se sobresee en el juicio respecto de dicha autoridad". A dismissal decides nothing about the merits; the court never said he signed the order or that it was lawful, and the new-order effect concerns the Director de Reglamentos.

questions.stem: What does the ruling leave the Director de Reglamentos free to do?
choices: Close the bakery at once, since the stay has ended.
Issue a new order, if he sees fit, that states its legal grounds and reasons.
Nothing: the municipality may never inspect the bakery again.
Only appeal directly to the Supreme Court.
questions.explanation: Considerando QUINTO grants the amparo "para el efecto de que la autoridad deje sin efectos la orden y, si lo estima procedente, emita una nueva, debidamente fundada y motivada", and says the authority keeps its power (potestad) to inspect businesses. Closing the bakery at once or never inspecting it again both change what the ruling says.

questions.stem: Complete the formula that leads into the operative points of a Mexican ruling: Por lo expuesto y ___, se resuelve.
questions.explanation: "Por lo expuesto y fundado, se resuelve" (for the reasons and on the grounds stated, it is resolved). "Expuesto" refers to the reasons set out, "fundado" to the legal grounds, the same pair as in "fundar y motivar".

questions.stem: Match each term of an amparo to what it names.
choices: the person who files the amparo
the authority whose act is challenged
a party with an interest in the act standing
the court that hears an appeal
questions.explanation: These are the Ley de Amparo's terms (article 5 names the parties: quejoso, autoridad responsable, tercero interesado and the Ministerio Público Federal). The act itself is el acto reclamado. An appeal by review goes to a tribunal colegiado, which isn't a party.

questions.stem: Which statements about "la jurisprudencia" in Mexican legal Spanish are true? Select all that apply.
choices: It means case law that binds other courts.
It is the usual Spanish word for legal philosophy.
A published tesis does not always bind as jurisprudencia.
It is a synonym of "la sentencia".
questions.explanation: Jurisprudencia is binding case law, a false friend of English "jurisprudence" (legal theory, usually). A tesis is a published criterion and binds only under the Ley de Amparo's conditions. "La sentencia" is a single ruling, not a body of case law.

questions.stem: Label the numbered parts of this ruling's layout.

image.alt: The layout of a ruling without its headings: a heading box at the top, then three shaded blocks of text lines one below the other, and two signature lines at the bottom. Four numbered markers sit on the heading box and the three blocks.

questions.explanation: A traditional Mexican ruling opens with a heading (court, case number, parties), then the resultandos (what happened), the considerandos (the reasons) and the puntos resolutivos (the decision). Cláusulas and comparecencia are parts of a notarial deed (lesson 16h2), not of a ruling.

questions.stem: What does "Se sobresee en el juicio" mean?
choices: A higher court will oversee the case.
The case is dismissed without a decision on its merits.
The challenged act is suspended for now.
questions.explanation: Sobreseer is to dismiss a case without deciding its merits, for example because the challenged act doesn't exist. Despite its look, it has nothing to do with English "oversee". Stopping the act for now is la suspensión.

questions.stem: The lawyer's letter must render "La Justicia de la Unión ampara y protege a Lucía Ramírez Ocampo contra el acto del Director de Reglamentos" for the client. Which sentence does it best?
choices: La Justicia de la Unión la ampara y la protege.
La jueza declaró que su panadería nunca podrá ser clausurada.
El juzgado sobreseyó el juicio a su favor.
La jueza le dio la razón frente al director de Reglamentos: su orden queda sin efecto.
questions.explanation: The plain version says who won and what follows, in the client's words. Repeating the formula explains nothing; "nunca podrá ser clausurada" adds a promise the ruling doesn't make (it allows a new, reasoned order); and a sobreseimiento is the opposite of winning on the merits.

questions.stem: The authority argues that "el juicio es improcedente". What is it claiming?
choices: That the law doesn't allow this action, so the court shouldn't decide it.
That the case has already been decided.
That the order was lawful on its merits.
questions.explanation: Improcedente means inadmissible: the action doesn't fit what the law allows. It is about admissibility, not behavior (English "improper"), and not about whether the order was right on its merits. In the ruling the court rejects the argument ("No le asiste la razón").

questions.stem: A Mexican news item mentions "la ministra Gómez" in a story about the Supreme Court. Who is she?
choices: A justice of the Suprema Corte de Justicia de la Nación.
A cabinet minister in the federal government.
A Protestant minister who testified in a case.
The head of the public prosecutor's office.
questions.explanation: In Mexico the members of the Supreme Court are ministros and ministras. A government minister is a secretario or secretaria de Estado in Mexico, and the prosecution is el ministerio público or la fiscalía.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The court granted the stay.
questions.explanation: Subject, verb, object: "El juzgado concedió la suspensión." Spanish also allows the verb first with the subject after it ("Concedió la suspensión el juzgado", "Concedió el juzgado la suspensión"), as in news and legal prose. Sobreseer would mean dismissing the case, not granting the stay.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The order doesn't state its legal grounds or its reasons.
questions.explanation: "Fundada y motivada" is the participle form of the formula fundar y motivar, agreeing with la orden (feminine). With no, the pair becomes "no está fundada ni motivada". The subject can also come last: "No está fundada ni motivada la orden." The masculine "fundado" doesn't agree with la orden.

questions.stem: Put the steps of an indirect amparo in order, as the lesson's simplified chart shows them.
choices: La persona afectada presenta la demanda de amparo.
La autoridad responsable rinde su informe.
questions.explanation: The claim is filed, then admitted (and a stay may be granted), the responsible authority reports, the constitutional hearing is held, and the ruling grants, denies or dismisses. Either side can then seek review before a tribunal colegiado.

questions.stem: In the progress note, what does "Niega fiebre" record?
choices: The doctor ruled out fever with a test.
The patient refuses treatment for fever.
The patient says she hasn't had a fever.
The patient denies being told she had a fever.
questions.explanation: In clinical notes negar reports what the patient says she doesn't have: "Niega fiebre, disnea y otra sintomatología respiratoria" means she reports none of them. Ruling something out after tests is descartar.

questions.stem: The note says: "Tos seca, probablemente secundaria a efecto adverso del antihipertensivo." Which sentence for the patient keeps the note's meaning?
choices: La tos probablemente se debe al medicamento para la presión.
La tos se debe al medicamento para la presión.
El medicamento le provocó la tos, sin ninguna duda.
La tos no tiene nada que ver con el medicamento.
questions.explanation: The note hedges with "probablemente", so the letter keeps "probablemente". Dropping it, or adding "sin ninguna duda", claims more than the doctor wrote; the last option contradicts the note.

questions.stem: Complete the note with the phrase that means "still to be ruled out": Lesión pigmentada de etiología a determinar; ___ lesión maligna.
questions.explanation: "A descartar" (also "por descartar", heard in several countries) marks a diagnosis still to be ruled out. It is a hedge: the doctor hasn't found a malignant lesion, only hasn't excluded one yet.

questions.stem: Match each Greek or Latin piece to its meaning.
questions.explanation: Gastritis is inflammation of the stomach, neuralgia nerve pain, anemia a condition of the blood, hipoglucemia low blood sugar. Removal is -ectomía.

questions.stem: Which of these belong in the anamnesis? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: The anamnesis is the history the patient tells: family history (antecedentes heredofamiliares) and the present illness (padecimiento actual), among others. A blood-pressure reading belongs to the exploración física, and the differential diagnosis to the diagnosis section.

questions.stem: Each numbered box of this record shows a line from Rosalba's note. Name its section.

image.alt: A clinical record without its headings. Six boxes show sample lines: Rosalba Ortega Ruiz, femenina de 58 años; Refiere tos seca de seis semanas de evolución; TA 148/92 mmHg, FC 78 lpm, IMC 28.9; Hemograma normal, glucosa en ayuno 132 mg/dL; Tos probablemente secundaria a efecto adverso; Interconsulta a Dermatología. A smaller box gives a date, a time and the word Evoluciona. Five numbered markers sit on the first, second, third and fifth boxes and on the small box.

questions.explanation: Name and age identify the patient; "refiere" introduces what she reports (the history); vital signs and measurements are the physical examination; "probablemente secundaria a" is a hedged diagnosis; a dated later entry is a progress note. The unmarked boxes are the studies and the plan.

questions.stem: What does Spain usually call the document Mexico calls "el expediente clínico"?
questions.explanation: Spain says la historia clínica; Mexico's term, set by NOM-004-SSA3-2012, is el expediente clínico (where historia clínica names the first full history). "El récord médico" is a calque from English; la receta is a prescription.

questions.stem: Which statement about "la metástasis" is correct?
choices: It is stressed on the last syllable.
It means the same as "la biopsia".
questions.explanation: Like la anamnesis and la epicrisis, it keeps the same form in the plural; it is stressed me-TAS-ta-sis. It is the spread of a malignant tumor, not a benign one, and a biopsy is the sample taken to tell them apart.

questions.stem: According to the WHO fact sheet the lesson cites (dated September 25, 2025), how is hypertension defined?
choices: One reading of 120/80 mmHg or more.
A reading of 140/90 mmHg or more on any single day.
Readings of 140/90 mmHg or more measured on two different days.
questions.explanation: The fact sheet defines it as 140/90 mmHg or more on two different days. Often there are no symptoms at all, which is why screening (el tamizaje) matters. This is a reading question about a source, not health advice.

questions.stem: Which sentence fits a letter to the patient?
choices: Paciente con hipertensión arterial sistémica en descontrol.
Su presión sigue más alta de lo que buscamos.
Femenina de 58 años con cifras tensionales elevadas.
questions.explanation: The letter uses usted, everyday words and full sentences. The other three are in the telegraphic, third-person style of the note, written for colleagues.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The physical examination showed nothing abnormal.
questions.explanation: "La exploración física no mostró alteraciones" is the usual phrasing in a note. The subject may also follow: "No mostró alteraciones la exploración física", "No mostró la exploración física alteraciones." "Ninguna" would need a singular noun (ninguna alteración).

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: She has had diabetes for eight years.
questions.explanation: Padecer (to suffer from) in the present with "desde hace" describes a condition that began eight years ago and continues. The time phrase can also open the sentence: "Desde hace ocho años padece diabetes." The preterite "padeció" would describe a finished illness and doesn't combine with "desde hace".

questions.stem: Put the sections of a clinical history in the order the lesson's table gives them.
questions.explanation: Identification first; then the history the patient tells; then what the doctor finds on examination and in tests; then the conclusion and the plan. Progress notes are added at later visits.

questions.stem: In the lesson's statement, how was the decision taken?
choices: Unanimously, to cut the rate by 25 basis points.
By a majority, to hold the rate at 7.25%; two members voted for a cut.
By a majority, to raise the rate; two members voted to hold it.
Unanimously, to hold the rate at 7.25%.
questions.explanation: "La Junta de Gobierno decidió, por mayoría, mantener la tasa objetivo en 7.25 %. Dos miembros votaron por reducirla en 25 puntos base." Por mayoría means not unanimous, and the dissent was for a cut.

questions.stem: Which news sentence keeps the strength of "Hacia delante, la Junta evaluará la pertinencia de reanudar los recortes"?
choices: El banco evaluará si reanuda los recortes.
El banco aseguró que habrá recortes en 2027.
questions.explanation: "Evaluará la pertinencia de" means it will assess whether cutting is appropriate: no commitment. "Reanudará" and "aseguró" turn the hedge into a promise, and "descartó" reverses it.

questions.stem: A rise of half a percentage point equals ___ basis points. (Give the number.)
questions.explanation: One percentage point is 100 basis points (puntos base), so 0.5 points is 50, and 25 basis points is a quarter point.

questions.stem: Match each term to its meaning.
choices: the ability to pay short-term debts
the use of debt to finance the business
questions.explanation: Assets (el activo) equal liabilities (el pasivo) plus equity (el capital contable, also el patrimonio). Liquidity is short-term; the use of debt is el apalancamiento.

questions.stem: Which phrases are hedges that don't commit the bank? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Se prevé que (it is expected), podría (could) and no se descarta (isn't ruled out) all limit the claim. "La Junta decidió mantener" reports a decision already taken.

questions.stem: Name the three numbered parts of this balance sheet.

image.alt: A balance sheet for a fictional company without its column headings. The left column lists cash, accounts receivable, inventories, machinery and equipment, and real estate, totaling 400. The upper right box lists suppliers, short-term loans and bonds issued, totaling 220. The lower right box lists share capital and retained earnings, totaling 180. Numbered markers sit at the top of each of the three boxes.

questions.explanation: Cash, receivables, inventories, machinery and buildings are what the company owns: el activo. Suppliers, loans and bonds issued are what it owes: el pasivo. Share capital and retained earnings belong to the owners: el capital contable. Check: 220 + 180 = 400.

questions.stem: A Mexican report says the debt reached "un billón de pesos". How much is that?
questions.explanation: Spanish un billón is a million millions, English trillion. English "billion" is mil millones (in Spanish, also un millardo, rarely used).

questions.stem: On the lesson's scale, which phrase sends the most restrictive (hawkish) signal?
choices: Prevé continuar con el ciclo de recortes.
Evaluará la pertinencia de reanudar los recortes.
Mantendrá la tasa sin cambios por un periodo prolongado.
questions.explanation: Announcing that a rate rise will be necessary is the clearest hawkish signal. Continuing or considering cuts is dovish, and holding for a long time sits in between (its reading depends on the cycle, as the lesson notes).

questions.stem: Which forms can fill the blank? Se prevé que la inflación ___ a su meta en el segundo semestre de 2027. Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: After "se prevé que" both the present subjunctive (converja) and the future (convergerá) occur in central-bank and press Spanish. The preterite contradicts a forecast about 2027, and the infinitive can't follow "que" here.

questions.stem: "La moneda nacional registró una depreciación de 2 % frente al dólar." What happened?
choices: The currency gained 2% against the dollar.
The dollar lost 2% of its value worldwide.
The currency lost value against the dollar.
questions.explanation: Depreciación is a loss of value; its opposite is apreciación. The statement adds that it could push up import prices.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The board decided to hold the target rate.
questions.explanation: "La Junta decidió mantener la tasa objetivo." Formal Spanish may also put the verb first: "Decidió la Junta mantener la tasa objetivo", "Decidió mantener la tasa objetivo la Junta." Reducir would mean cutting, not holding.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Inflation expectations remain above the target.
questions.explanation: The plural subject takes "se mantienen". The subject can also follow the verb or the verb phrase ("Se mantienen las expectativas de inflación por encima de la meta", "Se mantienen por encima de la meta las expectativas de inflación"), and the prepositional phrase can open the sentence ("Por encima de la meta se mantienen las expectativas de inflación"). The singular "se mantiene" doesn't agree.

questions.stem: Put the parts of a monetary-policy statement in the order the lesson gives them.
questions.explanation: The decision comes first, so readers learn it at once; then the reasons, from outside in (world, domestic economy, inflation); then the weighing of risks; and the guidance closes the statement.

questions.stem: In a patent claim, what does "que comprende" mean?
questions.explanation: "Comprende" in claims is "comprises": the object includes at least the listed parts and may have others. It doesn't mean understanding or explaining, and it doesn't limit the object to those parts.

questions.stem: Which of these is a dependent claim?
choices: 1. Una válvula ahorradora de agua que comprende una carcasa (10)…
2. La válvula de conformidad con la reivindicación 1, caracterizada porque…
Válvula ahorradora de agua para grifería doméstica
En el estado de la técnica se conocen reductores de caudal…
questions.explanation: A dependent claim refers back to an earlier one ("de conformidad con la reivindicación 1") and narrows it. Claim 1 is independent; the title and the prior-art paragraph aren't claims at all.

questions.stem: Complete the claim: …y un obturador (16) dispuesto entre ambas, caracterizada ___ comprende además un resorte (18).
questions.explanation: The fixed phrase is "caracterizado porque" (one word, porque), agreeing with the object: caracterizada for la válvula. "Por que" in two words would be a different construction.

questions.stem: Match each right to what it protects.
choices: an invention that is new, inventive and industrially applicable
an object whose new form makes it work better
a sign that identifies goods or services
confidential information that gives a competitive edge
an original literary or artistic work
questions.explanation: These are the industrial-property rights the IMPI administers. Literary and artistic works fall under copyright (los derechos de autor), a separate system.

questions.stem: Which sentences could a faithful lay explanation of the lesson's patent application include? Select all that apply.
choices: Según las pruebas del solicitante, deja pasar como máximo unos seis litros por minuto.
Es la mejor válvula del mercado.
Todavía no es una patente: el IMPI debe revisarla.
Ahorra 300 pesos al mes en el recibo del agua.
questions.explanation: The first keeps the figure with its source; the third keeps the application's limit. "La mejor del mercado" is the writer's praise, and the savings figure appears nowhere in the source: both add to it.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of the valve.

image.alt: The patent drawing of the valve without reference numbers or legend. A horizontal body with pipes at both ends and flow arrows; inside it a plunger; above it a housing with a coiled spring; on top a toothed gear and, above that, a knob. Five numbered markers sit on the body, the spring, the gear, the knob and the plunger.

questions.explanation: In the application: carcasa (10), obturador (16), resorte (18), engranaje (20), perilla de ajuste (22). El plano is the drawing itself and la tolerancia a permitted variation, not parts.

questions.stem: What is a Mexican NOM (norma oficial mexicana)?
choices: A patent granted by the IMPI.
questions.explanation: Under the Ley de Infraestructura de la Calidad (2020), NOMs are mandatory technical regulations; voluntary standards are NMX. Patents are a separate system.

questions.stem: How would a test report from Spain usually write the Mexican report's "6.0 L/min ± 0.2"?
questions.explanation: Spain writes the decimal comma, Mexico the decimal point; the RAE accepts both, but one text keeps one convention. Mixing them, or dropping the decimals, changes or garbles the figures.

questions.stem: "El titular tiene el derecho exclusivo de explotación de la patente." What is "la explotación" here?
choices: the public disclosure of the invention
the commercial use of the invention
questions.explanation: In patents (and mines or farms) explotación is neutral: commercial use or operation. The abuse sense applies to people. Expiry is caducar / la caducidad.

questions.stem: The application says: "En el estado de la técnica se conocen reductores de caudal de disco perforado." What does this sentence do?
choices: It claims that the perforated disc is the new invention.
It names devices that already existed before the application.
It describes the latest technology on the market as superior.
It reports the results of the durability test.
questions.explanation: El estado de la técnica is prior art: what was public before filing. The application names existing reducers to show what problem the invention solves, not to claim them or praise them.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The flow was measured at 200 kPa.
questions.explanation: A report uses the passive with se: "Se midió el caudal a 200 kPa." The subject can open the sentence ("El caudal se midió a 200 kPa"), and the measurement condition can come first or between ("A 200 kPa se midió el caudal", "Se midió a 200 kPa el caudal"). "Se midieron" doesn't agree with the singular caudal.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The patent lapsed because the annual fees weren't paid.
questions.explanation: "La patente caducó porque no se pagaron las anualidades." The subjects can also follow their verbs or precede them: "Caducó la patente…", "…porque las anualidades no se pagaron". A porque clause placed first would need a comma after it, which no tile gives, and an explanatory porque normally follows the main clause (to front the cause, Spanish prefers como: "Como no se pagaron las anualidades, la patente caducó"). "Caducaron" doesn't agree with la patente.

questions.stem: Put the pieces of this independent claim in order.
choices: Una válvula ahorradora de agua para grifería doméstica,
que comprende una carcasa (10) provista de una entrada (12) y una salida (14),
y un obturador (16) dispuesto entre ambas,
caracterizada porque comprende además un resorte (18).
questions.explanation: Preamble (the object), transition "que comprende", the elements, then the characterizing part introduced by "caracterizada porque". "Ambas" needs the entrada and salida already named.

questions.stem: What is Spain's usual word for the leaflet Mexico calls "el instructivo"?
questions.explanation: Spain says el prospecto (lee el prospecto). La receta is a prescription; la etiqueta is the label on the box.

questions.stem: What does "Consérvese a no más de 30 °C" on a Mexican box mean?
choices: Keep it at no more than 30 °C.
It was kept at 30 °C at the factory.
It can be kept at any temperature up to 30 days.
questions.explanation: Impersonal se + subjunctive (consérvese) gives a fixed instruction: "should be kept", "keep". It isn't a past tense or a description of how it was stored.

questions.stem: A neighbor asks, "¿Lo puedo tomar si estoy dando pecho?" Section 4 says: "si está amamantando, consulte a su médico antes de tomar este medicamento." Which reply relays it accurately?
choices: No, está prohibido durante la lactancia.
El instructivo dice que consulte a su médico antes de tomarlo.
questions.explanation: The leaflet neither forbids nor allows it: it sends her to her doctor first. "Está prohibido" upgrades a check-first warning to an absolute one; "no hay problema" and "la mitad" add claims the leaflet doesn't make.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses "la posología" correctly?
choices: La posología de este comprimido es de 7 mg.
La posología es de un comprimido al día durante una semana.
Se tomó una posología por error.
La posología del medicamento caduca en 2027.
questions.explanation: Posología is the whole dosage plan: amount, frequency and duration. One amount (7 mg) is the dose (la dosis), you take a dose, not a posología, and expiry belongs to the medicine.

questions.stem: Complete the legend found on Mexican medicine boxes: No se deje al ___ de los niños.
questions.explanation: "No se deje al alcance de los niños" (keep out of children's reach) uses impersonal se + subjunctive, like consérvese.

questions.stem: Match each section of a leaflet to what it says.
choices: who must not take the medicine
how much to take and how often
the side effects it may cause
its effects together with other medicines or food
questions.explanation: These are four of the fixed sections. The manufacturing date isn't a leaflet section; the box shows the lot and expiry date.

questions.stem: In the invented leaflet, which ingredients are excipients? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Section 2 lists alvorastina as the active ingredient (principio activo) and lactose, cellulose and magnesium stearate as excipients. The leaflet warns about the lactose because excipients matter for intolerances.

questions.stem: Each numbered part of this leaflet shows a sample line. Name its section.

image.alt: The invented leaflet without its section headings. Eight boxes in two columns show sample lines: Cada comprimido contiene 7 mg de alvorastina; Alivia los síntomas de la rinitis alérgica; No tome este medicamento si es alérgico a…; Puede causar somnolencia: no maneje; Frecuentes: dolor de cabeza, boca seca; Los tranquilizantes aumentan la somnolencia; Un comprimido al día, con o sin alimentos; Si toma más de lo indicado, acuda a urgencias. A band at the bottom with a warning triangle reads No se deje al alcance de los niños and Reporte las reacciones adversas. Five numbered markers sit on the first and third boxes of the left column, the second and third boxes of the right column, and the bottom band.

questions.explanation: What each tablet contains is the formula; "no tome… si" is a contraindication; another medicine that adds drowsiness is an interaction; "un comprimido al día" is the dosage; the fixed warnings at the bottom are the legends.

questions.stem: In a leaflet from Spain, side effects listed as "poco frecuentes" may affect…
questions.explanation: The EU template's bands: muy frecuentes (more than 1 in 10), frecuentes (up to 1 in 10), poco frecuentes (up to 1 in 100), raras (up to 1 in 1,000), muy raras (up to 1 in 10,000).

questions.stem: A relative forgot yesterday's tablet. Which summary of section 6 is accurate?
choices: Tómela en cuanto se acuerde, salvo que ya casi sea hora de la siguiente; nunca tome dos juntas.
questions.explanation: Section 6: take it as soon as you remember unless the next dose is near, in which case skip it, and never take a double dose. Always skipping drops half the rule; urgencias is for an overdose (section 7).

questions.stem: "Este medicamento está contraindicado en menores de 12 años." What does it mean?
choices: It hasn't been tested in children, so the dose is unknown.
Children may take it with a doctor's note.
It works less well in children.
It must not be given to children under 12.
questions.explanation: Contraindicado means it must not be used in that case. "No está indicado" would only mean it isn't meant for that use; the leaflet's section 3 also says "No se administre a menores de 12 años".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Swallow the tablet whole.
questions.explanation: The usted imperative trague (from tragar) gives the instruction; "entero" agrees with el comprimido and can go before or after it: "Trague entero el comprimido." "Mastique" (chew) is what the leaflet forbids.

questions.stem: Which of these warnings is the strongest?
choices: Evite las bebidas alcohólicas durante el tratamiento.
Consulte a su médico antes de tomarlo.
No tome este medicamento si es alérgico a la alvorastina.
Si tiene alguna duda, consulte a su médico.
questions.explanation: "No tome… si" is an absolute prohibition (a contraindication). "Evite" is a strong recommendation, and "consulte a su médico" sends the reader to check first.

questions.stem: How does a Mexican notario público differ from a US notary public?
choices: There is no difference: both only witness signatures.
The Mexican notario is a lawyer appointed after an exam and holds la fe pública.
The US notary public must be a lawyer; the Mexican notario need not be.
The Mexican notario only works in courts.
questions.explanation: Mexico follows the Latin notariate: the notario is a law graduate, appointed by the state government after a demanding exam, who certifies acts with fe pública and keeps them in the protocol. A US notary public generally witnesses signatures and isn't a lawyer.

questions.stem: Who speaks in "ANTE MÍ, licenciada Elena Sáenz Robles…"?
questions.explanation: Deeds are written in the notary's voice: ante mí (before me), doy fe (I attest). The parties are named after "COMPARECEN".

questions.stem: Under the deed, who may live in the house on Hidalgo street, and until when?
choices: Valeria, from the day of the deed.
Nobody, until the deed is registered.
Valeria and her brother, in equal shares.
Her parents, for as long as either of them lives.
questions.explanation: Clause SEGUNDA reserves a life usufruct (usufructo vitalicio) to the donors: they may live in it, rent it and keep the income until the second of them dies. Valeria owns it now, but only the bare ownership.

questions.stem: What is "la nuda propiedad"?
choices: ownership of land with no building
ownership without the right to use the property or enjoy its income
a property owned jointly by siblings
questions.explanation: Bare ownership: the owner holds the title while someone else has the usufruct. When the usufruct ends, it becomes full ownership (plena propiedad). A property with no charges is "libre de todo gravamen".

questions.stem: Complete the Mexican legal formula: Declaran los donantes, bajo protesta de decir ___, que el inmueble se encuentra libre de todo gravamen.
questions.explanation: "Bajo protesta de decir verdad" (under a formal promise to tell the truth) is a fixed Mexican legal formula: recognize it, use it only in legal documents.

questions.stem: Match each person in a will to their role.
choices: inherits all or a share of the estate
certifies the will as a public official
questions.explanation: In Joaquín's will he is the testator, his children are the heirs, Sofía is a legatee (the piano), and Valeria is the executor. Certifying is the notary's job.

questions.stem: In the gift deed, who are the otorgantes? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: The donors give and the donee accepts: all three grant the act and sign it, so all are otorgantes (and comparecientes). The notary authorizes the deed but isn't a party.

questions.stem: Each numbered block of this deed shows a sample line. Name the part.

image.alt: A public deed layout without its part names. Under the heading Escritura número 18,452, libro 612, five blocks show sample lines: Querétaro, a 14 de octubre de 2026, ANTE MÍ…; COMPARECEN: los donantes y la donataria; I. … II. …; PRIMERA. … SEGUNDA. … TERCERA. …; YO, LA NOTARIA, DOY FE: …. Below them are signature lines and a round seal. Numbered markers sit on the five blocks.

questions.explanation: Place, date and the notary open the deed (proemio); the parties appear (comparecencia); the background is numbered in Roman numerals (antecedentes); the agreement in ordinal words (cláusulas); the notary certifies (doy fe). Resultandos and considerandos belong to court rulings (lesson 13).

questions.stem: Under Joaquín's will, what is Sofía's position?
choices: She is a third heir, with an equal share.
She is a legatee: she receives the piano.
She inherits the house on Hidalgo street.
questions.explanation: Clause SEGUNDA leaves her one specific item, the piano (un legado), so she is a legataria. The heirs are Valeria and Andrés; the substitute executor is Andrés; the house was already given to Valeria by the deed.

questions.stem: Explaining the will to Andrés, which closing sentence respects the mediator's limits?
choices: La casa no cuenta en el reparto, así que no te preocupes.
La donación es ilegal y la puedes anular.
Valeria tendrá que darte la mitad de la casa.
Cómo cuenta eso en el reparto es una pregunta para el notario, no para mí.
questions.explanation: The documents don't settle how the earlier gift affects the division, so the mediator points to the question and sends it to a professional. The other three answer a legal question the documents don't answer.

questions.stem: What does "Murió intestado" mean?
choices: He died without a valid will.
He died before signing a deed.
questions.explanation: Intestado: without a will. The law then decides who inherits, through la sucesión intestamentaria.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The contract was formalized in a public deed.
questions.explanation: "El contrato se formalizó en escritura pública": a passive with se. The verb may come first, with the subject at the end or right after it: "Se formalizó en escritura pública el contrato", "Se formalizó el contrato en escritura pública". The prepositional phrase can also open it: "En escritura pública se formalizó el contrato". "Se formalizaron" doesn't agree with el contrato.

questions.stem: Complete: Valeria es ___ albacea de su padre.
questions.explanation: Albacea has one form for both genders, and the article shows the gender: el albacea for a man, la albacea for a woman.

questions.stem: What does it mean to call Spanish a pluricentric language?
choices: It has several centers of prestige, and each country's educated speakers set a standard for that country.
Madrid sets the standard, and the other countries follow it with regional variations.
It has no standard at all: every speaker's usage is equally correct in every situation.
The academies impose one grammar and one vocabulary on all twenty-odd countries.
questions.explanation: Pluricentric means several centers: each country has its own norma culta (educated norm), and Mexico's is as much a standard as Spain's. That doesn't mean anything goes: each standard is the usage of educated speakers in formal speech and writing. The academies (ASALE) share one spelling but describe each country's usage instead of imposing Madrid's.

questions.stem: In the sentence "Patio y plaza son hispanismos del inglés", what is a hispanismo?
choices: a person of Hispanic origin living in an English-speaking country
a Latin American word that Spain doesn't use
a word that only educated speakers use
a Spanish word borrowed by another language
questions.explanation: El hispanismo is a Spanish loanword in another language, like English patio, plaza and canyon (it also names the study of Hispanic cultures). It isn't a Hispanic person, and a Latin American word is an americanismo.

questions.stem: You are adapting a Mexican notice for readers in all Spanish-speaking countries. Which changes fit the lesson's method? Select all that apply.
choices: Replace "ni modo" with a general expression such as "no te preocupes".
Write "250 pesos mexicanos (MXN)" instead of "250 pesos".
Switch from tú to vosotros so readers in Spain feel addressed.
questions.explanation: "Ni modo" is a colloquial Mexicanism, so a general phrase helps; giving the currency makes the price clear outside Mexico. Spain's "coche" only moves the text from one region to another (choose "automóvil" or "vehículo"), and vosotros would be odd everywhere outside Spain: tú works across the region.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of the dubbing studio.

image.alt: A dubbing studio with five numbered parts: a large screen showing a cartoon face, the headphones on the voice actor's head, a microphone on a stand, a sheet of paper on a lectern, and the lectern's stand.

questions.explanation: The actor faces la pantalla (screen) and speaks into el micrófono, wearing los audífonos (Spain: los auriculares). El guion (script) rests on el atril (lectern). La cabina is the whole booth she stands in, not one of the numbered parts.

questions.stem: Match each term from the dubbing trade to its meaning.
choices: the film in its own language
a voice heard but not seen
the match between the lines and the lips
a dubbed version made in Spain
questions.explanation: La versión original (VO) is the original-language film; la voz en off is a narrator or speaker heard but not seen; la sincronía is lip sync; el subtitulaje (Mexico's usual term; Spain usually says el subtitulado) is subtitling. A Spanish dubbed version is simply un doblaje hecho en España.

questions.stem: Adapt the Mexican sentence for readers in every Spanish-speaking country, without using Spain's word. Type one word for "carro": Si vienes en ___, hay estacionamiento.
questions.explanation: "Automóvil" (or "vehículo") is understood everywhere and belongs to no single region; "auto" is also widely used in the Americas. "Coche" would move the text to Spain, and "carro" keeps it Mexican.

questions.stem: Listen to the dubbing director. According to her, what is the other half of the job?

audio.text: La sincronía es la mitad del trabajo. La otra mitad es actuar: si el público nota que estamos leyendo, perdimos.

questions.explanation: She says "La sincronía es la mitad del trabajo; la otra mitad es actuar": lip sync is half the job, acting is the other half. Jokes, accent and speed aren't what she named.

questions.stem: Listen to a line from a Mexican script. A director preparing a "neutral" version for all of Latin America would most likely replace which part?

audio.text: Préstamelo hoy y mañana te lo devuelvo, no seas mala onda.

choices: the tú form of the verb
questions.explanation: "No seas mala onda" (don't be a bad sport) is colloquial slang, heard in Mexico and elsewhere but not general, the kind of expression neutral dubbing avoids; a general phrase such as "no seas así" works everywhere. "Mañana te lo devuelvo", the tú forms and "préstamelo" are general Spanish.

questions.stem: In the online DLE, the verb "currar" is marked "coloq. Esp." What should a writer for readers in many countries take from that label?
choices: It is an error and should never be written.
It is a formal word used in Spanish legal texts.
It is informal and used in Spain, so readers elsewhere may not know it.
It is used everywhere except Spain.
questions.explanation: Coloq. means colloquial and Esp. means Spain: the sense is informal and Spanish. That is a warning, not a ban: replace or explain the word for other readers. Remember the reverse isn't guaranteed: an unmarked word (molar has no country mark) isn't always general.

questions.stem: Which statement about isoglosses is accurate?
choices: An isogloss is the border of a country's official language.
Isoglosses for different words usually coincide with national borders.
An isogloss is a word that has the same meaning everywhere.
Isoglosses for different features rarely coincide, so one map can't show "Latin American Spanish" for every word.
questions.explanation: An isogloss is a line where one feature (a word, a sound, a form) gives way to another. The line for carro/coche/auto and the line for computadora/ordenador fall in different places, and neither follows borders exactly.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: What is called "alberca" in Mexico is known in other countries as "piscina".
questions.explanation: "Lo que en México se llama alberca se conoce en otros países como piscina": lo que + clause works as the subject, and conocer como means "to know as". The subject clause can also go last: "Se conoce en otros países como piscina lo que en México se llama alberca." The phrase keeps the local word and gives the general one.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Each country has its own educated norm.
questions.explanation: "Cada país tiene su propia norma culta." The subject may also follow the verb ("Tiene cada país su propia norma culta"), a more emphatic order. Sus propias doesn't agree with the singular norma.

questions.stem: A Spanish student says to you and two friends: "¿Os apetece venir al cine?" Who is she talking to?
questions.explanation: Os is the object pronoun of vosotros, Spain's informal "you all". Mexico would say "¿Se les antoja venir al cine?" (ustedes). The formal plural in Spain is ustedes too.

questions.stem: You read in a Spanish novel: "A Juan le vi ayer en la estación." How does the norm treat this le?
choices: It is accepted: le as a direct object for one male person is admitted, though Mexico writes lo.
It is an error everywhere and is never written in Spain.
It means "I saw something for Juan".
It is accepted for women as well: A María le vi.
questions.explanation: This is leísmo of person: le for a man as a direct object. The RAE accepts it for one male person, so it appears in Spain's careful writing; Mexican and international writing keeps lo (A Juan lo vi ayer). Le for a woman or for things is not accepted.

questions.stem: Listen to a speaker from Spain (the app asks for a Spain voice, but your device may use another Spanish voice). What did the speaker do this morning?

audio.text: Esta mañana he ido a por el pan y me he encontrado con tu hermano.

choices: He is going to buy bread now.
He bought bread yesterday and met the listener's brother.
He went for bread this morning and ran into the listener's brother.
He has never met the listener's brother.
questions.explanation: Spain uses the perfect for today's events (he ido, me he encontrado = I went, I ran into), and "a por el pan" means "to get bread". So: this morning he went for bread and ran into your brother. Mexico would say "Hoy en la mañana fui por el pan y me encontré a tu hermano."

questions.stem: Listen to a speaker from Spain (the app asks for a Spain voice, but your device may use another Spanish voice). Which summary is right?

audio.text: Mi primo curra en un bar bastante cutre, pero el jefe es muy majo.

choices: The cousin works in a shabby bar, but his boss is nice.
The cousin is looking for a job in a nice bar.
The cousin's boss is shabby but the bar is lovely.
The cousin owns a bar with his boss.
questions.explanation: Currar is "to work" (informal, Spain), cutre "shabby, tacky" and majo "nice". So the cousin works in a shabby bar, and the boss is very nice.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of the street scene in Salamanca.

image.alt: A street in Salamanca with five numbered parts: the front wall of a small bar with the sign EL RINCÓN, a beer tap on the window ledge, a small glass of beer beside it, a long sandwich on a plate, and a small beach bar on a summer poster (palm tree, sea) on the building opposite.

questions.explanation: La tasca is the simple bar itself; on its ledge are el grifo (in Spain also a beer tap: cerveza de grifo), la caña (a small draft beer) and el bocadillo (a baguette sandwich). The poster shows a chiringuito, a beach bar. A botellón is a street drinking party, not shown.

questions.stem: Match each word from Spain with the Mexican word for the same thing.
questions.explanation: Curro/chamba (job), pasta/lana (money), grifo/llave (faucet; in Mexico la llave also means key), atasco/tráfico (traffic jam; Mexico also says el embotellamiento). La palomilla (gang of friends) matches Spain's la peña, which isn't in the list.

questions.stem: Which of these are typical of Spain's Spanish rather than Mexico's? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Vosotros, a por and the perfect for today's events (esta mañana he salido) are features of Spain. "¿Qué tú quieres?", with the subject before the verb in a question, is Caribbean (lesson 19).

questions.stem: Rewrite the leísta sentence in the Mexican standard. Type the missing pronoun: A Juan ___ vi ayer.
questions.explanation: Mexico and this course use lo for a man as a direct object: "A Juan lo vi ayer." Spain's "le vi" is accepted for one male person, but it isn't the Mexican norm.

questions.stem: In a Spanish e-mail: "¿Qué ___ anoche en la cena?" Which vosotros form means "What did you all eat last night?"
questions.explanation: Comisteis is the vosotros preterite of comer, right for a finished event last night. Comíais is the imperfect (used to eat), coméis the present and comáis the present subjunctive. You'll never need to produce these, but you should recognize them at once.

questions.stem: A friend from Madrid says "Voy a coger el autobús." In Mexico you would say the same thing as:
questions.explanation: In Spain coger simply means "to take", but in Mexico and much of Latin America it is vulgar, so Mexicans say tomar (or agarrar) el camión. Cachar is Chilean for "to understand", and a por is Spain's "to go and get".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: In Salamanca I live in a university residence hall.
questions.explanation: "En Salamanca vivo en un colegio mayor": el colegio mayor is a Spanish institution you may well write about. The place phrases can go before or after the verb. Vivís is a vosotros form, which you recognize but don't write.

questions.stem: Build the question in Spanish (Mexican standard).
questions.prompt: When are you coming to see me in Salamanca?
questions.explanation: "¿Cuándo vienes a verme a Salamanca?" (or "…a Salamanca a verme"). Venís is the vosotros form (and the Rioplatense vos form), not the tú form of the Mexican standard.

questions.stem: Where is a question like "¿Qué tú quieres?", with the subject before the verb, typical?
questions.explanation: Questions without inversion, together with frequent overt subjects, are typical of Caribbean Spanish (Cuba, Puerto Rico, the Dominican Republic and the coasts of Venezuela and Colombia). Elsewhere the standard is "¿Qué quieres (tú)?"

questions.stem: An Andean speaker says: "Mañana va a llover, dice." What does "dice" add?
choices: that the speaker is sure it will rain
that someone specific called a minute ago
that the speaker is quoting what they heard, not what they know
that the speaker is asking a question
questions.explanation: Sentence-final dice is a reportative: it marks hearsay ("they say", "reportedly"). Researchers often link it to Quechua, which marks hearsay with a suffix on the verb.

questions.stem: Listen to a colleague from Santiago. When will she send the file?

audio.text: ¿Cachái que mañana es feriado? Te mando el archivo al tiro.

questions.explanation: Al tiro means "right away" in Chile, faster than Mexico's ahorita, which can mean "in a while". ¿Cachái? is "do you get it?", with a Chilean voseo ending. The app's voice can't reproduce a Chilean accent.

questions.stem: Listen to a speaker from Buenos Aires. What is he asking?

audio.text: Che, ¿vos sabés a qué hora pasa el bondi?

choices: whether you know when the bus comes
whether you know where the subway is
whether you have change for the taxi
whether you want to share a car
questions.explanation: El bondi is the bus in the Río de la Plata (informal), and "vos sabés" is the voseo form of "tú sabes". He is asking whether you know what time the bus comes.

questions.stem: Match each word with the area where it is usual.
questions.explanation: Al tiro (right away) is Chilean; el bondi (bus) belongs to Buenos Aires and Montevideo; la chompa (sweater, probably from English jumper) is Andean; el chamo (kid) is Venezuelan. None is Spain's.

questions.stem: Which of these does the norm NOT accept? Select all that apply.
choices: La dije que viniera. (for "I told her to come")
Lo di un regalo. (for "I gave him a present")
A Juan le vi ayer. (for "I saw Juan yesterday")
Me lo explicó para que yo lo entendiera.
questions.explanation: La dije (laísmo) and lo di (loísmo) use a direct-object pronoun as an indirect object: the norm rejects both. Le vi for one man (leísmo of person) is accepted, and "para que yo lo entendiera" is the standard form of the Caribbean "para yo entenderlo".

questions.stem: A Chilean friend writes "¿Cómo estái?" Write the same greeting in the Mexican standard: ¿Cómo ___?
questions.explanation: Chilean verbal voseo keeps tú (or no pronoun) but uses a voseo ending, estái(s). The Mexican and general tú form is estás.

questions.stem: Which is the Rioplatense voseo command for "come here!"?
questions.explanation: Voseo commands drop the -d of the old vosotros command and stress the last syllable: vení, hablá, comé. Ven is the tú command, venga the usted command and venid Spain's vosotros command.

questions.stem: A porteño mentions "el gallego del bar de abajo, que en realidad es de Madrid". What does "el gallego" mean here?
choices: a man who speaks the Galician language
a man who works in a bar
a Spaniard (colloquially), wherever he is from
questions.explanation: In much of Latin America, especially Argentina, Uruguay and Cuba, gallego is colloquially any Spaniard, because so many emigrants came from Galicia. The speaker even says the man is from Madrid.

questions.stem: Which country's 1992 constitution makes Spanish and Guarani its official languages?
questions.explanation: Paraguay's Constitution of 1992 (art. 140) makes Spanish and Guarani official, and most Paraguayans speak both. Peru's 1993 constitution makes Quechua, Aymara and other Indigenous languages official where they predominate; Bolivia's 2009 constitution lists many Indigenous languages.

questions.stem: Build the standard version of "Me lo explicó para yo entenderlo".
questions.prompt: She explained it to me so that I would understand it.
questions.explanation: The standard uses para que + subjunctive when the subject changes: "Me lo explicó para que yo lo entendiera." The purpose clause can also come first, and yo can follow the verb. "Para yo entenderlo" is the Caribbean (and informal) pattern you recognize.

questions.stem: Build the polite request in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Can you say it again for me?
questions.explanation: "¿Me lo puedes repetir?", often after "Perdona,". Asking for a repetition is normal when a regional word or form is new to you. ("¿Puedes repetírmelo?" is also right, but these tiles build the version with the pronouns before the verb. Repitas, a subjunctive, doesn't fit here.)

questions.stem: In Ecuador you hear "Dame pasando la sal". Write the general request with the tú command: ___ la sal, por favor.
questions.explanation: "Pásame la sal, por favor" (or usted "Páseme"). Dar + gerund (dame pasando) is a softened request described as typical of Ecuadorian Spanish; its link to Kichwa is debated.

questions.stem: Who is a heritage speaker of Spanish?
choices: someone who learned Spanish as an adult in a classroom
someone who grew up hearing Spanish at home but was schooled mainly in another language
someone who inherited property in a Spanish-speaking country
questions.explanation: A heritage speaker (el hablante de herencia) grew up with Spanish at home and schooling in another language, usually English. Heritage speakers often speak with native ease and write less confidently; their Spanish is a variety, not "broken" Spanish.

questions.stem: "Te llamo para atrás" is a calque from English. What would a writer of standard Spanish say?
choices: Te llamo de vuelta para atrás.
questions.explanation: "Llamar para atrás" translates "call back" word for word. The standard is "devolver la llamada" (or "te llamo después / más tarde"). Describe the calque as a feature of US Spanish, but use the standard in formal writing.

questions.stem: Listen to a speaker at the round table. What is her view of code-switching?

audio.text: El cambio de código es una habilidad de bilingües, no una deficiencia. Lo que sí preocupa es la falta de transmisión intergeneracional.

choices: It is a deficiency that schools must correct.
It is a skill of bilingual speakers.
It shows that Spanish is disappearing in the United States.
questions.explanation: She says "El cambio de código es una habilidad de bilingües, no una deficiencia": a skill, not a deficiency. Her worry is a different one: the lack of transmission between generations.

questions.stem: Listen. Which term from the lesson names what the speaker describes?

audio.text: Hay familias en las que los abuelos son monolingües en quechua y los nietos solo hablan español.

questions.explanation: A community moving from Quechua to Spanish over generations, so that grandparents speak only Quechua and grandchildren only Spanish, is language shift (el desplazamiento lingüístico). Convergence is two languages growing alike; a loanword is a single borrowed word; diglossia is two languages with separate roles.

questions.stem: Match each term with its definition.
choices: an earlier language whose speakers shifted and left traces
a word taken from another language
two languages in contact growing alike
two languages or varieties with separate social roles
a phrase translated word for word
questions.explanation: Substrate: Nahuatl under Mexican Spanish, Quechua under Andean Spanish. Loanword: el elote, el tianguis. Convergence: shared structures after long contact. Diglossia: one language for school and law, another for home. A word-for-word phrase is a calque (el calco).

questions.stem: According to the lesson, which of these are standard in formal Spanish writing? Select all that apply.
choices: Los estudiantes deben inscribirse antes del viernes. (generic masculine)
Los estudiantes y las estudiantes deben inscribirse antes del viernes.
El alumnado debe inscribirse antes del viernes.
Les estudiantes deben inscribirse antes del viernes.
questions.explanation: The generic masculine, gender doubling and collective or neutral wording (el alumnado) are all standard; choose one and keep it. Forms in -e (les estudiantes) are not accepted by the RAE, though some groups use them on purpose.

questions.stem: Complete with the participle: Muchas palabras de mis abuelos han ___ en desuso.
questions.explanation: "Caer en desuso" means "to fall out of use"; the perfect is "han caído en desuso". Note the written accent on caído (ca-Í-do).

questions.stem: Put these waves of loanwords into Spanish in chronological order, from the earliest.
questions.explanation: Arabic words entered during the centuries of al-Andalus (711–1492); Taíno words came with the first voyages in the 1490s, before the conquest of Mexico brought Nahuatl words in the 16th century; French words such as garaje came mostly in the 19th and early 20th centuries, and English words in the 20th century and since.

questions.stem: Which sentence presents the inclusive-language debate in the neutral, attributed way the lesson recommends?
choices: El lenguaje inclusivo es incorrecto y no debe usarse.
El masculino genérico excluye a las mujeres.
Todo el mundo sabe que el desdoblamiento es innecesario.
La RAE sostiene que el masculino genérico es inclusivo, mientras que muchas instituciones recomiendan el desdoblamiento.
questions.explanation: A fair presentation says who holds each position: the RAE on one side, many institutions on the other. The other sentences state one side as fact, or appeal to "everybody", without attribution.

questions.stem: Which situation is usually cited as the Spanish-speaking example of diglossia?
choices: English and Spanish in a bilingual dictionary
questions.explanation: Paraguay, where Spanish and Guarani have long had different social roles, is the classic example; Guarani's official status since 1992 has changed that division. The term was made famous by Charles Ferguson in 1959.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The RAE holds that the generic masculine includes everyone.
questions.explanation: "La RAE sostiene que el masculino genérico incluye a todos." Sostener que reports a claim and takes the indicative (incluye). The subject of the que clause may also go last: "…que incluye a todos el masculino genérico". Attribution keeps a debated claim neutral.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Quechua is losing speakers to Spanish.
questions.explanation: "El quechua pierde hablantes frente al español." Frente a means "against, compared with". The phrase frente al español can come first or between subject and verb, and after a fronted phrase the subject can follow the verb.

questions.stem: On what date did the Catholic Monarchs sign the edict that expelled the Jews who would not convert?
questions.explanation: The edict was signed in Granada on March 31, 1492. January 2, 1492 is the surrender of Granada and October 12, 1492 Columbus's landfall; Portugal ordered its own expulsion a few years later.

questions.stem: Where does the word "sefardí" come from?
choices: from Sefarad, the Hebrew name for the Iberian Peninsula
from the name of a Spanish king
questions.explanation: Sefardí (Sephardic; plural sefardíes, also sefardís) comes from Sefarad, the Hebrew name for the Iberian Peninsula.

questions.stem: Judeo-Spanish "fijo" corresponds to modern Spanish "hijo". What does the f- show?
choices: a spelling mistake that became standard
an older form that Spanish later changed to a silent h
questions.explanation: Medieval Spanish wrote and said fijo; later the f- became h- and then fell silent in Spain's Spanish. Judeo-Spanish, cut off after 1492, kept the older form (fijo, favlar).

questions.stem: Match each Judeo-Spanish form, as the lesson's sources give it, with modern Spanish.
questions.explanation: Fijo and favlar keep the old f-; muestro shows nue- → mue-; kaza is a phonetic spelling that also keeps a z sound between vowels. Huésped (guest) is what Judeo-Spanish calls musafir, a Turkish loanword.

questions.stem: Match each Judeo-Spanish loanword with the language it came from.
questions.explanation: Ottoman neighbors gave Turkish words (musafir, araba); Hebrew supplied words of religion (haham, kal); meldar is traced to Greek; French words such as abazur came largely through the Alliance Israélite Universelle schools. Arabic loanwords are typical of Haketia in Morocco.

questions.stem: Which statements about the name "ladino" are accurate? Select all that apply.
choices: It is a common name for Judeo-Spanish in Israel and in English.
Many scholars reserve it for the word-for-word translation language of Hebrew sacred texts.
It is the only name speakers have ever used for their language.
In Central America, ladino also names a person of non-Indigenous culture.
questions.explanation: Ladino is widespread in Israel and in English, but many scholars keep it for the calque language of religious translations; speakers have also said judezmo or espanyol. In Central America ladino has another sense entirely, which is one reason judeoespañol is safer in a formal text.

questions.stem: What is the difference between "la aljama" and "la judería"?
choices: They are two spellings of the same word.
The aljama was the self-governing community; the judería was the quarter where Jews lived.
The aljama was a synagogue; the judería a school.
The aljama was a Muslim quarter; the judería was a Christian one.
questions.explanation: An aljama was a self-governing Jewish (or Muslim) community in medieval Spain; a judería is the Jewish quarter of a town, like those still preserved in Toledo, Girona and Córdoba.

questions.stem: Listen to the opening of the article. Where did the grandmother's family come from?

audio.text: La familia de mi abuela llegó a la Ciudad de México en los años veinte, desde Esmirna, la ciudad turca que hoy se llama Izmir.

questions.explanation: The writer says the family came to Mexico City in the 1920s "desde Esmirna", the Turkish city now called Izmir, like other Sephardic families of the former Ottoman Empire.

questions.stem: Listen. Which summary keeps the speaker's hedge?

audio.text: Los especialistas calculan que hoy lo hablan pocas decenas de miles de personas en el mundo, aunque las cifras varían mucho según la fuente.

choices: Hoy lo hablan exactamente cincuenta mil personas.
Según los especialistas, lo hablan pocas decenas de miles de personas, aunque las cifras varían.
Lo hablan millones de personas en Israel.
questions.explanation: The source attributes the figure to specialists and says the numbers vary by source; a faithful summary keeps both. An exact figure adds precision the source doesn't have, and "nadie" and "millones" contradict it.

questions.stem: Where was Haketia (la haquitía) spoken?
choices: in northern Morocco, in cities such as Tetuán and Tangier
questions.explanation: Haketia is the Judeo-Spanish of northern Morocco, rich in Arabic words. The Sephardim of the Ottoman Empire (Istanbul, Izmir, Thessaloniki) spoke the eastern varieties.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The Sephardim kept the language for centuries.
questions.explanation: "Los sefardíes conservaron el idioma durante siglos": the preterite presents the centuries as one completed span. The time phrase can open the sentence or follow the verb, and after it the subject may follow the verb or close the sentence. Conservó would need a singular subject.

questions.stem: Write the plural: el pueblo sefardí → los ___ (the Sephardim).
questions.explanation: The plural of sefardí is sefardíes; sefardís is also used. Both are accepted, as with other words ending in stressed -í.

questions.stem: Which is the only African country with Spanish as an official language?
questions.explanation: Equatorial Guinea, a Spanish colony until 1968, has Spanish as an official language together with French and Portuguese. Its academy joined ASALE in 2016.

questions.stem: What does the Philippines' 1987 Constitution say about languages?
choices: Spanish and English are the official languages.
Filipino and English are official; Spanish and Arabic are promoted on a voluntary and optional basis.
Spanish is the only official language.
Tagalog and Chavacano are the official languages.
questions.explanation: Under the 1987 Constitution the official languages are Filipino (based on Tagalog) and English; Spanish and Arabic are to be promoted voluntarily and optionally. Spanish survives as a remnant and in thousands of loanwords.

questions.stem: In the Chavacano sentence "Ya mirá yo cun José" (I saw José), what does "ya" do?
questions.explanation: In Chavacano the verb (mirá) doesn't change; small markers before it give the tense: ta present, ya past, di or ay future. Spanish ya "already" became a tense marker. Cun (from con) marks the person who is the object, like Spanish a.

questions.stem: Match each Tagalog word with its Spanish source.
questions.explanation: These are among the thousands of Spanish loanwords in Tagalog. Camote matches Tagalog kamote, a Nahuatl word that reached the Philippines through Mexican Spanish, which isn't among the items.

questions.stem: Which statements describe a creole such as Chavacano? Select all that apply.
choices: It forms when speakers of different languages build a shared language.
Children learn it as their first language.
It takes most words from one language and much of its grammar from others.
It is a careless way of speaking the language its words come from.
questions.explanation: A creole is a full language with native speakers, typically with vocabulary from one language and grammar shaped by others (Spanish words, Philippine grammar in Chavacano). It is not broken Spanish.

questions.stem: Between which years did the Manila galleon cross the Pacific between Acapulco and Manila?
questions.explanation: The galleon ran from 1565, when Urdaneta found the return route, to 1815. 1898 is when Spain lost the Philippines and 1821 Mexico's independence.

questions.stem: Listen to a teacher from Malabo. What role does Spanish play for her?

audio.text: En casa hablamos fang, pero con mis alumnos bubis el español es lo que tenemos en común.

choices: It is a language she never uses with her students.
It is a language only the government uses.
It is the shared language between speakers of different first languages.
questions.explanation: She speaks Fang at home, and Spanish is what she has in common with her Bubi students and others: a lingua franca (la lengua franca).

questions.stem: Listen to a radio announcer from Zamboanga. What is he defending?

audio.text: Para ustedes suena a español mal hablado. Para nosotros es nuestra lengua materna, la que aprendimos de nuestras madres.

choices: that Chavacano is a mother tongue in its own right
that Spanish should be official again
questions.explanation: He says that to Spanish speakers it sounds like badly spoken Spanish, but for his community it is "nuestra lengua materna": a creole, a full language learned from mothers.

questions.stem: Complete with one adjective: En Guinea Ecuatorial, el español es ___ con el francés y el portugués.
questions.explanation: Cooficial (co-official) takes the same form for both genders: el español es cooficial, la lengua cooficial.

questions.stem: Put these events in chronological order, from the earliest.
choices: The Philippines pass to the United States
questions.explanation: 1565 Legazpi; 1571 Manila; 1815 the last galleon; 1898 the Philippines pass to the United States; 1968 Equatorial Guinea's independence.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The galleon linked Acapulco with Manila.
questions.explanation: "El galeón unía Acapulco con Manila": the imperfect describes a regular, repeated link over two and a half centuries. The subject can also follow the verb. Unían would need a plural subject.

questions.stem: In general Spanish, what does the adjective "chabacano" mean?
questions.explanation: The adjective means tacky or vulgar, and the creole's name is usually explained from it. In Mexico the noun el chabacano is also an apricot.

questions.stem: Listen to the first part of the radio program. What does the biologist say about carrying capacity?

audio.text: Bienvenidos a Costa adentro. Hoy hablamos de un tema que en el Caribe mexicano ya no es nuevo: la masificación turística. Me acompañan la bióloga Itzel Canché y el economista Rodrigo Saldaña. Itzel, ¿cuánta gente aguanta una playa? Depende de la playa. Lo que llamamos capacidad de carga no es un número mágico: incluye el arrecife, el agua dulce, la basura, el drenaje. En algunos tramos del litoral creemos que ya se rebasó, pero los datos son incompletos y conviene ser prudentes. Rodrigo, desde la economía, ¿la saturación es un problema? Lo es, aunque no para todos por igual. La derrama económica del turismo sostiene a miles de familias; eso nadie lo discute. El problema es la estacionalidad: cuando llega el sargazo, la ocupación hotelera puede bajar en algunas zonas, y los empleos son los primeros en resentirlo.

choices: It is a fixed number of visitors per beach.
It is a set of limits, and the data on it are incomplete.
It has clearly been exceeded on the whole coast.
It depends mainly on hotel occupancy.
questions.explanation: Canché says carrying capacity "no es un número mágico" but includes the reef, fresh water, waste and drainage, and that some stretches have probably been exceeded ("creemos"), though the data are incomplete. Hotel occupancy is the economist's point about seasonality.

questions.stem: Listen to the second part of the program. Where do the two experts disagree?

audio.text: Y ojo: el sargazo no lo causa el turismo. Es un fenómeno del Atlántico que todavía estamos estudiando. De acuerdo. Lo que sí depende de nosotros es cómo crecemos. La renta vacacional, por ejemplo, ha multiplicado la oferta de cuartos sin pasar por los mismos permisos que un hotel. Podría haber ya una sobreoferta en ciertos destinos turísticos, aunque no tengo cifras definitivas. Ahí coincidimos. Sin ordenamiento territorial, cada nuevo desarrollo suma presión sobre el agua y el manglar. ¿Una moratoria, entonces? Yo no iría tan lejos. Preferiría reglas claras para todos. Yo sí la consideraría en las zonas más frágiles, al menos mientras se mide bien la huella ecológica.

choices: On the need for land-use planning
On whether vacation rentals have added rooms
questions.explanation: They agree that tourism doesn't cause sargassum and that land-use planning is needed ("Ahí coincidimos"). On a moratorium they part ways: he "no iría tan lejos" and prefers clear rules; she would consider one in the most fragile zones.

questions.stem: The economist said: "Podría haber ya una sobreoferta en ciertos destinos turísticos, aunque no tengo cifras definitivas." Which sentences report him with the same strength? Select all that apply.
choices: Saldaña estima que podría haber una sobreoferta en algunos destinos.
Saldaña considera posible una sobreoferta en algunos destinos.
Saldaña afirma que hay una sobreoferta en algunos destinos.
Saldaña no descarta que haya una sobreoferta en algunos destinos.
Saldaña demuestra que existe una sobreoferta en algunos destinos.
questions.explanation: "Estima que podría", "considera posible" and "no descarta que" + subjunctive all keep his hedge. "Afirma que hay" turns a possibility into a claim, and "demuestra" adds proof he explicitly says he doesn't have ("no tengo cifras definitivas").

questions.stem: Choose the reporting verb that fits the news item: "Una investigadora ___ esa lectura: reconoció que la presión existe, pero señaló otras causas."
questions.explanation: "Matizar" (B1) is to qualify: she accepts part of the reading (the pressure exists) and adds limits (other causes, no conclusive evidence). "Confirmó" and "celebró" say she agreed fully, and "demostró" claims a proof the text doesn't give.

questions.stem: Complete with the present of "aunar": "La propuesta ___ conservación y empleo." (The proposal combines conservation and jobs.)
questions.explanation: "Aúna": the stem is stressed in the él form, so the u takes a written accent (aúno, aúnas, aúna, aúnan; but aunamos). Without it, "auna" would be stressed on the a.

questions.stem: Match each phrase with what it does in a synthesis.
choices: attributes a claim to a source
questions.explanation: "Según…" attributes; "coinciden en que" marks agreement; "frente a esta postura" contrasts; "a juicio de quien firma" (in the view of the undersigned) introduces the writer's own assessment, kept apart from the sources.

questions.stem: Put the steps for writing a synthesis in order.
choices: Read the instructions for genre, reader and purpose
Take notes on each source, hedges included
Build a grid of sources and points
Reread for hedges, register and length
