questions.explanation: The instructions fix the register and genre, so they come first; notes feed the grid; the grid gives the paragraph plan; then you write and, last, check your text against the sources and the word range.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this coast.

image.alt: A Caribbean coast in cross-section: hotels and a palm tree on the left, a beach sloping into the sea with clumps of brown seaweed on the sand, a pier running out toward a cruise ship, and a coral reef on the sea floor on the right. Four parts are numbered.

questions.explanation: The ship is el crucero (B1), near el muelle (the pier); the brown seaweed on the beach is el sargazo; the coral on the sea floor is el arrecife (B2). El litoral is the whole coastal strip, not one numbered part, and la vitrina is a display case.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Both sources agree that the data are incomplete.
questions.explanation: "Ambas fuentes coinciden en que los datos son incompletos." "Coincidir" takes "en" before a que-clause, so "coinciden que" is queísmo, which careful writing avoids. The subject can also follow the verb: "Coinciden ambas fuentes en que…"

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The economist thinks there could be an oversupply.
questions.explanation: "El economista estima que podría haber una sobreoferta." The conditional "podría" keeps his hedge; the tile "hay" would turn it into a flat claim. In formal writing the subject can follow the verb: "Estima el economista que…"

questions.stem: In the 2024 sample exam, as a 2024 study describes it, what does writing task 1 ask for?
choices: A 200–250-word text from a list of notes
A 400–450-word text from a radio excerpt and two written texts, in a set genre for a set reader
A free essay of any length giving your opinion on one article
questions.explanation: Task 1 is mediation from several sources: two experts on the radio and two informational texts, synthesized in 400–450 words for the reader and genre the instructions name. The 220–250-word task from one talk is the DELE C1's; notes into 200–250 words is C2's task 2.

questions.stem: Complete with the preterite of "contraponer": "En su carta, las cooperativas ___ el turismo de cruceros al de estancias largas."
questions.explanation: "Contraponer" is conjugated like "poner": puse → contrapuse, pusieron → contrapusieron. The subject is plural (las cooperativas).

questions.stem: Listen to the exhibition designer's voice message to the copywriter. What does he ask her not to do?

audio.text: Paula, te dejo los apuntes para la cédula de la sala 2. Es una cédula temática, de doscientas a doscientas cincuenta palabras, para público general; piensa también en los grupos de secundaria y prepa que nos visitan. Lo más importante: no pongas fechas exactas sobre cuándo empezó a consumirse el cacao, porque los especialistas no se ponen de acuerdo. Habla de la espuma, que era lo más apreciado, y de las semillas como moneda. Cierra invitando a ver la vitrina tres, y ojo con decir que la palabra chocolate viene del náhuatl: eso está en discusión. Gracias.

choices: Mention the foam of the drink
Give exact dates for when cacao began to be consumed
Invite visitors to look at case 3
questions.explanation: "No pongas fechas exactas sobre cuándo empezó a consumirse el cacao, porque los especialistas no se ponen de acuerdo." He asks for the foam and the invitation to case 3, and the label is to be 200–250 words.

questions.stem: Listen to the message again. Who is the target reader of the label?

audio.text: Paula, te dejo los apuntes para la cédula de la sala 2. Es una cédula temática, de doscientas a doscientas cincuenta palabras, para público general; piensa también en los grupos de secundaria y prepa que nos visitan. Lo más importante: no pongas fechas exactas sobre cuándo empezó a consumirse el cacao, porque los especialistas no se ponen de acuerdo. Habla de la espuma, que era lo más apreciado, y de las semillas como moneda. Cierra invitando a ver la vitrina tres, y ojo con decir que la palabra chocolate viene del náhuatl: eso está en discusión. Gracias.

choices: The general public, including school groups of teenagers
questions.explanation: "Para público general; piensa también en los grupos de secundaria y prepa": the general public, with middle and high school groups in mind. That reader decides the register: clear, no jargon.

questions.stem: Which version corrects the draft sentence "Los españoles al principio no les gustó su sabor amargo"?
choices: Los españoles, al principio, no les gustó su sabor amargo.
A los españoles al principio no le gustaron su sabor amargo.
A los españoles, al principio, no los gustó su sabor amargo.
A los españoles, al principio, no les gustó su sabor amargo.
questions.explanation: "Gustar" needs the person as an indirect object with "a": "A los españoles… no les gustó su sabor". The subject is "su sabor" (singular), so "gustó", not "gustaron"; "los" is a direct-object pronoun and doesn't fit. The commas around "al principio" are optional.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct in careful writing? Select all that apply.
choices: El comercio consistía en embarques a Sevilla.
Las semillas de cacao siguió circulando como moneda.
Esto dio origen a una costumbre.
El comercio con Europa, consistía en embarques.
La nueva bebida carecía de espuma.
questions.explanation: "Consistir en", "dio" (monosyllables take no accent) and "carecer de" (to lack) are all correct. "Las semillas… siguió" breaks agreement (siguieron), and a comma never separates a subject from its verb.

questions.stem: Match each problem from the draft with the better form.
questions.explanation: "Eventualmente" means possibly or now and then, not "eventually"; the DPD advises against "en base a" (it prefers "sobre la base de" and doesn't fault "con base en", lesson 08), though "en base a" is very frequent in Mexico; "se sabe de que" is dequeísmo; "caso de exhibición" translates "case" word for word, and the Spanish term is "la vitrina".

questions.stem: Complete with the verb that means "to spell out, make explicit": "Conviene ___ quién es el lector meta."
questions.explanation: "Explicitar" is to make explicit what a text leaves implied. It isn't A1's "deletrear" (to spell a word letter by letter).

questions.stem: Put the parts of the model label "El cacao: bebida y moneda" in the order the copywriter used.
choices: What cacao is and where it grows
Its ancient use and the debate about dates
The drink and its prized foam
The seeds as money and tribute
The objects in case 3, with a question to the visitor
questions.explanation: The label moves from the plant to its history, then to its two uses (drink, money), then to the objects the visitor can see, and ends on the words, pointing to the next room.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this exhibition hall.

image.alt: A museum hall: a large text panel on the wall on the left; on the right, a glass case on a pedestal holding a three-legged vessel and a gourd cup, with a small card at the foot of the vessel. Four parts are numbered.

questions.explanation: The wall panel is la cédula (in Mexican museums); the glass case is la vitrina; the vessel inside is la pieza de museo; the small card with material, date and provenance is la ficha técnica. La sangría is a paragraph indent.

questions.stem: Which is the best post-edited version of "Please do not touch the display case" for a sign in a Mexican museum?
choices: Favor de no tocar la vitrina.
Por favor no toque el caso de exhibición.
Favor de no tocar el caso.
Por favor, no tocar la caja de exhibición.
questions.explanation: "Favor de" + infinitive is the polite notice Mexican signs commonly use, and "la vitrina" is the term for a display case. "Caso" is a false friend for "case" here, and "caja de exhibición" isn't the term.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The copywriter (a woman) polished the final version.
questions.explanation: "La redactora pulió la versión final." "Pulir" is a regular -ir verb: pulí, pulió ("puló" doesn't exist). The subject can also follow the verb: "Pulió la versión final la redactora."

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The spell-checker doesn't catch false friends.
questions.explanation: "El corrector automático no detecta los falsos amigos": a false friend is a real word, correctly spelled, used in the wrong sense. A statement of fact takes the indicative ("detecta"); the subject can also follow the verb.

questions.stem: What does the lesson say about writing task 2 in the 2024 format?
choices: It is a 400–450-word synthesis of three sources.
In the 2024 sample exam it turns notes into a 200–250-word text; whether it still includes correcting a draft isn't confirmed.
It is always the correction of a machine-translated text.
It was removed from the exam in 2024.
questions.explanation: As a 2024 study describes the sample exam, task 2 turns a list of notes into a 200–250-word text in a set genre and role. The old format corrected a draft, sometimes machine-translated; whether that survives is to be checked in the 2024 guide, so the lesson practices both.

questions.stem: Listen to the start of the presentation. What worries the demographer the speaker quotes?

audio.text: Los materiales que elegí tratan del envejecimiento de la población y de sus consecuencias para las pensiones. Son dos textos breves, uno de carácter demográfico y otro económico, y una gráfica con dos pirámides de población. Voy a presentarlos en ese orden, luego los voy a relacionar y, al final, daré mi opinión. El primer texto parte de datos del INEGI: en México hay unos 19 millones de personas de 60 años o más, casi el 15 % de la población, y la edad mediana ya es de 32 años. Lo interesante es el enfoque de la demógrafa que cita: para ella, vivir más es un logro, y lo que le preocupa no es el envejecimiento en sí, sino su velocidad.

choices: The speed at which the population is aging
The fact that people live longer
The number of children born each year
questions.explanation: "Para ella, vivir más es un logro, y lo que le preocupa no es el envejecimiento en sí, sino su velocidad." Living longer is an achievement for her, not the worry.

questions.stem: Listen to the end of the presentation. What does the speaker point out that none of the materials covers?

audio.text: Si los comparo, los tres materiales coinciden en la dirección del cambio, pero cada uno mira un aspecto distinto: el primero, la sociedad; el segundo, el dinero; la gráfica, la forma general. Ninguno, por cierto, habla de quién cuidará a las personas mayores. Y esa es precisamente mi opinión: creo que el debate suele reducirse a las pensiones, cuando el cuidado, la salud y la vivienda importan tanto como el monto que cada quien reciba. Una pensión suficiente es necesaria, pero no basta para envejecer bien. En resumen, los materiales muestran un cambio que ya empezó, y la pregunta es si nos va a encontrar preparados.

choices: Who will care for older people
questions.explanation: "Ninguno, por cierto, habla de quién cuidará a las personas mayores." Pensions, the pyramid and the reform are all in the materials; care is the gap she builds her opinion on.

questions.stem: In a group, the mean pension is 6800 pesos and the median is 4200 pesos. What follows?
choices: Most people in the group receive about 6800 pesos.
Half the group receives 4200 pesos or less.
Nobody in the group receives more than 6800 pesos.
questions.explanation: The median is the middle value: half the cases are at or below it. A mean far above the median means a few high pensions pull the average up, so the median describes the typical case better than the mean.

questions.stem: Complete with the word for the middle value of an ordered series: "La ___ es más baja que la media, porque unos pocos ganan mucho."
questions.explanation: "La mediana" (median) is the middle value; "la media" is the mean, and B2's "el promedio" the everyday average.

questions.stem: Which sentences present a projection with the right caution? Select all that apply.
choices: Según la proyección, en 2050 habría unas 39 personas mayores por cada 100 en edad de trabajar.
En 2050 habrá exactamente 39 personas mayores por cada 100 en edad de trabajar.
De mantenerse la tendencia, la proporción podría llegar al 24 %.
La gráfica prueba que la baja de la fecundidad causó el cambio.
Se trata de una proyección, no de un pronóstico.
questions.explanation: A projection holds only if its assumptions do: "según la proyección… habría", "de mantenerse la tendencia… podría" and the explicit caveat are right. "Habrá exactamente" turns it into a certainty, and a chart of quantities can't prove a cause.

questions.stem: Match each term with its meaning.
choices: dependents per 100 people of working age
the share of the last salary that the pension replaces
a period when the working-age population grows faster than the dependent population
a group born in the same years, followed over time
the average number of children per woman
questions.explanation: The distractor describes la fecundidad (fertility), usually measured as children per woman.

questions.stem: Put the parts of the model presentation in the order the speaker used.
choices: Introduction: the topic, the materials and the plan
questions.explanation: She announces her plan ("voy a presentarlos en ese orden, luego los voy a relacionar y, al final, daré mi opinión") and follows it: each material, the comparison, the opinion, the close.

questions.stem: In these fictional pyramids, what share of the population is 60 or over in the 2050 projection?

image.alt: Two population pyramids with fictional data. Under the 2025 pyramid: 0–14, 22.5%; 60 or over, 14.2%. Under the 2050 projection: 0–14, 15.6%; 60 or over, 23.8%.

questions.explanation: The label under the 2050 pyramid gives 23.8% aged 60 or over (14.2% is 2025, and 15.6% is the 0–14 group in 2050). 39 is a ratio from the model article: older people per 100 of working age.

questions.stem: According to the text on pensions, how many weeks of contributions are required in 2031?
questions.explanation: The requirement was 750 weeks in 2021 and rises by 25 a year until it reaches 1000 in 2031 (the reform of 2020, as the text summarizes it).

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: It would be risky to extrapolate these data.
questions.explanation: "Sería arriesgado extrapolar estos datos" or, with the infinitive phrase first, "Extrapolar estos datos sería arriesgado." After "sería arriesgado" Spanish uses the infinitive, not the gerund.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The median is lower than the mean.
questions.explanation: "La mediana es más baja que la media." "El medio" is the middle or a means, not the statistical mean.

questions.stem: What does the speaking test's first task involve at C2, according to the Instituto Cervantes' examiner-training material (2023)?
choices: Reading a single article aloud and summarizing it in two minutes
A 5–6-minute presentation from several texts and charts, prepared in 30 minutes, from notes that may be consulted but not read
A debate with another candidate on four headlines
A written summary of a talk
questions.explanation: You choose between two sets of materials, prepare for 30 minutes and present for 5–6 minutes; at C2 the materials include several texts. Notes may be consulted, not read aloud, and the examiner signals at five minutes.

questions.stem: Listen to part of Claire's letter. What happened to her hesitation with unfamiliar accents?

audio.text: Lo segundo fue escuchar mucho y de todas partes: podcasts argentinos, noticieros colombianos, una serie española. Al principio titubeaba con cada acento; al cabo de unas semanas, el titubeo se volvió curiosidad. Nadie te pide que imites esas variedades, pero sí que las entiendas.

choices: It became curiosity after a few weeks.
It disappeared when she started imitating the accents.
It stopped her from listening to Spanish podcasts.
It made her choose only Mexican sources.
questions.explanation: "Al principio titubeaba con cada acento; al cabo de unas semanas, el titubeo se volvió curiosidad." She adds that nobody asks you to imitate the varieties, only to understand them.

questions.stem: Listen to another part of the letter. What didn't work for Claire?

audio.text: Ahora, lo que no me funcionó: los modelos de examen anteriores a 2024. El formato cambió, y preparé durante semanas una tarea que ya no existe. Revisa siempre la fecha de cada material y consulta la guía oficial.

questions.explanation: "Lo que no me funcionó: los modelos de examen anteriores a 2024." The format changed, and she practiced a task that no longer exists; she recommends checking every material's date and the official guide.

questions.stem: How long is the DELE C2's written expression, mediation and interaction test (test 2), as the Instituto Cervantes describes it?
questions.explanation: Test 2 lasts 150 minutes for its three texts. Test 1 lasts 105 minutes; the speaking test 20, plus 30 minutes to prepare; 80 minutes is the DELE C1's writing test.

questions.stem: Match each DELE C2 test with what it contains.
choices: language use, reading and listening tasks
a presentation, an interview and a conversation
a single essay on a literary work
questions.explanation: Test 1 combines language use with reading and listening (52 items); test 2 has the three writing tasks (sources, notes, data); test 3 has the three speaking tasks. Mediation is in tests 2 and 3.

questions.stem: Which of these does the lesson tell you to check in the official guide? Select all that apply.
choices: How the written texts are marked
That the exam has three tests
That the tests are worth about a third of the points each
questions.explanation: The pass rule, the written marking scales, dates and fees aren't settled by the sources this course could read, so check them in the guide. The three tests and their points come from the Instituto Cervantes' DELE C2 page.

questions.stem: Complete: the Spanish version of the CEFR names the C2 level "___".
questions.explanation: C2 is "Maestría" (mastery), and C1 and C2 together are the "usuario competente" (proficient user).

questions.stem: Which description fits C2 as this lesson presents the CEFR?
choices: A native speaker's accent and a vocabulary of rare words
Ease in understanding, precise expression with finer shades of meaning, smooth texts suited to the reader, and mediation from several sources
Fluent conversation on everyday topics only
questions.explanation: The descriptors stress ease, precision, fine distinctions of meaning, smoothly flowing texts in a suitable style and mediation. The lesson notes that C2 doesn't describe a native speaker, isn't error-free, and rewards suitability and relevance as much as lexical richness.

questions.stem: "She answered without hesitation." Complete: "Respondió ___ titubeos."
questions.explanation: "Sin titubeos" means without hesitation. "Con titubeos" is correct Spanish too, but it means the opposite: hesitantly.

questions.stem: Put Claire's advice in the order her letter gives it.
choices: Stop collecting rare words and aim for the exact term
Listen to many varieties of Spanish
Write a weekly synthesis from several sources
Record yourself and aim for clarity
Don't prepare with pre-2024 model exams
questions.explanation: The letter numbers its points (lo primero, lo segundo, lo tercero), then turns to speaking, then to "lo que no me funcionó", and ends with the educated register.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Nobody expects your Spanish to be spotless.
questions.explanation: "Nadie espera que tu español sea intachable." "Esperar que" with the sense of expecting or hoping takes the subjunctive ("sea").

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Each test is worth a third of the points.
questions.explanation: "Cada prueba vale un tercio de los puntos." "Cada" takes a singular verb ("vale"). The subject can also follow the verb.

questions.stem: In the speaking test, as the 2023 training material describes it, who gives a holistic mark for the three tasks?
choices: A third examiner who listens to a recording
questions.explanation: The interviewer gives one overall (holistic) mark; the rater listens and marks each task analytically, in separate categories. The 2024 guide may describe the roles differently: check it.

questions.stem: Choose the word that fits: "Los resultados ___ de manifiesto una tendencia clara."
questions.explanation: "Poner de manifiesto" (to show clearly) is a fixed phrase (C1). The other verbs don't combine with "de manifiesto": collocation decides.

questions.stem: In a scientific article, the authors admit a limitation of their study: "Sus autores ___ que la muestra era reducida." Which verb fits the sense and the register?
questions.explanation: Authors who admit a limitation "reconocen" it. "Delatar" is to inform on someone, "presumir" to boast (or to presume, which changes the meaning), and "chismear" (to gossip) is colloquial.

questions.stem: Complete with one preposition: "Los autores invitan ___ la cautela al interpretar los resultados."
questions.explanation: "Invitar a" + noun or infinitive: "invitan a la cautela" (they call for caution). Government decides here.

questions.stem: In "Elogio de la fila", which sentence fills the gap? "Claro que la igualdad de la fila tiene sus matices. ___ Más polémicas son las filas que se compran."
choices: Por eso muchas instituciones han sustituido la fila visible por el número de turno.
Nadie la inventó y nadie la decreta.
Hay filas preferentes para personas mayores, embarazadas o con discapacidad, y casi nadie las discute.
La pantalla que anuncia los turnos ordena mejor, pero no reúne a nadie.
questions.explanation: "Más polémicas" (more controversial) needs a less controversial case just before it: priority lines that almost nobody disputes. The other sentences belong to other paragraphs (the origin of the line, turn numbers, screens).

questions.stem: In the same essay, which sentence fills the gap? "___ La medida es eficaz: nadie tiene que permanecer de pie."
choices: Por eso muchas instituciones han sustituido la fila visible por el número de turno o la cita en línea.
Pocas leyes se cumplen con tanta naturalidad.
El que se cuela no rompe una norma legal.
Lo asombroso no es que haya filas, sino que funcionen.
questions.explanation: "La medida" (the measure) points back to a measure just named: replacing the visible line with ticket numbers or online appointments. That also explains why nobody has to stand.

questions.stem: Match each short academic text with what it does.
left: Reseña de un volumen colectivo sobre la siesta en la literatura española.
Se encuestó a 1200 usuarios mediante un cuestionario en línea de veinte preguntas.
El artículo contrasta los tiempos de espera en los hospitales públicos de tres países.
choices: It describes how data were collected.
It argues for a change in the law.
questions.explanation: "Reseña de un volumen" is a book review; "se encuestó… mediante un cuestionario" describes a method; "contrasta… en tres países" compares places. None of the three argues for a legal change.

questions.stem: Listen to the short monologue. What is the speaker doing?

audio.text: Ay, sí, claro, como tú nunca llegas tarde... Bueno, ya, olvídalo. Lo importante es que llegaste, ¿no? Pásale, pásale, que se enfría la comida y la abuela ya preguntó por ti tres veces.

choices: Teasing someone about being late, then welcoming them
Complaining that the food is cold
Asking someone to call her grandmother
questions.explanation: "Como tú nunca llegas tarde" is ironic teasing; "olvídalo… lo importante es que llegaste… pásale" welcomes the latecomer in. The food and the grandmother are reasons to come in, not complaints or requests. Glosses: pásale (Mexico: come in).

questions.stem: Listen to two speakers. Which idea belongs to the second speaker, Julio?

audio.text: Marta: Yo trabajo desde cafés casi todos los días. Me concentro mejor con un poco de ruido, y además salgo de la casa, que para mí es fundamental. Lo único que me molesta es depender del internet del lugar. Julio: Pues yo lo intenté un mes y no me funcionó. Gastaba más de lo que pensaba, y no podía hacer llamadas sin que todo el mundo se enterara de mis asuntos. Prefiero una oficina compartida, aunque cueste.

choices: Working in cafés helps him concentrate.
Getting out of the house is essential for him.
He depends on the café's internet.
He couldn't make calls without others hearing his business.
questions.explanation: Julio tried cafés for a month: he spent more than expected and couldn't make calls privately, so he prefers a shared office. Concentration, getting out and the internet are Marta's points: the classic trap of matching an idea to the wrong speaker.

questions.stem: Listen to part of a talk. Which ideas does the speaker express? Select all that apply.

audio.text: Cuando hablamos de memoria solemos imaginar un archivo: guardamos un recuerdo y, más tarde, lo sacamos intacto. La investigación de las últimas décadas sugiere otra cosa. Cada vez que recordamos algo, lo reconstruimos, y en esa reconstrucción se cuelan detalles nuevos. Eso no significa que la memoria sea inútil; significa que es un proceso, no un depósito. Por eso los testigos de buena fe pueden equivocarse, y por eso conviene anotar lo importante cuanto antes. Les propongo un ejercicio sencillo: escriban hoy lo que hicieron el fin de semana y vuelvan a contarlo dentro de un mes. Comparen las dos versiones. No buscamos culpables, sino entender cómo trabaja nuestra mente.

choices: It's worth writing important things down soon.
Memories are stored intact, like files.
questions.explanation: She says each act of remembering reconstructs the memory, that witnesses "de buena fe" can be wrong, and that it's worth noting important things "cuanto antes". She explicitly denies that memory is useless, and the file image is the idea she argues against.

questions.stem: Which are signs that an option may be a trap? Select all that apply.
choices: It repeats words from the text with another meaning.
It attributes a claim to the wrong speaker.
It is true in general but not what the text says.
It uses a synonym of a word in the text.
It paraphrases a sentence of the text.
questions.explanation: Repeated words in a new sense, a misattributed claim and a true-but-absent statement are the classic traps. The right answer very often uses synonyms or a paraphrase, so neither is a warning sign by itself.

questions.stem: What is "una pregunta capciosa"?
choices: A question with two right answers
A question about the gist of a text
A question built to deceive, which good exams avoid
A question that repeats the text's words
questions.explanation: "Una pregunta capciosa" (a trick question) is designed to mislead. Exam distractors are wrong for a reason you can name, which is different.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I got to the answer by elimination.
questions.explanation: "Llegué a la respuesta por descarte." "Por descarte" is the fixed phrase (by elimination); it can also go first or right after the verb.

questions.stem: As preparation sites describe it, which task was added to test 1 in 2024?
choices: Short monologues matched to their communicative intention
A long debate with three-option questions
Fragments to put back into a text
questions.explanation: The new task 7: short monologues matched to the speaker's intention, where tone, idioms and colloquial language matter. The others come from the old format. Check the 2024 guide for the details.

questions.stem: Listen to part of the presentation. According to the agronomist, what is the main benefit of rooftop gardens?

audio.text: El primer texto es una columna de una agrónoma especializada en agricultura urbana. Su postura es favorable, pero no ingenua. Por un lado, enumera las ventajas de un huerto en la azotea: el edificio se calienta menos en verano, se producen algunos alimentos y, sobre todo, los vecinos tienen un motivo para encontrarse. Por otro, advierte que no todas las azoteas resisten el peso de la tierra y del agua, y que el riego y el mantenimiento tienen un costo que casi nunca se calcula al principio. Me pareció interesante que no presente los huertos como una solución al problema de los alimentos, sino como un proyecto social. De hecho, ella misma reconoce que la cantidad de comida que se obtiene es modesta, y que el beneficio principal es otro: que personas que viven en el mismo edificio, y que a veces ni se saludan, compartan una tarea.

choices: Neighbors share a task and get to know each other.
questions.explanation: She admits the amount of food is modest; "el beneficio principal es otro": neighbors who barely greet each other share a task. The weight of soil and water is one of her warnings, not a benefit.

questions.stem: Listen to the speaker on the chart. How does she treat its figures?

audio.text: En cuanto a la gráfica, muestra los resultados de una encuesta, con datos ficticios, sobre quién participaría en un huerto en la azotea de su edificio. El interés baja con la edad: un 41 % de las personas de 18 a 29 años, un 35 % de las de 30 a 49, y solo un 22 % de las mayores de 50. La gráfica no explica por qué; podríamos pensar en el esfuerzo físico, o en que los jóvenes viven más a menudo en edificios con azotea común, pero eso ya sería interpretación mía. Tampoco sabemos cuántas personas respondieron ni en qué ciudad, así que conviene tomar las cifras como una tendencia y no como un resultado definitivo.

choices: As proof that older people dislike gardening
As a trend, since the number of respondents and the city aren't given
As official statistics from the city
As the main argument of her opinion
questions.explanation: She flags the data as fictional, labels her explanation as "interpretación mía", and says that, without the number of respondents or the city, the figures are a trend, not a definitive result.

questions.stem: As the 2023 training material describes it, what are the three parts of the speaking test's interview (task 2)?
choices: Extending the topic, relating it to you, and the materials you didn't choose
A role play, a negotiation, and a debate
Your studies, your work, and your plans
questions.explanation: The interview follows task 1's topic: it extends it, personalizes it, and asks about the materials you didn't choose.

questions.stem: Match each formula with what it does.
left: En eso le doy la razón.
questions.explanation: Conceding, steering back, holding the floor and offering a counterexample are the moves of C2 interaction; none of these formulas closes a presentation (that would be "En resumen…").

questions.stem: In the model task 3 conversation, which moves does the candidate make? Select all that apply.
choices: He concedes the risk of cheating before counter-arguing.
He answers a counterexample with a parallel case.
He names his change of position.
He switches from usted to tú.
He refuses to answer the last question.
questions.explanation: "En eso le doy la razón" concedes; nervous students are answered with students who panic in exams; "Matizo mi postura" names the change. He keeps usted throughout, and he answers the last question after buying a second to think.

questions.stem: Complete with the preterite of "reconducir": "La moderadora ___ el debate hacia el tema."
questions.explanation: "Reconducir" goes like "conducir": conduje, condujo → reconduje, recondujo (not "recondució").

questions.stem: The interviewer challenges your position directly (una interpelación). What does the lesson advise?
choices: Ignore the challenge and continue your argument.
Answer the challenge, then steer back to your point.
Ask the interviewer to change the topic.
questions.explanation: Answer the challenge itself (concede what is reasonable, counter-argue where needed) and then reconducir: bring the conversation back to the task.

questions.stem: What does "el tira y afloja" mean?
choices: A give-and-take of concessions and demands
questions.explanation: "El tira y afloja" (literally "pull and slacken") is a give-and-take: each side yields a little and holds firm on what matters.

questions.stem: Put the parts of the speaking test in order.
choices: Task 3: the conversation on a headline
questions.explanation: You prepare task 1 for 30 minutes; then, in the 20-minute test, you present, are interviewed on the same topic, and finally choose a headline and negotiate.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish (usted).
questions.prompt: On that you're right.
questions.explanation: "En eso le doy la razón" (literally "on that I give you the reason"). "Dar la razón a alguien" takes an indirect object: le, not lo. The phrase can also end the sentence: "Le doy la razón en eso."

questions.stem: The interviewer uses usted. Which reply keeps the same form of address throughout?
choices: Si lo piensas bien, usted también ha visto exámenes injustos.
Si lo piensa bien, tú también has visto exámenes injustos.
Si lo piensa bien, usted también ha visto exámenes injustos.
Si lo piensas bien, tú también has visto exámenes injustos.
questions.explanation: "Si lo piensa bien, usted… ha visto" keeps usted. The two mixed replies switch between tú and usted, and the all-tú reply abandons the interviewer's usted.

questions.stem: As the 2023 training material describes it, which categories does the rater mark for each speaking task?
choices: The number of words and the time used
Only whether the candidate gave an opinion
Fluency, accuracy, range, and the task's own category with task fulfilment
questions.explanation: The rater's analytic marks cover fluency, accuracy and range, plus each task's own category (mediation, interview or interaction) with task fulfilment. The interviewer gives a holistic mark.

questions.stem: What does the lesson suggest instead of filling an awkward silence with "este… este…"?
choices: Waiting in silence until the examiner speaks
questions.explanation: A rephrasing keeps you talking with content, gives you time to think, and shows range; "este… este…" only fills the gap.

questions.stem: Listen to the doctor. Which English rendering is accurate and complete?

audio.text: Le voy a pedir una radiografía para descartar una fractura. Mientras tanto, reposo, hielo y el pie en alto.

choices: I'm going to order an X-ray. Rest.
I'm going to order an X-ray to rule out a fracture. In the meantime, rest, ice, and keep your foot raised.
I'm sure it's a fracture, so I'll order an X-ray. Rest, ice, and keep your foot raised.
I'm going to order an X-ray to rule out a fracture. Don't worry, it's probably nothing.
questions.explanation: Every element is there: the X-ray, its purpose (to rule out a fracture), and the three instructions. The other versions omit instructions, change "descartar" into certainty, or add reassurance the doctor never gave.

questions.stem: Listen to the supplier. What should the interpreter do?

audio.text: No se preocupe: el pedido se lo mandamos ahorita.

choices: Say, in both languages, that she is asking for clarification, then ask what "ahorita" means here.
questions.explanation: "Ahorita" can mean right now, in a while, or later, and in a deal the difference matters. Any guess adds a meaning the speaker didn't commit to; leaving it out is an omission. The transparent move is to ask, openly, in both languages.

questions.stem: The patient says: "I twisted my ankle." What does the interpreter say to the doctor?
choices: Dice que se torció el tobillo.
La paciente se torció el tobillo, doctora.
questions.explanation: Interpreters speak in the first person, so each party talks to the other: "Me torcí el tobillo." Reporting ("dice que") puts the interpreter between them, and "creo" adds a hedge the patient didn't use.

questions.stem: Match each kind of interpreting with how it works.
choices: short turns, both ways, sitting with the two parties
after a passage of a few minutes, from notes
almost at the same time as the speaker, usually from a booth
questions.explanation: Liaison works in short two-way turns; consecutive renders a longer passage afterwards, from notes; simultaneous runs alongside the speaker from a cabina. Translating a document is translation, not interpreting.

questions.stem: Which principles do most interpreters' codes share, as the lesson describes them? Select all that apply.
choices: Rendering everything, with no omissions or additions
Advising the party who seems confused
Softening rude remarks to keep the peace
questions.explanation: Accuracy, confidentiality and impartiality are shared principles. Advice is outside the role, and softening a remark changes the message, which accuracy rules out.

questions.stem: Complete with the verb meaning "to convey": "Hay que ___ el tono, no solo las palabras."
questions.explanation: "Trasladar" (to convey into another language; also to move or transfer). "Transmitir" also fits this sentence and is accepted.

questions.stem: The patient says: "I don't think I heard anything." Which rendering keeps her meaning?
choices: No escuché nada, doctora, de verdad.
questions.explanation: "Creo que no" keeps her hedge. "No escuché nada" is firmer than what she said; "seguro que" and "de verdad" add certainty she didn't express.

questions.stem: Why do many health and legal services advise against using a relative as an interpreter?
choices: The law forbids it in every country.
A relative may soften bad news or add their own view, and confidentiality is harder to keep.
Relatives always charge more than professionals.
questions.explanation: The lesson gives this as common professional guidance, not a universal law: relatives can filter or add to the message, can be put in a painful position, and make confidentiality harder. Rules vary by institution and country.

questions.stem: Put the interpreter's steps in order when an ambiguous word comes up.
choices: Notice that the word has more than one possible meaning
Tell both parties that she is asking for clarification
Ask the speaker what the word means here
questions.explanation: She stops guessing, makes the step out of role visible to both sides, asks, and then interprets the answer: "En esta semana, a más tardar el viernes" becomes "This week, by Friday at the latest".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Everything I hear is confidential.
questions.explanation: "Todo lo que escuche es confidencial", Julián's promise in the lesson; the subjunctive "escuche" refers to whatever he may hear, and "todo lo que" takes a singular verb. The subject can also follow: "Es confidencial todo lo que escuche."

questions.stem: In this lesson, what is "la cabina"?
choices: A toll booth on a highway
A soundproof booth for simultaneous interpreters
questions.explanation: In interpreting, "la cabina" is the booth simultaneous interpreters work in. A toll booth is A2's "la caseta".

questions.stem: What did Julián do after saying "antibiótico" by mistake?
choices: He corrected himself openly and told both parties.
He let it pass, since the doctor would ask again.
He asked the patient to repeat the whole answer.
He told the doctor privately, in Spanish only.
questions.explanation: He corrected the word at once ("corrección del intérprete") and then told the patient, in English, what he had corrected. In a medical history an uncorrected slip is worse than a short interruption, and nothing should be said that one party doesn't understand.

questions.stem: What does "la deontología" mean in this lesson?
questions.explanation: "La deontología" is a profession's ethics: for interpreters, accuracy, impartiality, confidentiality and transparency. The study of teeth is "la odontología", a different word.

cards.back: Four surviving editions dated 1554 (Burgos, Medina del Campo, Alcalá de Henares, Antwerp); a copy of the Medina edition was found walled up in Barcarrota in 1992.
Nobody knows. Fray Juan de Ortega, Diego Hurtado de Mendoza and Alfonso de Valdés are among many names proposed.
A letter (epístola) from the adult Lázaro to an unnamed Vuestra Merced, who asked him about a certain "caso".
A blind man (from Salamanca), a stingy cleric in Maqueda, a penniless squire in Toledo.
Lázaro becomes town crier in Toledo and marries the archpriest of San Salvador's servant; people gossip, and he says he has never been better off.
First-person life of a rogue of low birth, serving master after master, in loosely linked episodes that satirize society.
Mateo Alemán, Part I 1599 (Madrid), Part II 1604 (Lisbon); fixed the label pícaro. Alemán sailed to New Spain in 1608.
Francisco de Quevedo, printed 1626: a darker picaresque, full of wordplay.
José Joaquín Fernández de Lizardi (El Pensador Mexicano); began to appear in 1816, last volume 1831; often called the first Latin American novel.
Who writes, to whom, why now? Where do the narrator's judgment and yours part ways? That gap is where the irony sits.
Sketches of local types and customs (Larra, Mesonero Romanos, Guillermo Prieto); from las costumbres.
Realism shows contemporary society as it is; naturalism (Zola) adds heredity and environment, the novel as experiment.
Emilia Pardo Bazán, 1883: essays that brought the naturalism debate to Spain.
Las Palmas 1843 – Madrid 1920. Episodios nacionales (46 novels, 1873–1912), Doña Perfecta (1876), Fortunata y Jacinta (1886–1887).
Juanito Santa Cruz, a rich heir, between his childless wife Jacinta and his working-class lover Fortunata, who bears his son.
Zamora 1852 – Oviedo 1901; law professor and feared critic; La Regenta (1884–1885).
Ana Ozores in Vetusta (usually read as Oviedo), between her confessor, the canon Fermín de Pas, and the seducer Álvaro Mesía.
Federico Gamboa, 1903: the best-known Mexican naturalist novel; filmed in 1932.
¡Qué fácil era todo en París! The narrator's past tense with the character's own exclamation, no pensó que.
Situate the passage, state the theme, analyze techniques with short quotations, conclude with a reasoned judgment.
December 1927, Ateneo of Seville: a tribute for the 300th anniversary of Góngora's death.
Salinas, Guillén, Diego, Aleixandre (Nobel 1977), Dámaso Alonso, Alberti, Cernuda, Prados, Altolaguirre, Lorca.
June 5, 1898, Fuente Vaqueros (Granada).
Lorca, 1928: eighteen ballads (romances) set in a mythic Andalusia.
Written during Lorca's stay in New York and Cuba (1929–1930); published in 1940.
Bodas de sangre (1933), Yerma (1934), La casa de Bernarda Alba (finished June 1936; premiered Buenos Aires, March 8, 1945).
Shot by Nationalist forces near Víznar and Alfacar in August 1936 (usually dated August 18); his remains have not been found.
In Lorca's 1933 Buenos Aires lecture, the dark force that makes a performance shiver; everyday tener duende = to have charm.
Ramón Gómez de la Serna's one-line form: humor plus metaphor.
Emilio Prados (d. 1962), Luis Cernuda (d. 1963), Manuel Altolaguirre and Concha Méndez.
Find the two things joined, what they share, say it plainly, then ask what the image adds.
The hesitation between a natural and a supernatural explanation; explained = uncanny; accepted = marvelous.
In magical realism the impossible is told as normal; in the fantastic its irruption is unsettling and makes us doubt.
Buenos Aires 1899 – Geneva 1986. Ficciones (1944), El Aleph (1949); director of the National Library 1955–1973; Cervantes Prize 1979.
Labyrinths, mirrors, libraries, encyclopedias, infinity, doubles, apocryphal books.
A work that contains a smaller image of itself: a dreamer who is dreamed, a labyrinth inside the labyrinth.
Adolfo Bioy Casares, 1940: a fugitive on an island loves a woman who is an image replayed by a machine.
cards.topic: The Río de la Plata circle

cards.back: 1940, compiled by Borges, Bioy Casares and Silvina Ocampo.
cards.topic: The Río de la Plata circle

cards.back: Zapotlán el Grande 1918 – Guadalajara 2001. Confabulario (1952), with "El guardagujas"; a bestiary of animal sketches.
Pinos, Zacatecas, 1928 – 2020. Tiempo destrozado (1959), Música concreta (1964), Árboles petrificados (1977, Villaurrutia Prize).
Habrá sido el cansancio; Sería algún colega: the future and conditional of conjecture keep the natural explanation uncertain.
Denotation, connotation, register, collocation, region, intensity, evaluation. Test a choice by substitution: does it change what we learn about the thing or the speaker?
esbelto praises; delgado is neutral; flaco is plain and informal (and a Mexican nickname); escuálido worries or scorns.
terco (B2) criticizes: won't listen; tenaz (C1) praises: won't give up; perseverante praises effort over time.
aducir razones (offers reasons, often doubted: adujo, aduje); esgrimir un argumento o un arma (wields); argüir que… (contends, formal: arguyo, arguyó, argüimos).
apostillar: adds a pointed remark after someone else; espetarle algo a alguien: blurts out something blunt or rude.
mutter between the teeth; stammer (or babble, like a baby); jabber fast and unclearly; grumble with displeasure.

cards.front: neutral verbs for minutes and news
cards.back: dijo, afirmó, señaló. Masculló, espetó, farfulló judge the speaker and don't belong in neutral reports.
en nariz (el aroma) → en boca (sabor, acidez, cuerpo) → el regusto / el final → a recommendation.
In coffee tasting, a virtue (una acidez brillante); in daily life, heartburn (tengo acidez).
dry and puckering (strong tea, some cacao); velvety; smooth, rich and slightly oily (praise for mezcal, an insult for a person).
words (colisionar / chocar); who is visible (roles and se, or yo, mi mamá); nouns or verbs (nominal style); sentence shape (one long period or fragments); marks of speech (¿eh?, ¡pum!).
A move into another register inside one text. By accident, a slip (se peló in a claim); on purpose, humor through incongruity (¡El siniestro! at a family meal).
el parte: an official report (el parte médico; in Spain, the crash form); la parte: a part. In Mexico, police write el informe policial, insurers el reporte.
el cofre (Spain el capó), la cajuela (Spain el maletero, Argentina el baúl), la salpicadera (Spain el guardabarros), la carrocería, el parabrisas.
el siniestro (the insured event, the claim), el ajustador (adjuster), la póliza, el deducible (Spain la franquicia), el peritaje, la responsabilidad civil.
se dio a la fuga (fled the scene). Also: un chavo en moto → un motociclista; no me pasó nada → resulté ilesa.
argot: the vocabulary of a trade or group (plural argots). caló: first the Romani variety of the Spanish Gitanos (its usual sense in Spain); in Mexico, widely, street slang. For recognition.
Keep every fact and every hedge; add none; hold one register; explain jargon instead of swapping it for another hard word.
infligir un daño, una derrota (inflict: inflijo); infringir una norma, la ley (break: infrinjo). Not inflingir.
absolver al acusado (acquit: absuelvo, absuelto) / absorber el agua; proveer de agua (supply: proveyó, provisto) / prever la escasez (foresee).
daños y perjuicios (harm) / un prejuicio (prejudice); expiar una culpa (atone: expío) / espiar al vecino (spy).
To suffer from a defect: El informe adolece de imprecisiones. For "to lack", write carecer de (the DPD calls adolecer = carecer improper).
detentar el poder: hold it unlawfully (DLE); ostentar / ocupar un cargo: hold it lawfully. Legal Spanish also uses detentar for mere possession.
One each: Las dos ganadoras recibieron sendos diplomas. Plural only (sendas). Not "both" (ambos), not "huge".

álgido: very cold and critical, culminating (both in the DLE: don't correct it); lívido: bruised or very pale, not furious; bizarro: brave, gallant (the "bizarre" sense is a loan; prefer raro in formal writing).
impropiedad: an error of meaning (adolecer for carecer); solecismo: an error of syntax (Hubieron quejas → Hubo quejas).
a typo; a slip of the tongue or pen (los lapsus); a small slip-up (los deslices); a blooper that makes readers smile.

cards.front: cotejar, enmendar, la fe de erratas, tergiversar
cards.back: check against the original; correct (enmiendo); the published correction; twist someone's words, usually on purpose.
Suggest, don't order; give the reason and the source: Te sugiero cambiar "detenta" por "ocupa": "detentar" sugiere que el cargo es ilegítimo.
voz patrimonial: came down through speech and changed (llamar, entero, estrecho); cultismo: borrowed later from written Latin (clamar, íntegro, estricto).
llamar / clamar, entero / íntegro, estrecho / estricto, delgado / delicado, colgar / colocar.
Latin clusters kept (-ct-, cl-), vowels kept (delicado vs delgado), Latin stress (íntegro, espécimen).

cards.front: motu proprio, grosso modo, statu quo
cards.back: Not de motu propio, not a grosso modo, not status quo (DPD).
Ortografía (2010): in italics, no written accents: per capita, sui generis. The DPD (2005) wrote per cápita, still common in print.

cards.front: a priori, de facto, in situ, sine qua non
cards.back: before the evidence; in fact, whatever the law says; on site; indispensable (condición sine qua non).
Genus (capital) + specific epithet (lower case), both in italics: Ambystoma mexicanum. Epithets honoring people: -i for a man, -ae for a woman.
Plural los especímenes: unusually, the stress moves one syllable in the plural, and the accent with it (es-PÉ-ci-men, es-pe-CÍ-me-nes).
hiper- over, hipo- under, endo- inside, exo- outside, poli- many, -logía study of, -grafía writing, -cracia power.
Diccionario de la lengua española (RAE and ASALE): general Spanish, with usage and country labels; 23rd edition 2014, updated online (23.8 in December 2024); a printed 24th edition announced.
Diccionario del español de México (El Colegio de México, Luis Fernando Lara; project from 1973): describes all the Spanish used in Mexico since 1921. Second edition online, 2020.
Academia Mexicana de la Lengua (first published 2010): only words and senses particular to Mexico.
lema (headword), etimología, acepciones (numbered senses with part of speech), marcas de uso (Méx., coloq., despect., desus., Der.), ejemplos.
To file every form under its headword: canté, cantaríamos → cantar; adujeron → aducir.
The RAE's corpus of Spanish from 2001 on, Spain and the Americas, written and oral; words lemmatized and tagged; filter by country, region or topic.
Every occurrence of a word, one per line, word in the center: read down the right-hand column to see collocations. (In grammar, la concordancia is agreement.)
La frecuencia de uso tells you a word is common, not that it fits your sentence; check meaning and company.
Define by a more general word plus what sets this one apart: el croquis: dibujo (genus) rápido y esquemático (difference). No circles; same part of speech.
Un tesauro groups words by meaning: it suggests candidates but doesn't tell you their connotation or company.
la toponimia studies place names (topónimos); la onomástica, all proper names, including personal names (antropónimos). In Spain especially, la onomástica is also a name day.
-tlan (place of: Mazatlán), -co (in, place: Acapulco), -pan (on: Zapopan), -tepec (at the hill: Chapultepec). Meanings usually given; scholars sometimes disagree.
on the grasshopper hill; place of deer; place of the large reeds (meanings usually given).
bajo la advocación de San Juan: dedicated to Saint John; el santo patrono (la patrona): the town's protector saint.
Hidalgo, Morelos, Ciudad Juárez; official names such as Coahuila de Zaragoza, Michoacán de Ocampo, Veracruz de Ignacio de la Llave.
Guadalajara (river of stones), Guadalquivir (the great river), Medina (city), Alcalá (the castle). Usual etymologies.
Londres, Nueva York, Múnich, Pekín (recommended by the RAE's Ortografía; Beijing also common in the press). Use established Spanish names.
tapatío (Guadalajara), regiomontano / regio (Monterrey), capitalino / chilango (Mexico City), mexiquense (Estado de México), poblano, jarocho. Lower case.
Colloquial; origin debated; once derogatory, now used proudly by many. In formal writing: capitalino, or name the city.
An old spelling of the j sound: México, Oaxaca, Texas, said with j. Méjico is recorded but rare.

cards.front: Dos horas después, la policía detenía al sospechoso.
cards.back: A single finished event told in the imperfect, with a time phrase: slowed down, closing a sequence. Allowed in your narratives; a preterite is never wrong.

cards.front: Narrative imperfect without a time phrase?
cards.back: It reads as a habit or an action in progress: La policía detenía al sospechoso (used to arrest / was arresting). Anchor it: A las seis y diez…
Yo era el detective y tú eras el ladrón (I'd be the detective…). Soñé que estaba en una estación… Recognition only.
A past event told in the present: En 1969 Bernal publica su novela. Neutral in biographies; in fiction it puts the reader in the scene.
Future of conjecture: It must be about eleven. / He must have left.

cards.front: Tendría setenta años. / Habría sido el chofer.
cards.back: Conditional of conjecture, a guess about a past moment: He must have been seventy. / It must have been the driver.
Concessive future: He may be very smart, but… (not a prediction).

cards.front: El sospechoso habría huido (in a newspaper)
cards.back: Conditional of rumor: reportedly fled. Style guides advise attribution instead: Según la fiscalía, el sospechoso huyó.
Pretérito anterior (literary): No sooner had he finished than he left. Everyday: En cuanto terminó, se fue.
Literary -ra as a past: the man who had been (once was) president. Plain form: el que fue presidente.
Policiaca: the puzzle (crime, detective, solution). Negra: darker, the city and impunity matter as much as the culprit.
Published 1969; its antihero is Filiberto García. Often called the founding Mexican novela negra.
Protasis: the condition (si llueve). Apodosis: the result (se suspende el partido).

cards.front: De seguir así… / De haberlo sabido…
cards.back: De + infinitive: present or future condition. De + compound infinitive: a past that didn't happen.
With de + infinitive, a different subject goes after the infinitive: Had they won…

cards.front: Como no llegues… / Como no llegaste…
cards.back: Como + subjunctive: a warning (if you don't come…). Como + indicative: a reason (since you didn't come…).
With even a little: A poco que estudies, apruebas.

cards.front: de no ser por / de no ser que / de no ser porque
cards.back: De no ser por + noun: but for. De no ser que + subjunctive: unless. De no ser porque + indicative: if it weren't for the fact that.

cards.front: Si no hubiera llegado la imprenta, hoy leeríamos menos.
cards.back: Mixed counterfactual: past condition, present result.
Both standard in the result of a past counterfactual; hubiese venido is accepted, never required.

cards.front: sea como fuere / sea cual fuere
cards.back: Be that as it may / whatever it may be (plural: sean cuales fueren). Everyday: sea como sea, sea cual sea.
Changes one fact, checks it is plausible, follows the consequences and hedges each later step (cabe suponer, quizá).

cards.front: el que / el cual / quien after a preposition
cards.back: el pozo del que sacan agua; la norma conforme a la cual…; los técnicos con quienes hablamos. Prefer el cual after long prepositions and far from the antecedent.
Refer to a whole clause: El suelo cede, lo cual agrieta los muros. Lo cual is a little more formal.
…the thing possessed: una colonia cuyas calles se hunden.

cards.front: una colonia que sus calles se hunden
cards.back: Que su for cuyo: frequent in speech; the DPD advises against it in careful language. Write cuyas calles.

cards.front: Los vecinos que protestaron… / Los vecinos, que protestaron, …
cards.back: No commas: only those who protested. Commas: all of them protested.
Not standard: after a noun, quien without a preposition needs the nonrestrictive commas.
A scale of separation for asides: commas (close), dashes (stronger), parentheses (outside the line of thought).
Never a single comma between a subject and its verb, however long the subject.
When the reader must hold two open clauses, when two asides sit side by side, or when a relative is far from its antecedent.
Pumping water from the aquifer dries the lake clay above it, which compacts and doesn't recover: up to 40 cm a year in some areas (city civil protection, June 2024).
Formal gracias a, for a cause that helped: merced a la vigilancia comunitaria.

cards.front: a expensas de / en detrimento de
cards.back: A expensas de: at someone's cost, or paid by someone. En detrimento de: to the harm of a thing or value.
Without affecting (other rules or penalties still apply). Not 'despite'.
Lagging behind: ir a la zaga de. No irle a la zaga a alguien: to be just as good.

cards.front: a tenor de / a efectos de / en lo tocante a
cards.back: Según / para / en cuanto a, in formal and legal texts.
Advised against by the DPD. Use sobre la base de or a base de; con base en is not faulted, though careful style prefers the other two.

cards.front: de acuerdo a / de acuerdo con
cards.back: De acuerdo a is accepted and frequent in the Americas; de acuerdo con is preferred in careful use.
consistir en, incidir en, redundar en, abogar por, propender a.
Informar que is usual in the Americas, informar de que in Spain; don't mark either wrong.
1207 is the date in the colophon of the only manuscript (naming Per Abbat). The copy is usually dated to the fourteenth century; the date of composition is debated.
Romance closing verses of Arabic or Hebrew poems from al-Andalus, read through reconstruction; their place in the history of lyric is debated.
fazer → hacer; plaça → plaza; passar → pasar (voiceless s); dixo → dijo (x once like English sh).
Old second-person plural endings (cantades = cantáis); vos was respectful singular or plural.

cards.front: ca, e, non, fasta, maguer, asaz
cards.back: because, and, no, until, although, very.

cards.front: A tilde over a letter in a manuscript
cards.back: Usually an abbreviation for a missing n or m: año for anno, the origin of ñ.

cards.front: How to read an old passage
cards.back: Read aloud; make the regular swaps; find the verb; watch the little words; check meanings; compare with an edition's notes.
A collective noun takes a singular verb in its own clause, even with an aside: La gente, cansada, se fue.

cards.front: La mayoría de los vecinos votó / votaron.
cards.back: Both accepted (plural more frequent). With a predicate adjective, plural only: La mayoría de los vecinos están molestos.
Neuter subject + ser + plural predicate noun: the verb agrees with the predicate.

cards.front: Es uno de los que más saben / sabe.
cards.back: Both accepted; the plural is the more grammatical (its subject is los que).

cards.front: Se venden casas / Se busca a los responsables
cards.back: Passive se agrees with the noun (se venden casas; se vende casas is nonstandard). With a + people, impersonal and singular.

cards.front: La víctima, un hombre de 40 años, fue trasladada.
cards.back: Epicene noun: agreement follows the noun's gender, not the person's sex.

cards.front: el mar / la mar; el azúcar
cards.back: Ambiguous nouns: el mar in general use, la mar among sailors, in poetry and in alta mar; el azúcar, often with a feminine adjective (el azúcar morena).

cards.front: la jueza, la presidenta, la médica
cards.back: Feminine job titles the DLE records (check its online edition); la juez, la presidente are also heard.

Metonymy names a thing by something linked to it (leí a Rulfo: his books; Palacio Nacional: the presidency). Synecdoche is part for whole or whole for part (seis bocas; México ganó). Test: can you say X is a part of Y?
Oxymoron: two clashing words in one phrase (una calma impaciente). Paradox: a whole statement that seems self-contradictory (para encontrar tu voz, hay que callar).
A B / B A: no cambié mi pueblo; mi pueblo me cambió. The figure of the memorable closing line.
Polysyndeton repeats the conjunction (y… y… y…): slow, cumulative. Asyndeton drops it (llegó, firmó, se fue): fast, urgent.
One word serves several phrases: Él pidió café; ella, té. With two senses of one verb: Mi abuela contaba historias; mi madre, el dinero; perdió el miedo y el autobús.
A marked, unusual order, mostly in verse or solemn prose: de la ciudad las luces se apagaban. Ordinary fronting is not hyperbaton. Stress: i-PÉR-ba-ton.
Gradación: steps that rise (una libreta, un cuento, una novela, una vida). Aliteración: a repeated sound (la lluvia lenta y limpia).
Prosopopeya gives things human traits (las palabras me esperaban). Apóstrofe addresses someone absent (Y a ti, abuela…). Not el apóstrofo, the mark (').
El exordio opens a speech and wins goodwill (modesty, a small story). La peroración closes it: sums up and moves; the strongest figures go here.
El elogio: praise. El panegírico: praise with no reservations (often ironic). La semblanza: a short biographical sketch. La alocución: a short formal address by an authority.

The prizewinner (la galardonada); el laureado is more formal. The award itself is B2's el galardón. Ceremony words: el paraninfo (great hall), el estrado (platform), el atril (lectern), el jurado (jury).

Awarded each year by Spain's Ministry of Culture; presented on April 23 in the paraninfo of the Universidad de Alcalá. Mexican laureates: Paz 1981, Fuentes 1987, Pitol 2005, Pacheco 2009, Poniatowska 2013, del Paso 2015, Celorio 2025.
fallido (failed) → desigual, con altibajos (uneven) → logrado (well executed) → magistral (masterly). Soporífero and anodino: boring, bland.
Praise for restraint: sobrio, pulcro, depurado. Criticism of excess: recargado, ampuloso, efectista, pretencioso. Keep quality and ornament apart.
Loable and encomiable usually praise an effort or intention, often before a but: La intención es loable; el resultado, menos. Logrado praises the result.
Both worn out. Manido: an image or phrase handled too often (una metáfora manida). Trillado: a path or plot everyone has walked (un argumento trillado). Noun: el lugar común.
Efectista: effects for their own sake (smoke, music, tricks). B2's ostentoso: a showy display of wealth or luxury.
In criticism, la factura is the craftsmanship of a work: una novela de factura impecable. The everyday sense is an invoice.

un pobre hombre (pitiable) / un hombre pobre (penniless); cierto rumor (a certain) / un rumor cierto (true); un simple comentario (mere) / un comentario simple (plain); un viejo amigo (long-standing) / un amigo viejo (elderly); un nuevo libro (another) / un libro nuevo (brand-new).
An adjective before the noun that states an expected quality: la blanca nieve. Literary tone; several in a row make prose recargada.
Si bien…, con todo…; Se echa de menos…; Se le podría reprochar…; No es una obra fallida, pero sí desigual.
Ficha → presentación → descripción (no spoilers) → valoración with evidence → comparación → veredicto (for whom, and why).
Theme → structure → form (register, syntax, figures, vocabulary) → assessment (what the form does for the content).
Omnisciente (knows every mind and the future); testigo (first person, beside the protagonist; knows what he saw or was told); protagonista (tells his own story); second person (tú).
Voice: who tells. Focalization: whose eyes we see through. A third-person narrator can be focalized through a child (internal focalization).
1. Narrator's tenses: imperfect and conditional (llegaría). 2. Character's deixis with past tenses (mañana, ahora). 3. Questions and exclamations with no pensó: ¿Y si Julián no venía?
Narrator's summary → indirect speech (pensó que…) → free indirect style → direct speech («…», pensó) → interior monologue.
Analepsis: flashback. Prolepsis: flash-forward (años más tarde, vendería la casa). In medias res: starting in the middle of the action.
Frame story (a story inside a story); metafiction (fiction about its own writing); intertextuality (dialogue with other texts).
Ensemble novel (many voices); autofiction (the author's life mixed with invention); splitting of a narrator into two (yo / ella).

Luiselli, Los ingrávidos (2011): metafiction. Nettel, Después del invierno (2014, Premio Herralde): two alternating narrators. Herrera, Señales que precederán al fin del mundo (2009): allegorical journey. Melchor, Temporada de huracanes (2017): unbroken paragraphs, many perspectives.
The words that decide how an issue is seen: ajuste / aumento; reforma / recorte; actualización tarifaria / tarifazo. Neutral: name what happens.
Presupposition: taken for granted (seguiremos mejorando → it has been improving). Implicature: suggested, deniable (algunos cumplieron → others didn't).
Impersonal se and nominalizations remove the agent: Se tomó la decisión… (who decided?); la regularización de las tomas (who does what?).
hasta un 30 % (a maximum, perhaps for very few), más de, alrededor de, la mayoría de. En promedio + hasta mixes an average with a maximum.
maquillar las cifras (dress up the figures), edulcorar (sugarcoat), eludir (dodge), descalificar (disparage), polarizar (divide), tergiversar (distort).

cards.front: el chivo expiatorio, la propaganda, el doble discurso
cards.back: Scapegoat; persuasion disguised as information; saying one thing and doing another (or telling two audiences two things).
A recent sense under English influence (el gobierno impone su narrativa); its status is debated. Safer in formal writing: relato, discurso.

cards.front: Four questions of critical discourse analysis
cards.back: Who acts (named, hidden, blamed)? What is assumed? What is implied? What is left out? Then judge the frame.
Name the agent; use the plain verb (aumentar, not actualizar); attribute claims (según el organismo); quote unclear figures instead of fixing them; add no claims or hedges.
Lope's formula (Arte nuevo, 1609): three jornadas, tragic and comic mixed, many meters fitted to situations, plots of love, honor and enredo.
el galán (leading man), la dama (the lady), el gracioso (comic servant), la graciosa (the maid), el barba (the old man who guards honor).
Honor as reputation: what others say. In honor plots a rumor can be as dangerous as a crime.
El enredo: a tangle of mix-ups (letters, cloaks, darkness). Comedias de capa y espada: cloak-and-sword intrigue plays.
Open-air courtyard theater, afternoon performances: escenario, patio (standing mosqueteros), gradas (tiered benches), aposentos (latticed boxes), cazuela (women's gallery). Best preserved: Almagro.
loa (prologue) → play, with entremeses (comic interludes) between the jornadas → closing dance.
Calderón, first printed 1636. A prince locked in a tower because of a prophecy is tested, told it was a dream, and chooses to act well: free will vs fate; desengaño.
One-act religious allegory for Corpus Christi, abstract characters; Calderón's El gran teatro del mundo. Banned in 1765.
Born in New Spain c. 1581 (Taxco or Mexico City); died in Madrid 1639. La verdad sospechosa: a liar trapped by his lies, adapted by Corneille as Le Menteur (1644).
Four eight-syllable lines rhymed abba; Lope advised it for love scenes. Count syllables with synalepha (vowels joined across words).
Modernismo: Hispanic movement, about 1880–1915. English modernism (Joyce, Eliot) is later, closer to the Spanish vanguardias. Say modernismo in English.
Martí (Cuba, 1853–1895); Gutiérrez Nájera (Mexico City, 1859–1895); Darío (Nicaragua, 1867–1916); Silva (Colombia, 1865–1896); Nervo (Tepic, 1870–1919).
1882 Ismaelillo; 1888 Azul…; 1891 Versos sencillos; 1894 Revista Azul; 1896 Prosas profanas; 1898 Spain loses its last American colonies; 1905 Cantos de vida y esperanza.
el cisne (swan), el exotismo, la musicalidad, la sinestesia, precious objects (preciosismo, la orfebrería), rare words.
Spanish alexandrine: 14 syllables, 7 + 7, the modernistas' signature line. Free verse: no fixed meter or rhyme, the avant-gardes' line.
Darío (Prosas profanas): long lines, mythology, rare musical words, beauty and suggestion. Martí (Versos sencillos): short eight-syllable lines, plain words, sincerity.
Founded in Mexico City in 1894 by Manuel Gutiérrez Nájera (El Duque Job) and Carlos Díaz Dufoo; the magazine of Mexican modernismo. Later: the Revista Moderna (from 1898).
Often described as the first literary movement born in Spanish America to change the literature of Spain.

The two main parties to an amparo: the complainant, and the authority whose act is challenged (el acto reclamado). The Ley de Amparo also names el tercero interesado and el Ministerio Público Federal.
A stay: the court stops the challenged act while the case goes on, so the complainant isn't harmed first.
To end a case without deciding its merits (the act doesn't exist, or a bar applies): se sobresee en el juicio. Like leer: sobreseyó, sobreseyendo.
resultandos (what happened), considerandos (the reasons), puntos resolutivos or los resolutivos (the decision). Read the resolutivos first.
Article 16 of the Constitution: an act of authority must cite the exact rules that apply (fundar) and explain why the case fits them (motivar).

cards.front: por lo expuesto y fundado, se resuelve
cards.back: For the reasons and on the grounds stated, it is resolved: the formula that leads into the operative points.
Spanish jurisprudencia = binding case law; English jurisprudence usually = legal theory. A Mexican tesis is a published criterion, binding only under the Ley de Amparo's rules.
el demandado: defendant in a civil suit (la demanda); el acusado: defendant in a criminal case.
A justice of the Suprema Corte de Justicia de la Nación, not a government minister.
The prosecutor's investigation file in Mexico's accusatory system (nationwide from June 18, 2016), which replaced the averiguación previa.
Inadmissible: the law doesn't allow the action or appeal. Not "improper".
ficha de identificación, anamnesis (antecedentes, padecimiento actual), exploración física, estudios, diagnóstico (and diagnóstico diferencial), plan; then notas de evolución.
Reporting verbs in clinical notes: the patient reports, denies (niega fiebre = no fever), comes in for.
compatible con (fits), probable (likely), sugestivo de (points toward), a descartar (still to rule out).
Inflammation (gastritis), pain (neuralgia), in the blood (anemia, glucemia).
Above / below normal: hipertensión, hipoglucemia.
A benign tumor doesn't invade other tissue; a malignant one can, and its spread to another organ is la metástasis (plural las metástasis).
Screening: testing people who have no symptoms.
A past condition or a relative's illness that matters now: antecedentes heredofamiliares = family history.

cards.front: From the record to the patient
cards.back: usted, everyday words, one idea per sentence, what happens next, every fact and every hedge kept, no reassurance beyond the evidence.
Decision and vote; external context; domestic activity; inflation; balance of risks; guidance.

cards.front: el balance de riesgos sesgado al alza
cards.back: The risks to inflation are tilted upward: more could push it up than pull it down.
Slack: spare capacity in the economy (idle workers, unused plants), which holds prices down.
se prevé que (+ future or subjunctive), podría, sería necesario, de materializarse, no se descarta, en función de.
Keep each hedge at its own strength: prevé ≠ asegura; evaluará recortar ≠ recortará; no se descarta ≠ planea.
A quarter of a percentage point. From 4.3% to 4.6% is 0.3 percentage points (30 basis points), not 0.3%.

cards.front: el activo / el pasivo / el capital contable
cards.back: Assets / liabilities / equity (also el patrimonio). Assets = liabilities + equity.
Liquidity: paying short-term debts. Solvency: meeting all obligations in the long run.
Leverage: the use of debt to finance a business (liabilities against equity).
A trillion (a million millions). English "billion" = mil millones.

Novelty against the prior art, inventive step (actividad inventiva) and industrial application. A patent lasts 20 years from filing (extended only by a supplementary certificate for unreasonable delays in granting it); utility models 15.
Preamble (Una válvula…), transition (que comprende), elements, characterizing part (caracterizada porque…). One sentence.
Comprises: includes at least these parts. Not "understands".
The aforesaid: repeats an element already named (dicho resorte) so nothing is ambiguous.
A NOM (norma oficial mexicana) is a mandatory technical regulation; an NMX is a voluntary standard.
Passive and impersonal (se midió), noun chains (ensayo de durabilidad del obturador), measurements with tolerances (6.0 L/min ± 0.2).
Mexico writes 6.0, Spain 6,0; the RAE accepts both. Follow the text's convention.

cards.front: Explaining a technical text to a lay reader
cards.back: Start from the problem, define or replace terms, explain how step by step, keep figures with their source and the limits, add nothing.
A license to use an invention, usually paid for with royalties (las regalías).
A technical drawing or blueprint; also a city map. Not an airplane.
The package insert: Mexico's word / Spain's word.
The active ingredient / an inactive ingredient (which still matters for allergies and intolerances).
Posología: the whole dosage plan (how much, how often, how long). Dosis: one amount.
Contraindicado: could harm, don't use it. No indicado: not meant for that use.
Impersonal se + subjunctive: fixed instructions on Mexican boxes and labels ("keep", "shake", "do not use").
No tome (absolute) > Evite (strong) > Consulte a su médico antes de (check first); Suspenda y busque atención médica de inmediato (emergency).

cards.front: EU frequency bands for side effects
cards.back: muy frecuentes (>1 in 10), frecuentes (up to 1 in 10), poco frecuentes (up to 1 in 100), raras (up to 1 in 1,000), muy raras (up to 1 in 10,000).

cards.front: el comprimido / la tableta / la pastilla
cards.back: Tablet: the technical word, standard in Spain / the usual word on Mexican boxes / the everyday word everywhere.

cards.front: notario público (Mexico) vs US notary public
cards.back: The Mexican notario is a lawyer and public official who holds la fe pública; a US notary public witnesses signatures and generally isn't a lawyer.
proemio, comparecencia, antecedentes, cláusulas, generales y certificaciones, autorización.
Before me; I attest. Notarial formulas: recognize them, don't use them outside the protocol.
Under a formal promise to tell the truth: a Mexican legal formula.

cards.front: el heredero / el legatario / el albacea
cards.back: Inherits a share / receives a specific item (un legado) / carries out the will (el or la albacea).
The right to use a property and enjoy its income / ownership without that right.
The otorgante grants the act and signs; a compareciente is anyone who appears before the notary (a witness too).
To die without a valid will; the law then decides who inherits (la sucesión intestamentaria).

cards.front: Three kinds of power of attorney (Mexico)
cards.back: para pleitos y cobranzas, para actos de administración, para actos de dominio (the widest).
Spanish has several centers of prestige; each country's educated norm (norma culta) is a standard. Mexico's is as correct as Spain's.
The Asociación de Academias de la Lengua Española: created in Mexico in 1951, 23 academies today (Equatorial Guinea joined in 2016). Panhispanic works: DLE, Nueva gramática, DPD.
A word typical of a region / of a single city or area. Named by place: mexicanismo, americanismo, peninsularismo (Spain).
A Spanish loanword in another language (English patio, plaza, canyon); also the study of Hispanic cultures. Not a Hispanic person.
Méx., Esp., Am., Ant., Arg., Chile…: a warning that a sense is regional. But an unmarked word isn't always general (molar has no mark, yet is heard mainly in Spain).
A line where one feature gives way to another. The carro/coche/auto line and the computadora/ordenador line fall in different places and don't follow borders.
A working practice of dubbing and international publishing, not a variety: avoid slang, vosotros, vos and words rude somewhere; keep tú, ustedes and general words.
to dub: Doblaron la serie en México. (A1: to turn.) El doblaje = dubbing; el doblador, el actor de doblaje = voice actor.
la versión original (VO), la voz en off (voice-over), la sincronía (lip sync), el subtitulaje (Mexico; Spain el subtitulado), la traducción audiovisual
Spain: "to take, to catch" (coger el autobús). Mexico and much of Latin America: vulgar. Use tomar or agarrar.
Find local items; replace, explain or drop each; don't swap in another region's words; make references explicit (MXN, 24-hour times, acronyms); keep register and purpose.
lo que en México se llama… / conocido en otros países como… / se prefirió … por ser de uso general / sustituí … por …, más comprensible fuera de México
habláis, hablasteis, hablabais, hablaréis, hablaríais, habléis, habéis hablado; command hablad, sentaos. Pronouns os, vuestro.
A Juan le vi (Spain) = A Juan lo vi (Mexico). Accepted for one man; not for women or things. Write lo.
Esta mañana he salido temprano = Esta mañana salí temprano (Mexico). Read it as a simple past.
Spain: Voy a por pan = Voy por pan. Normal in Spain's speech; you don't need to produce it.
currar / el curro (work), flipar (be amazed), molar (be cool: me mola), el chaval (kid), majo (nice), cutre (tacky)
la pasta (money), el chollo (bargain), la peña (group of friends), el enchufe (connections), ¡venga! (come on!)
la tasca (tavern), la caña (small draft beer), el tapeo (tapas-hopping), el bocadillo (baguette sandwich), el chiringuito (beach bar), el botellón (street drinking party)
el grifo / la llave (faucet); el atasco / el tráfico, el embotellamiento (traffic jam); el ordenador / la computadora
el colegio mayor (residence hall with activities), el máster (plural másteres or másters), las oposiciones (competitive exams for public posts)
el puente: also a long weekend (Spain, and Mexico too). el tío: also "guy" in Spain (un tío majo).
Overt subjects (yo creo que yo voy), questions without inversion (¿Qué tú quieres?), para yo + infinitive, más nada / más nunca
Reportative dice (Mañana llueve, dice), double possessive (su casa de Juan), Ecuador's dar + gerund (dame pasando la sal)
le for lo (accepted for one man); la for le (La dije: not accepted); lo for le (Lo di un regalo: not accepted, stigmatized)
tú (Mexico); vos (Río de la Plata, Central America); usted with intimates (parts of Colombia, Costa Rica). Usted is formal everywhere.
vos hablás, comés, vivís, sos; commands hablá, comé, vení. Chile: tú + voseo endings (¿cómo estái?, ¿cachái?, tú sabís).
al tiro (right away), cachar (to get it), fome (boring), pololear / el pololo (go steady / boyfriend)
el chamo (kid), el pana (buddy), la vaina (thing, stuff)

cards.front: The Andes, South America, the Río de la Plata
cards.back: la chompa (sweater), el choclo (corn), la buseta (minibus: Colombia, Venezuela), el bondi (bus: Río de la Plata)
A Galician, the Galician language, and in much of Latin America, colloquially, any Spaniard.
Paraguay 1992 (art. 140): Spanish and Guarani. Peru 1993 (art. 48): Quechua, Aymara and others where they predominate. Bolivia 2009: many Indigenous languages.
Perdona, ¿qué quiere decir…? / ¿Cómo le dicen ustedes a…? / No te entendí bien, ¿me lo repites?
Grew up with Spanish at home, schooled in another language; speaks with ease, writes less. A variety, not "broken" Spanish.
